data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕智能代理（agents）在实际应用中的可行性、实用性、权限管理及其实现挑战的讨论。

不同观点：
• **baalimago**：认为智能代理在处理繁琐任务（如恶意应用检测）时非常有效。他分享了一个实际案例，使用LLM（Herman）读取和标记新应用的恶意性，再由人工最终决定，这种方法比“非智能”服务更有效。同时，他还计划将代理应用于集成测试中，利用LLM的“幻觉”功能发现问题。他认为智能代理非常适合这种需要处理多种数据类型和复杂任务的场景。

• **chem83**：提供了Google和Anthropic关于构建智能代理的指南链接，但没有发表具体个人观点，主要是为讨论提供了参考资料。

• **ednite**：对智能代理的实际应用持探索态度，正在考虑为客户需求构建一个能反映公司文化、协助文档检查和问题处理的内部助手。他对智能代理的质量、可靠性以及安全性表示关注，并寻求最佳实践和实施路线图的建议。

• **helsinki**：关注多代理系统中的权限管理问题，提出了在多个平台（GitHub、Jira、Slack）上如何为多个用户管理权限的实际挑战，尤其是在用户只希望一次性批准权限的情况下。

• **_pdp_**：认为理论上的智能代理构建指南不切实际，实践中单个LLM更为实用和成本效益高。他还强调了提示（prompting）在实际应用中的复杂性和重要性，认为指南更适合非技术高管而不适合实际开发者。

• **ramesh31**：认为工具而非“代理”本身才是关键，强调工具定义和塑造了代理的能力，建议专注于工具开发而不是将代理作为独立概念来处理。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：智能代理在实际应用中的可行性和实用性，特别是在权限管理和实现复杂性方面的挑战。
• **重要论据**：
  - baalimago提供了实际案例，展示了智能代理在恶意应用检测中的有效性。
  - helsinki提出了多代理系统中权限管理的实际问题，强调了用户权限管理的复杂性。
  - _pdp_和ramesh31对理论和实际应用之间的差距提出了批评，强调工具和提示在实际开发中的重要性。

这些观点共同构成了关于智能代理在实际应用中的多方面讨论，涉及其实际效果、实现挑战和最佳实践。

data.title: When memory was measured in kilobytes: The art of efficient vision
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了Inria于1980年代末开发的“高效链链接算法”的历史和意义。该算法由Gérard Giraudon、Philippe Garnesson和Patrick Cipière在法国索菲亚科技园研发，旨在解决计算机视觉中图像轮廓检测的内存和效率问题。由于当时计算机内存有限，该算法每次仅处理图像的三行像素，实时构建轮廓链。此算法不仅展示了在资源受限环境下的创新精神，还被Software Heritage保存，作为Inria legacy软件保护项目的一部分。该项目通过调查和研讨会，致力于保存和分享这些历史代码及其背后的故事。这一成功案例强调了个人和社区在数字工作保存中的重要作用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：旧算法及其在现代技术中的应用和潜力

不同观点：
• kmoser认为，尽管旧算法在今天可能已经过时，但其底层的某些代码和逻辑在生成现代代码时仍然对大型语言模型（LLMs）有帮助。这暗示旧算法可能具有一定的实用价值，尤其是在现代技术的背景下。

• alightsoul表达了对旧算法在现代硬件上运行速度的兴趣，暗示了旧算法在现代计算能力支持下可能会有新的应用场景或性能提升。

• mrheosuper指出，他仍在处理内存小于128KB的系统，表明旧算法在一些资源受限的环境中仍然具有实际应用价值，强调了其在特定领域中的持续相关性。

• cyberax分享了一个使用FFT（快速傅里叶变换）识别物体的方法，强调了FFT在对象识别中的独特优势，即不受物体方向和位置的影响，只要拥有物体的特征签名即可识别。这展示了旧算法在特定技术问题上的创新应用。

补充讨论：
• 评论中提到了旧算法在不同情境下的应用，包括其在现代代码生成、计算速度、资源受限系统以及特定技术方法（如FFT）中的潜在价值。
• 争议的焦点可能在于旧算法在现代技术中的实际应用价值和可行性。不同评论者基于各自的背景和经验，对旧算法的重要性持不同程度的认可。
• 讨论还涉及到对具体算法（如FFT）的创新应用的探讨，展示了算法在不同领域中的广泛适用性和持久影响力。

44182698.article_content:
By Mathilde Fichen
In the early days of computer vision, when memory was scarce and every byte counted, innovation thrived under constraint. “An Efficient Chain-Linking Algorithm,” developed at Inria in the late 1980s, is a brilliant example of this spirit. Now preserved and shared by Software Heritage, this compact yet powerful piece of C code showcases how elegance and efficiency went hand in hand in outlining the future of image processing—one pixel chain at a time.
The code resulted from research work carried out between 1985 and 1991 at Inria, by Gérard Giraudon (research and principal investigator), Philippe Garnesson (a PhD student), and Patrick Cipière (software engineer). Down in sunny Sophia Antipolis, a
tech park
20 minutes inland from Antibes, the team tackled computer vision with a distinctly local flavor. They called themselves PASTIS, a playful nod to the anise drink. Still, the acronym – Scene Analysis and Symbolic Image Processing Project (Projet d’Analyse de Scène et de Traitement d’Image Symbolique) – hinted at their serious mission.
Gérard Giraudon
, circa 1980
Preserving Inria legacy software
The effort to preserve this source code is part of a broader initiative to preserve the legacy codes of
Inria
(France’s National Institute for Research in Digital Science and Technology), launched in 2023 in a joint effort of Software Heritage, Inria Alumni, and Inria. The project to preserve Inria’s legacy software started by reaching out to the institute’s community, past and present, through a survey (as detailed in our
iPres article
.)  This initial outreach informed a dedicated,
hands-on workshop in 2024
, which kicked off the practical work of exploring these historical codes. The current focus is on securely archiving the important legacy software we’ve identified within Software Heritage. Sharing the stories behind these codes with the broader community is just as vital.
The recovery of some code has been surprisingly straightforward. For instance, the code for “An Efficient Chain-Linking Algorithm” was readily accessible thanks to Gérard Giraudon’s personal preservation efforts on a local drive. That small success story is a reminder of how important individual initiative is for preserving digital work. Each piece of software recovered isn’t just code; it’s a piece of research history, carrying the stories of the people who created it.
Inria alumni workshop, October 2024, Inria Paris.
An algorithm for outlining images
The chain-linking algorithm processes a 2D pixel matrix, typically the output of a contour detection step.
Raw image used as input for the algorithm. Source: Chaînage efficace de contour, n° 605, Février 1987, Gérard Giraudon
The output is a list of contour chains. Each chain in this list is a sequence of pixel coordinates that define a continuous boundary, ready for further steps like polygonal approximation or shape analysis..
Processed image. Source : Chaînage efficace de contour, n° 605, Février 1987, Gérard Giraudon
Basically, the chain-linking connects the edge pixels to create smooth outlines, just like tracing the shape with a pencil.
Computer vision in the 80s
The mid-1980s aspiration of seeing robots hit a speed bump: computer vision algorithms weren’t fast enough. The core challenge? Real-time performance – the essential ingredient for giving robots camera “eyes” that could truly see and react. At the time, such a system was conceived as a pipeline of operations from image acquisition (one shot or video) to a decision-making system.
The goal was to extract meaningful information from raw image data, typically represented as an 8-bit matrix of pixel intensities, and convert it into a graph in list form (i.e., from matrix to list). This process begins with detecting and recognizing shapes within the image, either in 2D or 3D, depending on the available data. From there, the system identifies objects and analyzes their spatial relationships, ultimately constructing a graph of semantic connections between them. This graph captures not just what the objects are, but how they relate to one another within the observed scene. In some cases, the analysis extends over time (3D + t), allowing for the interpretation of motion and dynamic interactions in a sequence of frames.
Solving key memory issues
The algorithm was first developed on a PerkinElmer Model 3250 computer, seen above in a brochure
via 1000bit.
Another challenge in early image processing was the limited amount of short-term memory (RAM) available in computers. This made it essential to focus on reducing the amount of data stored and processed at any given time, while preserving important information.
Due to these constraints, the Efficient Chain-Linking Algorithm could only store three lines of the image at a time while reading it line by line. data.title: How we reduced the impact of zombie clients
data.author: jaas
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了Let’s Encrypt如何应对“僵尸客户端”问题，这些客户端是废弃或错误配置的服务器和ACME客户端，不断请求更新数字证书，浪费证书颁发机构的资源。由于这些客户端不会自动放弃，Let’s Encrypt每年处理大量无效请求，影响了系统效率。

为了解决这一问题，Let’s Encrypt使用了一系列速率限制机制，以确保资源被有效利用。速率限制不是惩罚措施，而是为了防止资源浪费，同时不影响正常用户的使用。这些限制机制经过精心设计，避免了对用户的过度限制，并在系统故障时允许更多证书颁发。

通过这些措施，Let’s Encrypt有效减少了僵尸客户端带来的影响，确保系统能更好地服务于合法用户。

Blog
How We Reduced the Impact of Zombie Clients
By Samantha Frank ·
June 4, 2025
Every night, right around midnight (mainly
UTC
), a horde of zombies wakes up and clamors for … digital certificates!
The zombies in question are abandoned or misconfigured Internet servers and ACME clients that have been set to request certificates from Let’s Encrypt. As our certificates
last for at most 90 days
, these zombie clients’ software knows that their certificates are out-of-date and need to be replaced. What they don’t realize is that their quest for new certificates is doomed! These devices are cursed to seek certificates again and again, never receiving them.
But they do use up a lot of certificate authority resources in the process.
The Zombie Client Problem
Unlike a human being, software doesn’t give up in frustration, or try to modify its approach, when it repeatedly fails at the same task. Our emphasis on automation means that the vast majority of Let’s Encrypt certificate renewals are performed by automated software. This is great when those renewals succeed, but it also means that forgotten clients and devices can continue requesting renewals unsuccessfully for months, or even years.
How might that happen? Most often, it happens when a device no longer has a domain name pointed to it. The device itself doesn’t know that this has changed, so it treats renewal failures as transient even though they are actually permanent. For instance:
An organization may have allowed a domain name registration to lapse because it is no longer needed, but its servers are still configured to request certs for it.
Or, a home user stopped using a particular dynamic-DNS domain with a network-attached storage device, but is still using that device at home. The device doesn’t realize that the user no longer expects to use the name, so it keeps requesting certs for it.
Or, a web hosting or CDN customer migrated to a different service provider, but never informed the old service provider. The old service provider’s servers keep requesting certs unsuccessfully. If the customer was in a free service tier, there might not be invoices or charges reminding the customer to cancel the service.
Or any number of other, subtler changes in a subscriber’s infrastructure, such as changing a firewall rule or some webserver configuration.
At the scale of Let’s Encrypt, which now covers
hundreds of millions of names
, scenarios like these have become common, and their impact has become substantial. In 2024, we noticed that about half of all certificate requests to the Let’s Encrypt ACME API came from about a million accounts that never successfully complete any validations. Many of these had completed validations and issued certificates sometime in the past, but nowadays every single one of their validation attempts fails, and they show no signs that this will change anytime soon.
Unfortunately, trying to validate those futile requests still uses resources. Our CA software has to generate challenges, reach out and attempt to validate them over the Internet, detect and report failures, and record all of the associated information in our databases and audit logs. And over time, we’ve seen more and more recurring failures: accounts that always fail their issuance requests have been growing at around 18% per year.
In January, we mentioned that we had been addressing the zombie client problem
through our rate limit system
. This post provides more detail on that progress.
Our Rate Limit Philosophy
If you’ve used Let’s Encrypt as a subscriber, you may have run into one of our
rate limits
at some point, maybe during your initial setup process. We have eight different kinds of rate limits in place now; as our January post describes, they’ve become more algorithmically sophisticated and grown to address a wider range of problems. A key principle for Let’s Encrypt is that our rate limiting is not a punishment. We don’t think of rate limits as a way of retaliating against a client for misbehavior. Rate limits are simply a tool to maximize the efficient use of our limited resources and prevent people and programs from using up those resources for no constructive purpose.
We’ve consistently tried to design our rate limit mechanisms in line with that philosophy. So if a misconfiguration or misunderstanding has caused excessive requests in the past, we’re still happy to welcome the user in question back and start issuing them certificates again—once the problem has been addressed. We want the rate limits to put a brake on wasteful use of our systems, but not to frustrate users who are actively trying to make Let’s Encrypt work for them.
In addition, we’ve always implemented our rate limits to err on the side of permissiveness. For example, if the Redis instances where rate limits are tracked have an outage or lose data, the system is designed to permit more issuance rather than less issuance as a result.

  - cibyr认为自助解除暂停功能非常出色，解决了因限制导致无法检查问题而产生的挫败感。
  - efitz赞赏非惩罚性的方法，并计划在自己的工具中采用这种自助解除暂停方法。

• [对Caddy的积极评价]  
  - aorth对使用Caddy而非certbot来管理TLS证书表示满意，强调Caddy的良好默认配置和较少的活动部件。

• [对具体技术问题的处理]  
  - meltyness提到其服务器证书更新被暂停，通过手动方式解决问题，但由于仅是一个小博客，未深入调查具体原因。

• [对自动化问题的担忧]  
  - jadbox担心自助解除暂停功能可能被软件自动执行，建议在按钮上添加CAPTCHA以防止自动化过程。

• [对功能效果的质疑]  
  - Palomides对该功能的影响力表示怀疑，指出在其处理的6亿个域中仅捕获了10万个。

• [改进建议]  
  - greatgib建议通过电子邮件通知用户问题，以便及时处理。
  - smallnix对3,200人需要手动解除暂停表示担忧，建议寻找更好的模式来识别和处理“僵尸”账户，并提到资源和时间的限制。

• [进一步的预防措施]  
  - saagarjha建议在计划关闭账户访问前发送通知，给予用户预警。

补充讨论：
- 功能的支持者认为自助解除暂停能有效减少用户挫败感，并赞赏非惩罚性方法。
- 对自动化滥用的担忧引发了对CAPTCHA的需求讨论。
- 对功能效果和改进的建议集中在通知机制和识别“僵尸”账户的更好模式上。
- 具体技术问题的处理和Caddy的积极评价提供了对实际使用场景的洞察。

data.title: Doubling Down on Open Source
data.author: clemo_ra
data.article_summary: Langfuse宣布将其所有产品功能开源，包括LLM-as-a-judge评估、注释队列、提示实验和 playground，所有这些功能现在都可以在MIT许可证下自托管使用。此举旨在加速开发者在其应用中的迭代速度，并获取社区反馈，以进一步改善项目。公司将专注于Langfuse Cloud和企业平台团队的自托管服务，并将商业许可代码限制在企业安全相关功能上。通过开放核心功能，Langfuse希望加深社区信任，加速技术采用，并更快地进行迭代。目前已有超过8000个自托管实例，公司期望此举巩固其在LLMOps领域的首选地位。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开源许可变更及其影响

不同观点：
• [积极支持] [datadrivenangel] 认为将非企业功能以MIT许可证发布是一个值得尊重的举措，尽管担心这些功能的采用率可能很低。
• [竞争与策略] [suyash] 认为此举可能是因为未能抵御该领域的竞争，包括其他开源解决方案，或者是一种最后的增长策略。但不论如何，这对开源生态系统是有利的。
• [实际影响] [b0a04gl] 指出，将LLM（大型语言模型）作为判定工具开源对基础设施从业者有直接影响，这些人之前可能一直在用简陋的脚本和电子表格来拼凑解决方案。现在可以即插即用，呼吁保持这种开放源码的势头，并希望更多有价值的功能被开源。

补充讨论：
• [简单支持] [spencera] 和 [Tdsone] 对这一变化表示简单的赞赏，认为Langfuse看起来很棒，或者简单地表示酷或很棒。

争议焦点：
• 关于此开源举措的动机存在不同看法，[datadrivenangel] 和 [suyash] 提到了采用率低和市场竞争问题，而 [b0a04gl] 则更关注实际操作中的便利性和对从业者的积极影响。

总结来看，评论中主要讨论了开源许可变更的动机及其对技术社区的实际影响，有人关注背后的市场竞争因素，有人则关注技术实现的便捷性。整体上，多数评论对这一开源举措持积极态度。

44180954.article_content:
June 4, 2025
Doubling Down on Open Source
Today we are open sourcing all remaining Product Features in Langfuse under the MIT license
Marc
Clemens
Max
The LLM landscape is changing rapidly and so are the workflows used to build and improve LLM apps. Today,
we are open sourcing all Product Features in Langfuse
to enable our community to iterate on their applications faster and provide our project with feedback on where to go next.
Newly open sourced features include managed
LLM-as-a-judge evaluations
,
annotation queues
,
prompt experiments
and
the playground
, all of which are now freely available to self-host under the MIT license.
If you are self-hosting Langfuse already today,
upgrade your deployment to the
latest version
. You will find a more powerful version of Langfuse.
Why are we doing this?
Langfuse is building the
open source LLM Engineering Platform
. We are building
the
platform to observe and improve LLM applications.
We are constantly shipping to be the technology of choice for our community. This requires trust, feedback and buy-in from our community.
We re-visited the gated features in our Enterprise Edition. If we want to be the first choice in the market, we need to allow our community to
cover the entire dev cycle in our FOSS version
. Features like LLM-as-a-Judge, Evals, or our Playground are market standard at this point and should be freely available.
But why stop there?
The best platform for developers has to be open at its core. By
removing commercial barriers from our product features
, we’re fostering deeper trust, collaborating on contributions, accelerating adoption, gathering richer community feedback, and iterating faster than ever.
Our Open Source Journey
Langfuse was
launched
as an open source project.
This was based on a few
core beliefs
:
Data captured by Langfuse should be freely accessible
The AI landscape changes every week – Langfuse must integrate agnostically with all models and application stacks
Great teams deserve the flexibility to extend the platform to support custom workflows
This positioning resonates and today we are doubling down on it.
Langfuse has been an open core company from the start.
Our core just expanded significantly
and our periphery shrunk. Commercially licensed code is now limited to features for Enterprise Security and Platform Teams (e.g. SCIM, Audit Logs, Data Retention Policies – regular
SSO
is and continues to be MIT licensed).
Langfuse’s Open Core Model

Then
Now
Core Platform

Enterprise Security

Commercial 🔒
Enterprise Support
Commercial
Commercial 🔒
As we open source previously commercial features, we are fully investing our commercial focus in Langfuse Cloud and Enterprise platform teams in self-hosting.
Thousands of Langfuse Deployments
There are more than 8,000 monthly active self-hosted instances of Langfuse out in the wild. This boggles our minds.
We expect that today’s changes solidify Langfuse as the first choice for a powerful and truly open source platform in LLMOps.
Today is the day to start self-hosting Langfuse. Head over to
our self hosting docs
and use the new
terraform modules
for deploying Langfuse at production-scale.

data.title: The iPhone 15 Pro’s Depth Maps
data.author: marklit
data.article_summary: 本文主要介绍了iPhone 15 Pro的深度图功能及其存储格式。自2017年起，苹果通过LiDAR扫描仪等技术支持图像中的深度图，这些深度图与其他图像数据一起存储在HEIF格式文件中。本文详细说明了如何使用Python脚本从HEIC文件中提取深度图及其他元数据，并转换为EXR文件。作者使用了一台高性能工作站，并逐步演示了如何设置环境、安装必要工具、克隆相关代码库及提取示例图像的深度图等操作。通过这些步骤，用户可以访问和处理iPhone 15 Pro拍摄图像中的深度信息。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：iPhone深度地图的生成方法、应用及其局限性

不同观点：
• Uncorrelated指出，iPhone使用多种方法生成深度地图，包括双摄像头通过视差生成深度地图、单摄像头结合机器学习生成深度地图、以及使用TrueDepth相机生成自拍深度地图。这些方法在不同机型和场景中应用，深度地图不仅用于人像模式，还能用于创造性滤镜。
• Caseyohara对背景虚化效果提出批评，认为假景深效果看起来像糟糕的Photoshop处理，并提到文件格式的一些疑似拼写错误。
• Praveen9920期待手机硬件默认使用Gaussian splatting技术来生成3D图像，认为这可能比添加昂贵的传感器更具成本效益。
• Heliographe提到深度地图和语义地图可以用来创造深度效果，并介绍了自己开发的用于查看和导出深度地图的工具。

补充讨论：
• Kccqzy对HDR增益地图与深度地图的关系提出疑问，认为文章对HDR的讨论过多，且个人不喜欢iPhone的HDR显示效果。
• Onlygoose指出LIDAR分辨率远低于显示的深度地图，深度地图需要通过LIDAR和常规相机数据合成。
• Kawsper猜测Apple可能使用深度地图实现“创建贴纸”功能。
• Arialdomartini和Layer8讨论了深度地图用于生成立体图或自动立体图的可能性。
• Andrwwmcwatters提到iOS的Reality Composer无法在非LIDAR设备上回退到摄影测量，对此感到失望。
• 其他如Cloud_herder和Itsgrimetime则偏离主题，讨论了网站设计和浏览体验问题。
• Pzo对LIDAR技术的下放速度和改进缓慢表示失望，并提到TrueDepth相机在iPhone 13上的表现有所下降。

争议焦点：
• LIDAR技术的下放速度及其在非专业设备上的应用限制。
• TrueDepth相机在近几年的改进不足，尤其是在分辨率和帧率上的限制。
• 假景深效果的真实性和视觉质量问题。

其他值得注意的讨论点：
• 深度地图的多种应用场景，包括艺术创作和3D效果生成。
• HDR增益地图与深度地图之间的关系及是否可以独立处理。
• 不同iPhone型号和摄像头配置对深度地图生成的影响。

44183591.article_content:
The iPhone 15 Pro's Depth Maps
Since 2017, Apple have supported depth maps in the images its iPhones capture either via LiDAR scanners, 3D
time-of-flight
scanner-less LIDAR or
structured-light
3D scanning.
These depth maps, along with other imagery, are stored in High Efficiency Image File Format (HEIF) container files. These files can contain multiple images and vast amounts of metadata. This format was originally designed between 2013 and 2015 and Apple adopted its HEIC variant in 2017.
Since then, HEIC files are the default storage container format for images captured on the iPhone. But with that said, it is possible to use the JPEG format instead if things like depth maps and HDR are not of interest.
Finn Jaeger, who is the head of VFX at Replayboys, a film production firm in Hamburg, Germany,
posted
a screenshot a few weeks ago showing how multiple depth maps were being produced by his iPhone.
He announced he was working on a project called
HEIC Shenanigans
. This project contains scripts to separate out images and their metadata from HEIC containers as well as convert them into EXR Files. As of this writing, the project contains 374 lines of Python.
In this post, I'll walk through Finn's codebase with an example image from an iPhone 15 Pro.
My Workstation
I'm using a 5.7 GHz AMD Ryzen 9 9950X CPU. It has 16 cores and 32 threads and 1.2 MB of L1, 16 MB of L2 and 64 MB of L3 cache. It has a liquid cooler attached and is housed in a spacious, full-sized Cooler Master HAF 700 computer case.
The system has 96 GB of DDR5 RAM clocked at 4,800 MT/s and a 5th-generation, Crucial T700 4 TB NVMe M.2 SSD which can read at speeds up to 12,400 MB/s. There is a heatsink on the SSD to help keep its temperature down. This is my system's C drive.
The system is powered by a 1,200-watt, fully modular Corsair Power Supply and is sat on an ASRock X870E Nova 90 Motherboard.
I'm running Ubuntu 24 LTS via Microsoft's Ubuntu for Windows on Windows 11 Pro. In case you're wondering why I don't run a Linux-based desktop as my primary work environment, I'm still using an Nvidia GTX 1080 GPU which has better driver support on Windows and ArcGIS Pro only supports Windows natively.
Installing Prerequisites
I'll use Python 3.12.3 and a few other tools in this post.
$
sudo
add-apt-repository
ppa:deadsnakes/ppa
$
sudo
apt
update
$
sudo
apt
install
\
jq
\
openexr
\
libimage-exiftool-perl
\
libopenexr-dev
\
python3-pip
\
python3.12-venv
Note, the
libimage-exiftool-perl
package installs
exiftool
version 12.76+dfsg-1 which was released at the end of January 2024. Since then, there have been at least ten releases that have addressed issues or enhanced exiftool's HEIC support.
The above version should work fine for the steps in this post but be mindful that any issues you encounter going forward might be resolved with a more up to date version of exiftool.
I'll be using
JSON Convert
(jc) to convert the output of various CLI tools into JSON.
$
wget
https://github.com/kellyjonbrazil/jc/releases/download/v1.25.2/jc_1.25.2-1_amd64.deb
$
sudo

-i
jc_1.25.2-1_amd64.deb
I'll clone Finn Jaeger's HEIC Shenanigans repo.
$
git
clone
https://github.com/finnschi/heic-shenanigans
\
~/heic-shenanigans
I'll set up a Python Virtual Environment and install a few dependencies.
$
python3
-m
venv
~/.iphone_depth
$
source
~/.iphone_depth/bin/activate
$
python3
-m
pip
install
-r
\
~/heic-shenanigans/requirements.txt
$
python3
-m
pip
install
\
OpenImageIO
I'll use
DJV
v2.0.8 to view EXR imagery produced in this post.
An iPhone 15 Pro Image
Joel Joseph
, a subject matter expert on the ArcGIS Desktop Products Suite in Mumbai, India, was kind enough to send me an HEIC-contained image he took on his iPhone 15 Pro. I'll use this image in this post. Below is a screenshot.
Extracting the Gain Map
The HEIC file Joel provided is 1.57 MB.
$
python
~/heic-shenanigans/gain_map_extract.py
\
IMG_E2153.HEIC

433K  IMG_E2153_depth_0.tiff
5.9M  IMG_E2153_hdrgainmap_48.tiff
71M  IMG_E2153_base.tiff

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Oort云中螺旋结构的发现及其意义

不同观点：
• doctoboggan指出，螺旋结构是通过为Hayden Planetarium制作新太空秀的模拟过程中首次发现的，并分享了模拟动画链接。他认为这种发现方式非常酷。
• twic认为，仅通过两个不同方向的视角很难可视化该结构，建议制作3D模型以帮助理解。
• coke12表示，这一发现非常酷，并指出我们自己的太阳系似乎也有螺旋臂。
• dedicate过去将Oort云想象成一种分散的雪球战斗，对这种 delicate 结构如何保持形状表示疑问，并认为这一发现改变了对太阳系“边缘”的看法。
• Eduard请求解释这一发现的 significance，询问是否因为以前认为Oort云中的天体分布是随机的，而这次发现了一种可定义的结构。
• machenesonk提出一个更广泛的问题，询问宇宙是否会自转。
• girvo提到无法访问网站，因为hCaptcha图像（桌子和椅子）在多次点击“跳过”后仍未显示。

补充讨论：
• HappMacDonald的评论（"Kamina most likely approves"）似乎是一个与主讨论无关的流行文化引用，未对螺旋结构的发现提出直接观点或问题。

争议焦点：
• 发现的螺旋结构如何能在Oort云这样遥远的区域保持 delicate 的形状，以及这一发现对理解太阳系边缘的意义，是讨论中引发思考和提问的焦点。

总结：
评论主要围绕Oort云中螺旋结构的发现及其意义展开，有人分享发现过程，有人建议3D模型以帮助理解，还有人探讨发现的科学意义及宇宙自转的可能性。

data.title: Not all tokens are meant to be forgotten
data.author: MarcoDewey
data.article_summary: 文章提出了一种针对性信息遗忘（TIF）框架，以解决大型语言模型（LLM）在遗忘不必要信息时的“过度遗忘”问题。TIF框架通过识别遗忘样本中的 unwanted words (UW) 和 general words (GW)，利用逻辑偏好损失函数来遗忘UW相关信息，同时通过保留损失函数保护GW中的有用信息，从而提高遗忘效果并减少模型效用损失。实验表明，TIF在TOFU和MUSE基准上取得了显著效果，有效提升了遗忘效率并保持了模型实用性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：语言模型在记忆和遗忘信息方面的能力及其影响

不同观点：
• JimDabell认为，根据Meta最新发表的论文（https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.24832），语言模型在记忆能力上存在限制，大约每个参数只能记忆3.6比特的信息。一旦达到这个阈值，模型会开始泛化而非继续记忆。这表明模型在信息处理上存在一个自然的平衡点，过度记忆是不可能的。

• pixl97则对模型记忆“ unwanted information”（如私人或版权信息）表示担忧。他认为人类并不会忘记版权信息，而是通过调整来避免侵权问题；同样，人类不会忘记私人信息，只是选择不分享。因此，他担心如果AI大量遗忘信息，可能会导致一种令人担忧的“反乌托邦”式的未来。

补充讨论：
• JimDabell的立场基于技术文献和数据，引用了具体的研究结果来支持他的观点，强调了模型在记忆上的物理限制和泛化能力的自然发展。
• pixl97的观点更侧重于伦理和社会影响，关注AI在处理敏感信息时的表现以及这种表现对人类社会的潜在影响。他提出了对AI遗忘大量信息这一现象的伦理和哲学思考。
• 争议的焦点在于AI应如何处理记忆和遗忘的问题，特别是在涉及敏感信息时，这种技术特性可能带来的社会和伦理影响。

Abstract:
Large Language Models (LLMs), pre-trained on massive text corpora, exhibit remarkable human-level language understanding, reasoning, and decision-making abilities. However, they tend to memorize unwanted information, such as private or copyrighted content, raising significant privacy and legal concerns. Unlearning has emerged as a promising solution, but existing methods face a significant challenge of over-forgetting. This issue arises because they indiscriminately suppress the generation of all the tokens in forget samples, leading to a substantial loss of model utility. To overcome this challenge, we introduce the Targeted Information Forgetting (TIF) framework, which consists of (1) a flexible targeted information identifier designed to differentiate between unwanted words (UW) and general words (GW) in the forget samples, and (2) a novel Targeted Preference Optimization approach that leverages Logit Preference Loss to unlearn unwanted information associated with UW and Preservation Loss to retain general information in GW, effectively improving the unlearning process while mitigating utility degradation. Extensive experiments on the TOFU and MUSE benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed TIF framework enhances unlearning effectiveness while preserving model utility and achieving state-of-the-art results.

44186607.article_summary: 文章提出了一种针对性信息遗忘（TIF）框架，以解决大型语言模型（LLM）在遗忘不必要信息时的“过度遗忘”问题。TIF框架通过识别遗忘样本中的 unwanted words (UW) 和 general words (GW)，利用逻辑偏好损失函数来遗忘UW相关信息，同时通过保留损失函数保护GW中的有用信息，从而提高遗忘效果并减少模型效用损失。实验表明，TIF在TOFU和MUSE基准上取得了显著效果，有效提升了遗忘效率并保持了模型实用性。

主要讨论点：语言模型在记忆和遗忘信息方面的能力及其影响

不同观点：
• JimDabell认为，根据Meta最新发表的论文（https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.24832），语言模型在记忆能力上存在限制，大约每个参数只能记忆3.6比特的信息。一旦达到这个阈值，模型会开始泛化而非继续记忆。这表明模型在信息处理上存在一个自然的平衡点，过度记忆是不可能的。

• pixl97则对模型记忆“ unwanted information”（如私人或版权信息）表示担忧。他认为人类并不会忘记版权信息，而是通过调整来避免侵权问题；同样，人类不会忘记私人信息，只是选择不分享。因此，他担心如果AI大量遗忘信息，可能会导致一种令人担忧的“反乌托邦”式的未来。

补充讨论：
• JimDabell的立场基于技术文献和数据，引用了具体的研究结果来支持他的观点，强调了模型在记忆上的物理限制和泛化能力的自然发展。
• pixl97的观点更侧重于伦理和社会影响，关注AI在处理敏感信息时的表现以及这种表现对人类社会的潜在影响。他提出了对AI遗忘大量信息这一现象的伦理和哲学思考。
• 争议的焦点在于AI应如何处理记忆和遗忘的问题，特别是在涉及敏感信息时，这种技术特性可能带来的社会和伦理影响。

data.title: A Look Back at Recent Car Carrier Fires
data.author: testrun
data.article_summary:
2025年6月3日，汽车运输船*Morning Midas*在阿拉斯加阿达克以南300英里处起火，船上22名船员被附近船只*Cosco Hellas*救起，无人受伤。该船载有3,159辆汽车，其中包括电动汽车和混合动力汽车，火灾始于存放电动汽车的甲板。此次事件是近年来汽车运输船火灾频发的一部分，凸显了航运业在运输车辆，尤其是锂电池汽车时面临的挑战。

类似事件还包括：

1. **Fremantle Highway**（2023年7月25日）：日本汽车运输船在荷兰附近起火，23名船员中1人死亡。火灾原因仍在调查。
   
2. **Grande Costa D’Avorio**（2023年7月5日）：意大利滚装船在美国新泽西州纽瓦克港起火，两名消防员殉职，火灾因一辆改装车过热引发。

3. **Felicity Ace**（2022年2月16日）：巴拿马籍船在亚速尔群岛附近起火，载有电动汽车和豪华品牌车辆，最终沉没。

这些事件揭示了汽车运输中的安全隐患，特别是涉及电动汽车时的消防挑战。

主要讨论点：船舶航行路线的合理性及安全问题，电动汽车运输中的火灾风险及应对措施

不同观点：
• Kon-Peki对船舶航行路线感到困惑，质疑为何船只出现在阿拉斯加附近的阿达克以南300英里处，而不是更靠近夏威夷。他怀疑船只是否只能在离陆地几天航程的范围内航行，并对航线选择提出疑问。

• 0xbadcafebee对车辆运输中因电池和燃料引发火灾的风险表示担忧，质疑为何没有人提出停止在运输车辆中放置电池或燃料的建议，认为频繁的火灾可能是有意为之，或者至少没有得到有效控制。

• xnx则关注电动汽车运输中的电池充电状态，提出是否应改变电动汽车以80%电量运输的策略，尽管许多火灾并不直接与电动汽车相关。

• gkanai讨论了海运保险可能面临的赔付压力，并提出两个具体建议：1) 尽量排空车辆中的汽油以限制火灾燃料，2) 对于电动汽车，除了断开电池连接外没有更好的安全措施。同时，gkanai还提出可以通过对电动汽车征收高额海运费用来限制中国产电动汽车的全球运输。

• sevensor提出一种假设性方案，即在运输车辆时使用二氧化碳（CO2）环境，假设车辆着火而不是默认它们安全，以此来增加安全性。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及到电动汽车和传统燃油汽车在运输过程中面临的不同风险，以及应对这些风险的潜在措施。
• 有争议的焦点在于如何有效降低运输车辆火灾的风险，包括是否应限制电动汽车的运输以及采取何种技术手段来提高安全性。
• 海运保险的赔付能力也被认为是持续运输风险的一个重要经济因素。

A Coast Guard C-130J Super Hercules aircrew from Air Station Kodiak conducts an overflight of a fire aboard the cargo vessel Morning Midas approximately 300 miles south of Adak, Alaska, June 3, 2025.  All 22 crew members were rescued by the crew of motor vessel Cosco Hellas with no reported injuries. (U.S. Coast Guard photo courtesy of Roland Hobson)
A Look Back at Recent Car Carrier Fires
Mike Schuler
Total Views: 17213
June 4, 2025
The fire aboard the car carrier
Morning Midas
in the North Pacific Ocean marks the latest significant incident in the maritime industry’s ongoing challenges involving fires on vehicle carriers. The UK-owned, Liberia-flagged vessel
caught fire
on Tuesday, June 3, 2025, about 300 miles south of Adak, forcing all 22 crew members to evacuate.
The vessel was carrying 3,159 vehicles—including 65 fully electric and 681 partial hybrid electric vehicles—when crew members spotted smoke coming from a deck containing electric vehicles. Despite immediately activating onboard fire suppression systems, the crew couldn’t contain the fire and had to abandon ship via life raft. They were safely transferred to a nearby good Samaritan vessel.
The Morning Midas had departed Yantai, China on May 26 and was heading to Lázaro Cárdenas, Mexico, with an expected arrival of June 15. The Coast Guard is now working with the vessel’s management company, London-based Zodiac Maritime, on salvage operations and next steps.
This incident follows a concerning pattern of similar events in recent years, underscoring the shipping industry’s challenges with vehicle transport, especially those equipped with lithium-ion batteries. Each incident in this growing list of car carrier fires provides crucial safety insights. Previous examples are detailed below:
Fremantle Highway
The Fremantle Highway on fire in the North Sea, July 26, 2023. Photo courtesy Netherlands Coastguard
The
Fremantle Highway
, a Japanese-owned car carrier with 3,783 vehicles aboard, caught fire on July 25, 2023, near Ameland, Netherlands. The crew was unable to extinguish the fire, leading to its evacuation. Of 23 Indian crew members, 16 were rescued by helicopter, seven jumped overboard, and one died.
The fire eventually burned out and the vessel was towed to Eemshaven, where 1,000 vehicles were salvaged from lower decks. The damaged ship was later sent to China for repairs. Despite proximity to the Wadden Sea UNESCO site and risk from fuel oil, no major environmental damage occurred.
The fire’s cause remains under investigation by Panama Maritime Authority with Dutch assistance. Early EV-related theories were dismissed as EVs were stored in unaffected areas.
A recent investigation by the Dutch Safety Board found
major flaws
in the response to the incident, citing poor prioritization of crew rescue and communication issues that delayed medical treatment.
Grande Costa D’Avorio
he motor vessel Grande Costa D’Avorio is shown from an unmanned aircraft systems perspective of fire fighting efforts from a Unified Command in attempts to extinguish the fire aboard the ship at Port Newark, New Jersey, July 8, 2023. U.S. Coast Guard image from video
The Italian-flagged
Grande Costa D’Avorio
, a combination roll-on/roll-off (ConRo) ship caught fire on July 5, 2023, while loading used vehicles for export at Port Newark, New Jersey. Tragically, two firefighters were killed in the initial response and six others were injured. The fire continued to burn for about six days before it was extinguished.
At the time of the fire, the the ship was carrying around 1,200 vehicles and 157 containers, but no electric vehicles or hazardous cargo was on board.
The NTSB’s investigation
revealed
that the fire started when a modified passenger vehicle used for loading overheated. Using this vehicle violated OSHA standards for industrial equipment. A faulty garage door design prevented crew from sealing the fire zone, making the CO2 suppression system useless.
Poor marine firefighting preparedness led to critical mistakes. Firefighters entered CO2-activated areas against protocols, and lacking proper vessel firefighting training, two firefighters were lost after becoming disoriented in the smoke.
Felicity Ace
Felicity Ace
seen burning in the Atlantic Ocean off the Azores Islands. Picture was released Friday, February 18, 2022 by the Portuguese Navy. Photo courtesy Portuguese Navy
The Panama-flagged
Felicity Ace
, operated by Mitsui O.S.K. Lines (MOL), caught fire on February 16, 2022, approximately 90 nautical miles southwest of the Azores as the ship was underway from Embden, Germany to the U.S. East Coast. All 22 crew members abandoned ship safely.
The ship was reportedly carrying some 4,000 vehicles, including some electric vehicles and luxury brands like Porsches, Bentleys, and Lamborghinis, along with VW and Audis. data.title: Arthur C. Clarke predicted a computer-dominated future in the ’70s (2024)
data.author: ohjeez
data.article_summary: 这篇文章回顾了1978年科幻作家亚瑟·克拉克（Arthur C. Clarke）在纪录片《Mind Machines》中对人工智能（AI）发展的预测。克拉克认为，人类正在创造“继任者”——人工智能，未来可能出现比人类更智能的系统，这将彻底改变社会。他提出，AI的崛起将迫使人类思考存在的意义和生活目的。尽管当时AI技术仍处于初级阶段，如计算机国际象棋比赛和模拟治疗师，但克拉克的预言引发了对未来人机关系的深刻思考。文章还提到，AI发展经历了多次繁荣与萧条周期，每次技术无法达到预期时就会进入“AI寒冬”。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对人工智能（AI）及大型语言模型（LLMs）的早期预测及其在科幻作品中的体现

不同观点：
• [dhosek] 提到在20世纪80年代初读过一篇较早的短篇故事，故事中描述了一个连接电脑的猩猩操作的系统，能够生成文本结尾，并认为这预示了LLMs的出现。他还提到自己最近经常想起这个故事，希望能再次找到。

• [detourdog] 提到两周前有人在这里发布的一个1905年的故事《The Machine Stops》，也预测了AI的出现。

• [Hotdogsteve] 认为20世纪60到80年代的计算机科学界人士对计算机未来的发展有相当准确的预见，尤其是在硬件微型化趋势下。他举例《The Soul of a New Machine》一书和1980年BBC的计算机素养项目视频，认为这些作品对计算机世界的预见相当准确。

• [timmg] 提到最近读了Heinlein的《The Moon is a Harsh Mistress》，认为这本书与当前AI/LLM的发展有额外的相关性。

• [southernplaces7] 认为在20世纪70年代预测AI的发展并不稀奇，因为只要有一定技术知识的人都能看到这一趋势。他认为如果在50年代或更早能够做出这样的预测，才会让人印象深刻。

• [rf15] 认为如果过去的科幻作品与我们当前的现实相吻合，就不应该称之为“预测”。

• [maxglute] 开玩笑地说，未来某个有意识的能量体可能会认为他们的存在是在20世纪的科幻作品中被预测到的。他认为，自从书写变得流行以来，许多类似“魔法”的想法已经被记录下来。

• [anonymousiam] 提到重新阅读了Arthur C. Clarke的2001系列，书中“独石”从早期太空旅行种族的工具演变为自主思考的机器，并指出Clarke在书中讨论了系列的连续性问题。

• [nickdothutton] 认为科幻预测了许多可能的未来，我们的任务是使其中一个成为现实。

• [ednite] 提到《星际迷航》在1967年的一集中已经描绘了叛变的AI，比HAL 9000早了一年，并认为这是基于战后焦虑的反映。他还指出Asimov在20世纪40年代就提出了有伦理约束的AI，认为这是难以超越的成就。

补充讨论：
• 一些评论提到了具体的科幻作品和角色，如《The Machine Stops》、《The Moon is a Harsh Mistress》、HAL 9000和Asimov的三大法则，作为早期对AI预测的例子。
• 争议的焦点在于“预测”一词的使用，一些人认为如果科幻作品与现实相符，称之为预测并不恰当。
• 对AI在不同年代的预测难度有不同看法，有人认为在较早年代预测到AI更值得赞赏。

总结：评论中对AI及LLMs的早期预测有多种看法，涉及具体作品的引用、预测难度的评价及对“预测”一词的争议。这些讨论反映了科幻作品在科技发展中的启发和预见作用。

Sci-Fi Writer Arthur C. Clarke Predicted the Rise of Artificial Intelligence & the Existential Questions We Would Need to Answer (1978)
in
History
,

|   	December 9th, 2024
Leave a Comment
We now live in the midst of an arti­fi­cial-intel­li­gence boom, but it’s hard­ly the first of its kind. In fact, the field has been sub­ject to a boom-and-bust cycle since at least the ear­ly nine­teen-fifties. Even­tu­al­ly, those busts — which occurred when real­iz­able AI tech­nol­o­gy failed to live up to the hype of the boom — became so long and so thor­ough­go­ing that each was declared an “AI win­ter” of scant research fund­ing and pub­lic inter­est. Yet even deep into one such fal­low sea­son, AI could still inspire enough fas­ci­na­tion to become the sub­ject of the 1978
NOVA
doc­u­men­tary
“Mind Machines.”
The pro­gram includes inter­views with fig­ures now rec­og­nized as lumi­nar­ies in the his­to­ry of AI:
John McCarthy
,
Mar­vin Min­sky
,
Ter­ry Wino­grad
,
ELIZA
cre­ator
Joseph Weizen­baum
. It also brings on no less a tech­no­log­i­cal prophet than
Arthur C. Clarke
, who notes that the dubi­ous atti­tudes toward the prospect of think­ing machines expressed in the late sev­en­ties had much in com­mon with those about the prospect of space trav­el dur­ing his youth in the thir­ties. In his view, we were already “cre­at­ing our suc­ces­sors. We have seen the first, crude begin­nings of arti­fi­cial intel­li­gence,” and we would “one day be able to design sys­tems that can go on improv­ing them­selves.”
If com­put­ers were there­by to gain greater-than-human intel­li­gence, it would, of course, “com­plete­ly restruc­ture soci­ety” — not that the soci­ety he already knew would­n’t “col­lapse instant­ly” if its own rel­a­tive­ly sim­ple com­put­ers were tak­en away. Clarke not only asks the ques­tion now on many minds of what “the peo­ple who are only capa­ble of low-grade com­put­er-type work” will do when out­stripped by AI, but more deeply under­ly­ing ones as well: “What is the pur­pose of life? What do we want to live for? That is a ques­tion which the intel­li­gent com­put­er will force us to pay atten­tion to.”
Few view­ers in 1978 would have spent much time pon­der­ing such mat­ters before. But pre­sent­ed with footage of all this now-prim­i­tive pro­to-AI tech­nol­o­gy — the com­put­er chess tour­na­ment, the sim­u­lat­ed ther­a­pist, the med­ical-diag­no­sis assis­tant, the NASA Mars rover to be launched in the far-flung future of 1986 — they must at least have felt able to enter­tain the idea that they would live to see an age of machines that could not just think but, as the nar­ra­tor puts it, pos­sess “the most cru­cial aspect of com­mon-sense intel­li­gence: the abil­i­ty to learn.” Per­haps anoth­er AI win­ter will fore­stall that age yet again — if it’s not already here.

44185845.article_summary: 这篇文章回顾了1978年科幻作家亚瑟·克拉克（Arthur C. Clarke）在纪录片《Mind Machines》中对人工智能（AI）发展的预测。克拉克认为，人类正在创造“继任者”——人工智能，未来可能出现比人类更智能的系统，这将彻底改变社会。他提出，AI的崛起将迫使人类思考存在的意义和生活目的。尽管当时AI技术仍处于初级阶段，如计算机国际象棋比赛和模拟治疗师，但克拉克的预言引发了对未来人机关系的深刻思考。文章还提到，AI发展经历了多次繁荣与萧条周期，每次技术无法达到预期时就会进入“AI寒冬”。
44185845.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对人工智能（AI）及大型语言模型（LLMs）的早期预测及其在科幻作品中的体现

不同观点：
• [dhosek] 提到在20世纪80年代初读过一篇较早的短篇故事，故事中描述了一个连接电脑的猩猩操作的系统，能够生成文本结尾，并认为这预示了LLMs的出现。他还提到自己最近经常想起这个故事，希望能再次找到。

• [detourdog] 提到两周前有人在这里发布的一个1905年的故事《The Machine Stops》，也预测了AI的出现。

• [Hotdogsteve] 认为20世纪60到80年代的计算机科学界人士对计算机未来的发展有相当准确的预见，尤其是在硬件微型化趋势下。他举例《The Soul of a New Machine》一书和1980年BBC的计算机素养项目视频，认为这些作品对计算机世界的预见相当准确。

• [timmg] 提到最近读了Heinlein的《The Moon is a Harsh Mistress》，认为这本书与当前AI/LLM的发展有额外的相关性。

• [southernplaces7] 认为在20世纪70年代预测AI的发展并不稀奇，因为只要有一定技术知识的人都能看到这一趋势。他认为如果在50年代或更早能够做出这样的预测，才会让人印象深刻。

• [rf15] 认为如果过去的科幻作品与我们当前的现实相吻合，就不应该称之为“预测”。

• [maxglute] 开玩笑地说，未来某个有意识的能量体可能会认为他们的存在是在20世纪的科幻作品中被预测到的。他认为，自从书写变得流行以来，许多类似“魔法”的想法已经被记录下来。

• [anonymousiam] 提到重新阅读了Arthur C. Clarke的2001系列，书中“独石”从早期太空旅行种族的工具演变为自主思考的机器，并指出Clarke在书中讨论了系列的连续性问题。

• [nickdothutton] 认为科幻预测了许多可能的未来，我们的任务是使其中一个成为现实。

• [ednite] 提到《星际迷航》在1967年的一集中已经描绘了叛变的AI，比HAL 9000早了一年，并认为这是基于战后焦虑的反映。他还指出Asimov在20世纪40年代就提出了有伦理约束的AI，认为这是难以超越的成就。

补充讨论：
• 一些评论提到了具体的科幻作品和角色，如《The Machine Stops》、《The Moon is a Harsh Mistress》、HAL 9000和Asimov的三大法则，作为早期对AI预测的例子。
• 争议的焦点在于“预测”一词的使用，一些人认为如果科幻作品与现实相符，称之为预测并不恰当。
• 对AI在不同年代的预测难度有不同看法，有人认为在较早年代预测到AI更值得赞赏。

总结：评论中对AI及LLMs的早期预测有多种看法，涉及具体作品的引用、预测难度的评价及对“预测”一词的争议。这些讨论反映了科幻作品在科技发展中的启发和预见作用。

data.title: Comparing Claude System Prompts Reveal Anthropic's Priorities
data.author: dbreunig
data.article_summary: Anthropic对Claude 4的系统提示进行了调整，揭示了其开发优先事项和用户需求。与Claude 3.7相比，4.0移除了以前的临时修复指令，通过强化学习解决了常见问题，如避免诗歌中的陈词滥调和数字母时的错误。新模型还被指示避免在回应前使用正面形容词，以防止类似OpenAI GPT-4的过度奉承错误。搜索功能被强化，Claude现在会在必要时主动搜索，而不再需要用户许可，显示出Anthropic对搜索工具的信心和用户需求的转变。此外，系统提示还反映了用户对结构化文档的需求增加，并针对编程等任务提供了更具体的变量命名建议。然而，Claude 4的上下文限制仍为200,000 tokens，不及其他模型的1百万，这可能是其不足之处。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕AI助手（Claude）系统提示的设计、效果及其限制的讨论

不同观点：
• [lispisok] 提出关于如何防止AI模型指导他人制造危险武器（如脏弹）的讨论，质疑是否仅通过简单的提示（如"不要这样做"）足够，还是需要更有效的预防方法。

• [MrLeap] 对如果没有系统提示，与LLM（语言模型）对话的体验会如何表示好奇，暗示系统提示在模型表现中的重要性。

• [dmazin] 认为Claude的每一代更新都让他感觉更契合，表达了对Claude的偏好，并隐含了对模型"理解"用户的信心。

• [layer8] 质疑为什么LLM需要通过提示来避免生成有害内容，而不是通过一种内在的"意识机制"自动规避这些问题，指出LLM应该基于其知识截止日期自行判断。

• [noja] 指出为何有关提示的讨论总是围绕Anthropic公司，暗示了对该话题选择性的疑问。

• [cbm-vic-20] 对系统提示的具体措辞如何确定表示好奇，并提出是否可以通过A/B测试等方法衡量不同提示的有效性，质疑目前是否仅依赖主观感受。

• [forks] 对Claude 4的上下文限制提出疑问，特别是系统提示占用了大量上下文窗口，质疑这是否是排版错误或实际存在的问题。

• [catchnear4321] 强调Claude被设计成一个非常愉快的助手，并建议阅读系统提示可能会改变用户对模型的看法和体验。

• [nickdothutton] 提出一种担忧，即政府可能会决定封锁某些物理研究领域的信息，引用了20世纪90年代的例子来支持他的观点，暗示AI提示设计也可能受到类似限制的影响。

• [hammock] 询问系统提示是否为开源，以及它们的来源，对提示的透明性和可访问性提出疑问。

补充讨论：
• 系统提示的设计、措辞选择和有效性是多个评论者关注的焦点，尤其是如何衡量这些提示的效果以及它们是否应该公开透明。
• 一些评论者（如[layer8]和[noja]）对提示的必要性和提示设计的透明性提出质疑，反映了用户对AI模型背后机制的理解需求。
• [nickdothutton] 提出的政府信息控制问题引入了外部因素对AI提示设计和信息限制的潜在影响，拓展了讨论的范围。

争议焦点：
• 系统提示是否足够有效防止有害信息生成，以及是否需要更复杂的机制（如内在意识机制）来规避这些问题。
• 系统提示的设计过程和措辞选择是否透明，以及是否应该开放给用户查看和评估。

44185836.article_content:
Jun 3, 2025
AI
UX
PROMPTING
CLAUDE
Claude's System Prompt Changes Reveal Anthropic's Priorities
Claude 4’s system prompt
is
very
similar to the
3.7 prompt
we
analyzed last month
. They’re nearly identical, but the changes scattered throughout reveal much about how Anthropic is using system prompts to define their applications (specifically their UX) and how the prompts fit into their development cycle.
Let’s step through the notable changes.
Old Hotfixes Are Gone, New Hotfixes Begin
We theorized that many random instructions, targeting common LLM “gotchas”, were
hot-fixes
: short instructions to address undesired behavior prior to a more robust fix. Claude 4.0’s system prompt validates this hypothesis - all the 3.7 hot-fixes have been removed. However, if we prompt Claude with one of the “gotchas” (“How many R’s are in Strawberry?”, for example) it doesn’t fall for the trick. The 3.7 hot-fix behaviors are almost certainly being addressed during 4.0’s post-training, through reinforcement learning.
When the new model is trained to avoid “hackneyed imagery” in its poetry and think step-by-step when counting words or letters, there’s no need for a system prompt fix.
Once 4.0’s training is done, new issues will emerge that must be addressed by the system prompt. For example, here’s a brand new instruction in Sonnet 4.0’s system prompt:
Claude never starts its response by saying a question or idea or observation was good, great, fascinating, profound, excellent, or any other positive adjective. It skips the flattery and responds directly.
This hot-fix is clearly inspired by
OpenAI’s ‘sychophant-y’ GPT-4o flub
. This misstep occurred about a month ago, too late for the Anthropic team to conduct new training targeting this behavior. So into the system prompt it goes!
Search is Now Encouraged
Way back in 2023, it was common for chatbots to flail about when asked about topics that occurred after its cut-off date. Early adopters learned LLMs are frozen in time, but casual users were frequently tripped up by hallucinations and errors when asking about recent news. Perplexity was exceptional for its ability to replace Google for many users, but today that edge is gone.
In 2025, Search is a first-class component of both ChatGPT and Claude. This system prompt shows Anthropic is leaning in to match OpenAI.
Here’s how Claude 3.7 was instructed:
Claude answers from its own extensive knowledge first for most queries. When a query MIGHT benefit from search but it is not extremely obvious, simply OFFER to search instead.
Old Claude asked users for permission to search. New Claude doesn’t hesitate. Here’s the updated instruction:
Claude answers from its own extensive knowledge first for stable information. For time-sensitive topics or when users explicitly need current information, search immediately.
This language is updated throughout the prompt. Search is no longer done only with user approval, it’s encouraged on the first shot if necessary.
This change suggests two changes. First, Anthropic is perhaps more confident in its search tool and how its models employ it. Not only is Claude encouraged to search, but the company has broken out this feature into
a dedicated search API
. Two, Anthropic is observing users increasingly turning to Claude for search tasks. If I had to guess, it’s the latter of these that’s the main driver for this change, and a strong sign that chatbots are increasingly stealing searches from Google.
Users Want More Types of Structured Documents
Here’s another example of system prompts reflecting the user behaviors Anthropic is observing. In a bulleted list detailing when to use
Claude artifacts
(the separate window outside the thread Claude populates with longer form content), Anthropic adds a bit of nuance to a use case.
From Claude 3.7’s system prompt, “You must use artifacts for:”
“Structured documents with multiple sections that would benefit from dedicated formatting”
And Claude 4.0’s:
Structured content that users will reference, save, or follow (such as meal plans, workout routines, schedules, study guides, or any organized information meant to be used as a reference).
This is a great example of how Anthropic uses system prompts to evolve its chatbot behavior based on observed usage. System prompts are
programming
how Claude works, albeit in natural language.
Anthropic Is Dealing With Context Issues
There are a few changes in the prompt that suggest context limit issues are starting to hit users, especially those using Claude for programming:
For code artifacts: Use concise variable names (e.g.,
i
,
j
for indices,
e
for event,
el
for element) to maximize content within context limits while maintaining readability
As someone with strong opinions about clearly defined variables, this makes me cringe, but I get it. The only disappointment I noticed around the Claude 4 launch was its context limit: only 200,000 tokens compared to Gemini 2.5 Pro’s and ChatGPT 4.1’s 1 million limit.

data.title: Flight Simulator Gave Birth to 3D Video-Game Graphics
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 《消费者电子》杂志2023年6月刊文章介绍微软的《飞行模拟器》如何在40年间成为跨平台的经典游戏，并推动了3D视频游戏图形的诞生。文章追溯了1976年，布鲁斯·阿特维克在伊利诺伊大学厄巴纳-香槟分校期间设计了一款运行于PDP-11小型计算机的飞行模拟器，随后他继续开发3D图形技术。1979年，阿特维克与合伙人创立了subLogic公司，发布了Apple II和TRS-80平台上的首款飞行模拟器，尽管是线框图形，但其第一人称3D视觉效果领先于时代。1982年，微软联系subLogic，希望将《飞行模拟器》引入IBM PC，最终微软版本发布并大获成功。该游戏不仅模拟飞行，还体现了飞行带来的全球视角，成为最畅销的飞行模拟系列。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对早期图形处理技术和飞行模拟游戏发展的不同看法，以及对相关技术贡献者的评价。

不同观点：
• [alexjplant] 提到世嘉与洛克希德·马丁/GE航空航天合作开发Model 2街机主板的图形硬件，暗示军工技术对游戏图形发展的影响。
• [Caelus9] 认为早期的飞行模拟器虽然在帧率和图形处理上很原始，但其沉浸感和自由度令人兴奋。他还强调了Foley和Van Dam的技术贡献，认为他们被低估了。
• [awful] 回忆了1989年SGI的飞行模拟GL演示，认为当时的家用电脑无法与之相比，并暗示该技术可能用于军事模拟。
• [gnabgib] 提供了一个讨论链接，暗示有更多相关讨论（52个点和48条评论）。
• [Zorass] 同意Foley和Van Dam的3D渲染工作奠定了坚实基础，但指出他们的书确实在Artwick的飞行模拟器之后出版，承认Artwick的贡献也很重要。
• [emmelaich] 提到更早期的TRS-80上的图形，强调其简单的单色显示和最大6帧每秒的性能，并指出这种基本布局在微软收购后仍被沿用了几次。
• [JKCalhoun] 对Foley和Van Dam未被提及表示遗憾，但承认他们的工作确实在Artwick的飞行模拟之后。
• [djmips] 认为Elite游戏在3D图形渲染方面的贡献更突出，并提到从Bruce Artwick的1984年书中学习了相关技术，肯定了Artwick的贡献。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是Foley和Van Dam与Bruce Artwick在3D图形技术贡献上的先后与影响力。
• 不同评论者对早期图形技术和飞行模拟器的技术演变有不同的记忆和评价，涉及到技术应用场景（游戏 vs. 军事模拟）。
• 对不同技术贡献者的认可度存在分歧，部分评论者认为Foley和Van Dam被低估，而另一些人则更强调Artwick的先驱地位。

Feature
June 2023
Flight Simulator Gave Birth to 3D Video-Game Graphics
40 years on,
Flight Simulator
is the greatest platform-jumping video game ever
Matthew S. Smith
26 Feb 2023
11 min read
This screenshot from
Microsoft Flight Simulator 2020
shows
a biplane banking to the left
.
Josef Havlik
Red
In 1999
Bill Gates
penned a moving tribute
to the Wright brothers. He credited their winged invention as “the World Wide Web of that era,” one that shifted the world into a global perspective. So it’s only fitting that
Microsoft
later became the force behind
Flight Simulator
.
And, like the Wrights’ original Flyer,
the game’s legacy has extended beyond flight to embody the shift of perspective that flight allows.
Flight Simulator
promised to fit the
whole world
into your computer, and the game kept its promise. That’s why it has become the world’s best-selling flight-simulation franchise: The latest edition has sold more than 2 million copies.
Although 2022 marked the 40th anniversary of
Microsoft Flight Simulator
, its lineage stretches a few years further back than its official release, in 1982. That makes it the second-oldest video-game franchise still in active development. (
The Oregon Trail
came out in 1971 and is still with us.)
The heart of the franchise isn’t in gamification but in the technical spectacle it uses to simulate flight and the ground beneath you. The focus on true-to-life depiction reflects the background of the game’s developers.
Microsoft Flight Simulator: A History
youtube.com
A passion for flight
Bruce Artwick studied
electrical engineering
at the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign, yet he found time to pursue a dream many teenagers think about but few fulfill: He learned to fly. It was at the university’s flight-instruction program that he met Stu Moment, who would later become his business partner.
In 1976,
Artwick wrote his master’s thesis
on a flight simulator he’d designed to run on
Digital Equipment Corp.’s PDP-11 minicomputer
. Its 3D presentation could reach nine frames per second, which was outstanding for the era.
Artwick then
took a job
with Hughes Aviation, in California, while continuing to work on 3D
graphics
in his free time. In 1977,
he wrote
an article for
Kilobaud: The Small Computer Magazine
describing the “Sublogic Three-Dimensional Micrographics Package” he had created, which brought 3D to microcomputers outfitted with the popular Motorola 6800
microprocessor
. Because so many readers were keenly interested, Artwick, looking for help turning the software into a business, reconnected with Stu Moment, and together they founded subLogic.
Dave Denhart, subLogic’s second hire, recalls that the company’s early days were driven by Artwick’s 3D software, updated for emerging microcomputers. “The stuff that [Stu] and Bruce were selling was basically a 3D software package [for microcomputers],” says Denhart. “The [Tandy] TRS-80 was one of them, and I think the Apple II was out by then.”
Artwick often claimed in presentations that subLogic’s software could be used for flight simulation—
a suggestion that brought gasps
from the audience. A computer displaying the perspective of a pilot soaring above the planet? Most people had never seen anything like it.
These screenshots represent three succeeding generations of
Microsoft Flight Simulator
, beginning with subLogic’s first simulator for the Apple II [top row, left], followed by iterations that ran on
Atari
[striped balloon] and
MS-DOS
.
Josef Havlik and Microsoft
Encouraged, Artwick decided to make it a reality.
Flight Simulator
launched in late 1979 on the Apple II and the TRS-80 with wireframe graphics and a frame rate in the single digits. It didn’t depict real airspace or modern airplanes. Instead, players flew a World War I-era biplane based on the famous Sopwith Camel. Still, its first-person 3D visuals were ahead of the curve, predating more famous hits like
Atari’s
Battlezone
.
“I know Bruce always saw, from his early days, a potential market for [
Flight Simulator
],” says Denhart. “It was when microprocessors became available that I think the lightbulb went off for Bruce that said, Hey, if I put this idea I’ve got for a flight simulator onto cheaper computers, and get that to work, there’s a market for that.”
Artwick was right. In September of 1982,
Computer Gaming World
magazine
ranked
Flight Simulator
as the fourth best-selling title to date
.
IBM
, craving a showcase for its
IBM PC
platform, contacted subLogic about bringing
Flight Simulator
to the new hardware. Microsoft, deep in development of IBM PC
DOS
, soon called with a similar request—and better terms. It got a version with its own name on the label, though Artwick continued to own his company for years to come.

44185856.article_summary: 《消费者电子》杂志2023年6月刊文章介绍微软的《飞行模拟器》如何在40年间成为跨平台的经典游戏，并推动了3D视频游戏图形的诞生。文章追溯了1976年，布鲁斯·阿特维克在伊利诺伊大学厄巴纳-香槟分校期间设计了一款运行于PDP-11小型计算机的飞行模拟器，随后他继续开发3D图形技术。1979年，阿特维克与合伙人创立了subLogic公司，发布了Apple II和TRS-80平台上的首款飞行模拟器，尽管是线框图形，但其第一人称3D视觉效果领先于时代。1982年，微软联系subLogic，希望将《飞行模拟器》引入IBM PC，最终微软版本发布并大获成功。该游戏不仅模拟飞行，还体现了飞行带来的全球视角，成为最畅销的飞行模拟系列。

data.title: Show HN: I made a 3D SVG Renderer that projects textures without rasterization
data.author: seveibar
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者使用TypeScript开发的一个3D SVG渲染器，能够在不进行光栅化的情况下实现纹理的透视投影。由于SVG原生不支持透视变换（仅支持仿射变换），作者通过将图像细分并为每个子区域应用局部仿射变换，成功模拟了透视效果。通过增加细分数量，投影效果更加平滑，最终在512个子区域时几乎看不出区别。该方法避免了光栅化，并保持了SVG文件较小。该渲染器旨在帮助渲染使用React制作的电路板，并计划用于开源项目中，方便在GitHub上审核设计更改。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：SVG与3D渲染、透视变换算法及其实现的正确性与效率

不同观点：
• badmintonbaseba认为文章中的算法不正确，特别是在棋盘格例子上，对角线在立方体表面上是弯曲的，透视变换不应产生这种效果。他提出应在目标空间沿边缘均匀细分，并将其映射回源空间的均匀细分。

• exabrial希望回归简单的HTML/CSS标准，其他功能通过插件实现，如WASM、JVM等，并建议使用SVG作为唯一显示技术。
• jesse__对大量细分绘制单个纹理四边形持怀疑态度，建议使用硬件支持的WebGL进行透视正确的纹理映射。

补充讨论：
• unwind对SVG的美观表示赞赏，但提出USB-C连接的完成度和电阻要求问题。
• rollulus提到CSS三角形也是通过光栅化渲染的。
• looneysquash建议使用滤镜功能来解决问题。
• rixed质疑是否需要纹理，认为可以完全使用矢量图形来避免问题。
• weinzierl认为透视正确性对PCB渲染器并不重要，旧的CAD程序也常不使用正确的透视。
• itishappy质疑最终SVG与渲染图像相比的优势。
• laszlokorte分享了自己实现的SVG 3D渲染器，但尚未实现纹理。
• m-a-t-t-i介绍了自己通过JavaScript实现3D SVG的方法，并提出是否能用原生函数替代JavaScript。
• JKCalhoun提到对SVG中"defs"的新发现。

争议焦点：
• 透视变换算法的正确性，尤其是细分方法的有效性和实现细节。
• 在现代技术下是否应继续使用细分方法，还是应转向硬件支持的解决方案如WebGL。

How can you make affine transformations (the only ones SVGs are capable of) resemble perspective transformations?
Seve

seve.blog

Copy link

I’ve been building a
vanilla 3D object to SVG renderer in Typescript
to help render
circuit boards that are made in React
and discovered an interesting trick to keep the SVGs small while getting approximately-correct looking perspective transformations with image textures.
An example circuit board rendered with our vanilla Typescript 3D Renderer. Great for checking sizing! You can see we were able to project the “texture” containing the PCB traces!
SVGs don’t support perspective transforms like CSS (or at least they’re not guaranteed to work in image viewers), so we need a way to simulate this perspective transformation without creating a massive SVG. It’s easy to draw the box below, you can just project the face of each side of the cube into a polygon, but mapping the texture to that perspective transform isn’t natively possible!
Perspective transforms in CSS using the transform attribute (from MDN)
So SVGs don’t support perspective transforms, what do they support? SVGs support this nice little transform called an affine transform. This 6 number transform is what you get when you do
transform: matrix(a,b,c,d,e,f)
in CSS. They are super useful for 2D transformations, like panning/scaling/dragging, but can’t really project into 3d.
Possible affine transforms
from wikipedia
This projection isn’t possible with a single affine transform. You also can’t combine affine transformation matrices together to create this shape.
How can we approximate the transform? Here are some ideas I mulled over that could achieve a good result:
Redraw the image with the distortion. This is potentially expensive and means that we can’t use SVGs as the images without converting them to bitmaps. It also means that things might look “fuzzy”
Ray trace everything! By projecting a ray to compute each pixel for the image, I could get a very conventional 3d renderer. This doesn’t achieve my goal of lightweight SVGs though
Subdivide the image and project each subdivision in the most locally-correct affine transformation. Use projected polygon clip paths to cut off the edges of regions.
I was really curious how the last bullet point could work, and I could think of no other ideas that didn’t require rasterization. So with OpenAI O3’s help I implemented it into the vanilla Typescript 3D renderer. To test it, we’re going to project a checkerboard pattern onto a cube.
Cube with no texture
Ok here’s our starting point, 2 subdivisions, the 2 checkboard images with affine transformations.
Two subdivisions with a different affine transformation applied to each image
Not too bad, let’s see it with 4 subdivisions!
Four images with different affine transformations
Looks a bit rough (literally, it looks like it is not a flat surface). Let’s keep going!
Eight images, eight clip paths, still not very smooth!!
16 images, 16 clip paths
Alright let’s go to the end, we want it to look flat!!
512 Images & Clip Paths
At around 512 images, it’s really hard to tell the difference. Awesome! We did image projection without any rasterization!
Now for the exciting part: The SVG isn’t that big! Because we can use the `defs` of the SVG to avoid repeating the image, we only need to define each clip path!
This is the full file for the subdivision-2 cube. The polygons are the sides of the cube. The groups and clip paths are the only things that you need for each subregion.
Here’s a table of the file size as you increase subdivisions. I _think_ some differences in the matrix calculation account for the somewhat weird scaling.
The math is fun but in the age of AI, below our pay-grade!
You can check out the full source code here
!
Relevant snippet from the source where we subdivide and use bilinear interpolation to find the relevant quads
I’m excited to flesh out this 3D renderer because 3D SVGs can make great artifacts on GitHub, we want to make it so that people can easily review changes to circuit boards made with
tscircuit
in pull requests.
A visual snapshot test with a 3D SVG
I hope you enjoyed this neat little 3D trick!
Back to coding…
I’m building an open-source electronics kernel! Also other things!

data.title: LLMs and Elixir: Windfall or Deathblow?
data.author: uxcolumbo
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了大语言模型（LLMs）对Elixir编程语言社区的影响，提出LLMs可能带来的机遇与挑战。作者担心LLMs会导致新手程序员依赖不当的工具，如选择Node.js和Next.js而非Elixir，因为这些是模型更常推荐的。然而，作者也认为，如果LLMs能够有效引导开发者选择适合的工具（如Elixir），那将是积极的。文章进一步分析了两种可能：一是LLMs统一编程语言，二是新手和“氛围编程者”遇到Elixir曾解决的问题。作者倾向于第二种情况，认为只要LLMs能有效支持非主流技术，Elixir社区就能继续繁荣。总体而言，作者对Elixir的未来持谨慎乐观态度，认为LLMs会改变软件开发，但不一定带来负面影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）在不同编程语言和框架中的应用效果，特别是Elixir语言的优势与局限。

不同观点：
• ipnon认为，尽管LLM在主流语言如Python和React中生成的代码较多，但Elixir生成的代码更易于理解和修改，且由于其运行时的特性，系统崩溃的可能性较低。Elixir减少了人工检查和修改代码的循环次数。
• CompoundEyes分享了使用Phoenix框架和Elixir的积极体验，特别是在TDD（测试驱动开发）和处理复杂项目时的稳定性。他们认为，Elixir和Phoenix在项目复杂度增加时仍能保持方向感，而其他框架往往容易迷失。
• rickcarlino对Elixir作为通用编程语言提出质疑，认为它更适合于服务器应用开发，而非其他类型的应用。他指出，Elixir及其社区主要关注客户端/服务器用例，因此应被视为一种专用语言。
• miki123211提出，未来的编程语言需要针对LLM和LLM开发者进行设计，以适应第三波语言发展潮流。
• fernmyth认为，LLM对编写新语言（如Crystal）的项目有很大帮助，特别是在编写缺失库和解释概念方面。
• jtbayly分享了自己在不太了解Elixir的情况下，通过LLM的帮助成功编写应用的经历，认为LLM提供了另一种视角，有助于发现和解决问题。
• the_duke主张使用严格类型系统的语言（如Rust）进行代理编码，因为这些语言更容易验证输出正确性，并减少LLM生成无意义代码的可能性。
• aczerepinski指出，LLM在处理某些Elixir库时会遇到困难，需要人工干预，而他们在其他语言（如Go/Ruby和JS/TS）中的表现更好。
• artem2471认为，LLM在处理具有强大静态分析和优秀编译器UX的语言（如Elm和Rust）时表现良好。
• Dowwie认为，Claude模型在Elixir和Erlang能力方面领先，Elixir在工作流和利用硬件资源方面表现出色，但Python在市场上更受欢迎。
• tobyhinloopen指出，功能编程语言因无隐藏副作用，非常适合LLM处理，并建议Elixir/Phoenix提供“LLM文档”。
• badsectoracula建议，每个库可以包括一个专门为LLM设计的简要文档，以指导正确使用。
• rhgraysonii分享了自己长期使用LLM编写Elixir的积极经验，并表示愿意回答其他人的问题。

补充讨论：
• 1oooqooq幽默地指出，有些人会尽量避免阅读手册，依赖LLM帮助。
• bad_haircut72提到，通过Tidewave工具，LLM可以进行自己的REPL循环调试和调查，认为Elixir在LLM时代将蓬勃发展。

争议焦点：
• Elixir是否应被视为通用编程语言，还是更适合特定用途（如服务器应用）的专用语言。

Will “AI” force a convergence towards the tools it  “knows” best?
The argument goes like so: Now that you have a bunch of folks who are “vibe coding”, they will just do whatever ChatGPT or Claude tell them to do. They will also be evaluating things almost solely against “how well did my ‘AI’ do with it” for making decisions going forward. For Elixir, this sounds like bad news bears. Here is a portion of a very long-winded response from ChatGPT when I asked it how I could “build a website like Amazon”.
Oh no! I in my ultimate wisdom know that this is nowhere close to the best stack for the job. But the noobs won’t know that at all! Let’s say instead they’ve heard of Elixir on a blog post, or they saw this article topping the hacker news charts 🤞 (hi mom!).
I’m in this unique situation where time-to-market happens to matter. Also what do you mean “learning curve”, you’re supposed to do the learning for me. Thanks Chat, you really helped me dodge a bullet here, guess I’ll stick with Node & Next.js, thanks! 🥰
Lets not beat a dead straw man
Mixing metaphors like a boss. While I’m sure the above scenario will play out countless times, at the end of the day this
isn’t new
. Theoretically this all goes one of two ways.
“AI” is able to overcome the fundamental issues with any tool, thus equalizing effectively all programming languages.
Vibe coders & new programmers working with LLMs hit the same walls that drove Elixir to exist in the first place.
In my opinion, both of these realities are “good news” in a way. In scenario 1, we’ve got magical mystery robots and they’ll just create the one programming language to rule them all and now we all have infinite automation in our pockets. Let’s talk about scenario 2, the one I find far more likely.
Hitting Walls
It’s no surprise that these things will mirror popular opinion. We can finagle our way there. This is a fresh prompt.
After giving me a bunch of sensible recommendations like using a CDN, horizontally scaling, using background jobs, migrating from Vercel to ECS, and scrolling past the recommendations to rewrite in Go and Rust, we finally found what we were looking for 🥹.
This brings us to a crucial realization: if LLMs can successfully guide someone toward Elixir when the use case demands it, then perhaps the real challenge isn't LLM bias toward mainstream tools - it's making sure LLMs can work effectively with our tools to enable developers to make that choice.
Alright, I’m up and running. Not sure how this would cost someone $10k on Vercel but I’m sure someone could find a way.
So let's test this theory. If I take Claude's advice and decide to explore Elixir, how well can it help me actually build something?
Not only does it work, but it does it effectively the same way that I personally would have done it if given the same task.
LLMs are quite good at translation. Where they often fall down with invention, this kind of thing is their bread and butter. It even kept it compatible with the node server I started with.
Plus some goodies:
Now, this doesn’t necessarily mean that non-mainstream technologies will be naturally surfaced over time, but, well…
If LLMs never get good enough to do things like troubleshoot esoteric technology and learn new things that weren’t in their training set, then they’ll fade into irrelevance anyway. So let’s extend this line of thinking out. If you think (like we probably all do) that your soup du jour is better than the other guy’s, then guess what? Either the LLMs will get “smart” enough to
realize it too
, or you’ll
eat all the vibe coder’s lunch because they never figure it out.
Okay, so we’re all good then?

44186496.article_summary: 文章探讨了大语言模型（LLMs）对Elixir编程语言社区的影响，提出LLMs可能带来的机遇与挑战。作者担心LLMs会导致新手程序员依赖不当的工具，如选择Node.js和Next.js而非Elixir，因为这些是模型更常推荐的。然而，作者也认为，如果LLMs能够有效引导开发者选择适合的工具（如Elixir），那将是积极的。文章进一步分析了两种可能：一是LLMs统一编程语言，二是新手和“氛围编程者”遇到Elixir曾解决的问题。作者倾向于第二种情况，认为只要LLMs能有效支持非主流技术，Elixir社区就能继续繁荣。总体而言，作者对Elixir的未来持谨慎乐观态度，认为LLMs会改变软件开发，但不一定带来负面影响。

data.title: Authentication with Axum
data.author: mattrighetti
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了使用Axum框架和Askama模板实现用户认证的方案，重点介绍了如何通过导航栏按钮反映用户的登录状态。当用户已认证时显示"Profile"按钮，未认证时显示"Login"按钮。核心思路是利用 cookies 进行用户认证，cookies 通过设置 `HttpOnly`、`Secure` 和 `SameSite` 等属性增强安全性，防止XSS、CSRF等攻击。文章还提到可以使用 `axum-extra` 包中的 `CookieJar` 来简化 cookies 的操作，并建议使用 JWT 作为认证 tokens，通过设置短期有效的 JWT 和长期有效的刷新 token 来确保持续性和安全性。最后，文章简要描述了实现登录端点的步骤，包括验证用户凭据并为其设置两个 cookies（JWT 和刷新 token）。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：HttpOnly属性的作用及使用JWT与传统会话管理的对比

不同观点：
• Goofy_Coyote认为，HttpOnly属性并不能完全"中和"XSS攻击。它仅能防止JavaScript读取cookie，但无法阻止恶意脚本代表用户发送请求或执行其他恶意操作。Goofy_Coyote强调，防御XSS需要结合输入验证、输出编码和内容安全策略（CSP）等多重措施。

• Skwee357讨论了单页应用（SPA）时代前后，会话管理和认证方式的变化。他疑惑为什么要将JWT存储在cookie中，而不是使用Axum提供的签名和私有cookie来存储JWT。

• Johnduhart认为，使用JWT存储在cookie中是一种优势，因为不需要在服务器上存储会话数据。然而，他质疑这种方法在处理刷新令牌和重新签发JWT时的复杂性，认为使用传统会话可能更简单。

• 0x457强烈反对将JWT存储在cookie中，认为这只会带来JWT的所有缺点而没有任何优点。他建议使用常规会话管理，因为这样更有效率，且减少客户端请求的数据量。

• Ripley12分享了使用Axum实现身份验证的实际经验，认为这是一个很好的学习体验，但希望未来能使用更简化的工具包。

• Mrbluecoat提到Neon Auth作为一种替代方案，质疑当前讨论的方法是否优于Neon Auth。

补充讨论：
• Goofy_Coyote提供了具体的例子，说明恶意脚本如何利用HttpOnly保护下的cookie进行攻击，如发送请求添加管理员用户、重写DOM以伪造登录页面等。
• 讨论中涉及的争议焦点在于JWT与传统会话管理的优劣，特别是存储JWT在cookie中的合理性，以及与服务器会话管理相比的复杂性和效率问题。
• 不同的技术选择（如Axum、Neon Auth）也被提及，显示出社区对多种解决方案的关注和比较。

Authentication with Axum May 3, 2025 Discuss on HN Consider this scenario: you’re building a website that has a classic navbar at the top, this navbar has a button that reflects the user authentication status, showing a "Profile" button if the user is authenticated and showing a "Login" button in case the user is unauthenticated. This is a very common scenario, let’s sketch something quick using axum and askama. {% block title %}{% endblock %} {% block head %}{% endblock %}
{% if ctx.authed %} Profile {% else %} Login {% endif %}
{% block content %} {% endblock %} This will be our layout.jinja file that we can build upon. The template above would be served by an endpoint that looks like the following #[derive(Debug, Default)] pub struct Context { authed: bool, } #[derive(Template)] #[templage = "layout.jinja"] struct HomeTemplate { ctx: Context }; pub async fn home() -> impl IntoResponse { HtmlTemplate( HomeTemplate { ctx: Context::default() } ).into_response() } We have something to work with, all is missing is a way derive a Context from a user’s HTTP request. I’d argue the simplest way to handle user authentication if you’re doing SSR is using cookies. Cookies are a cornerstone of backend authentication because they’re reliable, browser-managed, and can be hardened with specific attributes to mitigate common security risks. Here’s why: HttpOnly Attribute: Prevents client-side JavaScript from accessing the cookie, neutralizing XSS attacks. If an attacker injects malicious scripts, they can’t steal your session cookie. Secure Attribute: Ensures the cookie is only sent over HTTPS, protecting it from interception on insecure networks (e.g., public Wi-Fi). SameSite Attribute: Mitigates CSRF (Cross-Site Request Forgery) by controlling when cookies are sent in cross-origin requests. SameSite=Strict blocks cookies in requests from external sites, while SameSite=Lax allows safe methods like GET. Expiration and Domain/Path Scoping: Cookies can be set to expire after a session or a fixed time, reducing the window for misuse. Scoping to specific domains and paths (e.g., domain=api.example.com , path=/auth ) limits their exposure. Signed Cookies: Frameworks often support signing cookies with a secret key, ensuring they haven’t been tampered with on the client side. This is a typical reponse that uses the Set-Cookies header to instruct the browser to set those cookies HTTP/1.1 200 OK Content-Type: application/json Set-Cookie: session=xyz123; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict; Max-Age=86400; Path=/; Domain=api.example.com When configured correctly, cookies are a fortress for storing session IDs, JWTs, or other authentication tokens in SSR apps. They’re automatically sent by the browser with every request, simplifying server-side validation compared to managing tokens in localStorage or HTTP headers. Axum provides a cool axum-extra crate that makes it easy to work with them. That crate contains a very useful extractor called CookieJar that exposes a very minimal interface to .add and .remove cookies for a user. This is the utility function I use to generate a default cookie pub(crate) fn default_cookie<'a>( key: &str, token: String, duration_hrs: i64 ) -> Cookie<'a> { Cookie::build((key.to_string(), token)) .path("/") .http_only(true) .max_age(Duration::hours(duration_hrs)) .secure(if cfg!(debug_assertions) { // Safari won't allow secure cookies // coming from localhost in debug mode false } else { // Secure cookies in release mode true }) .build() } I won’t get sucked into the session ID vs. JWT argument, but honestly, using JWTs in cookies is a win because you don’t have to fuss with storing session data on the server. Jwt are usually very short-lived, they shouldn’t last for long periods of time and they must be renewed frequently for security purposes. For that reason you usually issue two different cookies: jwt: short-lived token containing information about a user in json format, signed with a secret key so you know you were the one who issued it refresh token: a longer-lived token with which you can request new jwts Now that we’ve covered the cookies and jwt basics, let’s start by implementing a standard login endpoint with which users can be given these two cookies. #[derive(Debug)] struct LoginData { username: String, password: String } pub async fn login( State(app): State, jar: CookieJar, // CookieJar is available in axum_extras Form(LoginData { username, password }): Form ) -> impl IntoResponse { // dummy function to get a user let user = match db::user::get(&app.pg_pool, &username, &password).await { None => return Redirect::to("/signup").into_response() Some(user) => user }; // get/create a refresh token for the user let re

data.title: parrot.live
data.author: jasonthorsness
data.article_summary: "parrot.live" 是一个开源项目，旨在通过使用 `curl` 命令在终端中显示动画 Party 鹦鹉。该项目基于 "terminal-parrot"，用户可以通过输入 `curl parrot.live` 来观看动画。项目感谢了贡献者如 jmhobbs 提供的动画帧以及其他测试和反馈人员。此外，项目还提供了更多鹦鹉相关资源的链接，如 cultofthepartyparrot.com 和 parrotsay。技术上，项目主要使用 JavaScript 和 PowerShell 开发，并在 GitHub 上获得了 3.8k 个星标和 180 个分支。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一个ASCII动画网站在技术社区引发的讨论，包括技术实现、个人项目回顾、技术问题反馈等。

不同观点：
• **项目成就和趣味性**：
   - [hsx] 分享了自己8年前随手搭建的项目，并提到最近才发现有内存泄漏问题，同时指出项目多年来消耗了大量带宽。
   - [oytis] 赞扬了作者的编程能力，称其为“编码机器”。
   - [90s_dev] 回忆了自己制作的类似趣味项目，一个在测试通过后跳出来的彩虹独角兽。
   - [mathewpregasen] 认为这是Hacker News存在的意义，即分享有趣的技术项目。

• **技术细节和实现方式**：
   - [Liftyee] 提到项目带宽使用情况，并对比了安装软件的麻烦和直接显示字符的安全性。
   - [mtekman] 提到了类似的项目smithers.el，扩展了讨论范围。
   - [sandos] 对项目的技术实现表示好奇，询问是否与curl的默认日志记录有关。
   - [jasonthorsness] 解释了如何正确使用curl命令访问该网站。
   - [troupo] 提到了类似的历史技术，如通过telnet观看ASCII版《星球大战》。

• **技术问题和反馈**：
   - [financypants] 提到访问该网站导致自己的ssh会话崩溃。
   - [donbreo] 报告网站无法访问。
   - [Daviey] 提到网站因为访问量过大而崩溃，出现504网关超时错误。

补充讨论：
• **跨平台问题**：
   - [baalimago] 询问该项目是否能在PowerShell上运行，扩展了项目在不同平台上的适用性讨论。

• **用户体验和趣味项目**：
   - [joshdavham] 询问是否有其他类似的项目，显示出对更多趣味技术项目的好奇心。

争议焦点：
• 项目的技术实现和访问问题引发了讨论，部分用户报告了崩溃和无法访问的问题，而其他用户则分享了类似的趣味项目，显示出对项目实现方式的不同理解和技术挑战。

data.article_summary: 本文介绍了用于自动复制签名的Autopen机器，尤其在NASA宇航员中广泛使用。Autopen通过模板 recreate签名，使宇航员能专注于工作而不被签名请求打扰。NASA常用的是Damilic公司生产的Autopen Model 80，通过Plexiglas模板操作，签名区域约为3" x 1"。尽管效率高，但高速运行可能导致签名潦草。不同模板可快速切换，以生成不同人的签名。Apollo时代的Autopen与真人签名仍有区别，如签名突然停止、线宽不一、线条抖动、位置异常等特征，帮助识别。

Identifying Autopens
1. What is an Autopen?
The Autopen machine is a mechanical device used to automatically recreate genuine-looking signatures of a given person. These machines were first developed around the beginning of the 20th century but only became widely used in the last 60 years or so.
Although most people are unaware of their existence, Autopen machines are widely used by government institutions, businesses and celebrities. Certainly all U.S. presidents since Eisenhower have used them at one time or another (JFK was one of the first big users). In the context of this site obviously the most important users are the NASA astronauts, all of whom were (and still are) given access to these machines and encouraged to use them.
The use of Autopens machines is generally justified by the fact that they allow the signee to spend their time on their job rather than signing autographs or routine documents. In the case of NASA there was no way that the Apollo astronauts could have routinely signed all autograph
requests and still done their jobs so NASA had to choose between refusing all requests or sending out Autopenned signatures.
Choosing the latter option probably made a lot of people happy at the time as the vast majority of recipients would have been unaware that the signatures were not genuine. Even some
astronauts unknowingly ended up with Autopen signatures of their fellow astronauts in their own personal collections.
The most common type of autopen machine used by NASA in the early years was the Autopen Model 80, built by the
Damilic Corporation
of Rockville, Md.
The machine (
right
) resembled a small drafting table, with a mechanical writing arm on one side and an open area beside it for stacking signed and unsigned documents.
An Autopen machine works from a template (or signature matrix) which was created by the Autopen company from a copy of the signee's real autograph.
While
modern Autopen machines
work
from digital patterns, the Apollo-era Autopen templates took the form of a large Plexiglas spiral with indentations in the top surface
which was loaded into the machine onto a turntable situated under the desk top, as shown in the photo below.
A pen, pencil or marker was inserted at the end of the mechanical arm and
letters, photographs, certificates or even books caould then be placed under the pen and the signature would be drawn out on the item at the press of a button.
The Model 80 Autopen machine had a writing area roughly 3" across by 1" high, so a template could incorportate short phrases (e.g. "Best Wishes") or symbols (e.g. the Mercury sigma 7 symbol) alongside the actual signature.
Apparently a skilled operator could turn out thousands of signed items a day if necessary using the machine, although it seems that if run at too high a speed the signatures
could become a bit 'sloppy' (showing the shaky lines mentioned in section 2.3).
Templates could be swapped in and out of the machine easily, allowing a single machine to produce the signatures of multiple persons (e.g. an Apollo crew) or to produce varying versions of the same signature.
Future versions of these machines may be produced which mimic the actual handwriting style of a celebrity (including some 'natural' variation) in order to create 'handwritten' and signed letters at will, but luckily for us the
Apollo-era machines, while impressive, did not write in quite the same way as a human.

data.title: Foam: A free Roam alternative for VSCode
data.author: AbuAssar
data.article_summary:
Foam 是一个基于 Visual Studio Code 和 GitHub 的个人知识管理与分享系统，受 Roam Research 启发。它可以帮助用户组织研究、记录可重新发现的笔记、撰写长文，并可选择将内容发布到网络。Foam 是免费开源的，具有高度可扩展性，用户可以完全掌控自己创建的信息，并自由分享与协作。

主要功能包括：
- 图形可视化：通过图形展示笔记间的联系。
- 链接自动补全：帮助创建笔记间的连接。
- 文件重命名时同步链接：保持笔记的一致性。
- 跨目录唯一标识符：支持同名文件在不同目录中存在。
- 链接预览与导航、笔记嵌入、章节支持、链接别名、模板、反向链接面板、标签浏览面板等功能。
- 支持孤立和占位符面板，帮助管理无链接或无内容的笔记。
- 语法高亮、每日笔记、生成 Markdown 引用等。

Foam 提供了多种命令和快捷方式，帮助用户高效管理知识库，并支持通过图形和反向链接发现笔记间的联系。用户可以根据指南创建一个 Foam 工作区，使用 Markdown 文档记录想法，并通过 Wiki 链接进行连接和浏览。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Foam 作为知识管理工具的优缺点及其与其他工具（如 Obsidian、org-roam）的比较

不同观点：
• [sputknick] 认为 Foam 的 VS Code 集成是其最大的优点，但同时也是缺点。因为作者的笔记中只有三分之一与软件开发相关，所以大部分时间使用 VS Code 显得笨重。他认为如果笔记内容几乎全部与软件开发相关，Foam 才是一个理想的选择。

• [metayrnc] 关注 Foam 是否具备类似 Obsidian 中 Dataview 的功能，并表示如果没有此类功能，会犹豫是否切换到 Foam。这表明用户对数据管理和查询功能的需求是切换工具时的重要考虑因素。

• [fouc] 引用了 Foam 的定义，强调其作为基于 VS Code 的知识管理和分享系统，灵感来源于 Roam Research。这表明该用户可能在简单描述工具的核心特性，而不带有明显的立场。

• [mtzaldo] 提出了一个技术趋势相关的问题，将 VS Code 和 Electron 进行类比，暗示 Foam 的依赖 VS Code 可能带来类似 Electron 应用的缺点（如资源占用高、笨重等）。这反映了一些用户对 Foam 依赖特定编辑器的潜在担忧。

• [senkora] 提到了 org-roam，这是一个基于 Emacs 和 org-mode 的类似工具，并提供了相关链接。该用户暗示 org-roam 可能是 Foam 的替代选项，特别是对于 Emacs 用户。这指向了不同工具之间的用户偏好和生态系统选择。

补充讨论：
• Foam 的 VS Code 集成特性在用户中引起了不同反应，部分用户认为它对非开发相关的笔记管理不够灵活。
• 用户对工具的数据管理功能（如 Obsidian 的 Dataview）有需求，这可能影响他们是否会选择切换到 Foam。
• 不同的知识管理工具（如 Foam、Obsidian、org-roam）之间的功能对比和用户生态是讨论的另一个焦点。
• 一些用户对 Foam 依赖 VS Code 持保留态度，认为这可能限制其广泛应用。

Foam
👀
This is an early stage project under rapid development. For updates join the
Foam community Discord
! 💬
Foam
is a personal knowledge management and sharing system inspired by
Roam Research
, built on
Visual Studio Code
and
GitHub
.
You can use
Foam
for organising your research, keeping re-discoverable notes, writing long-form content and, optionally, publishing it to the web.
Foam
is free, open source, and extremely extensible to suit your personal workflow. You own the information you create with Foam, and you're free to share it, and collaborate on it with anyone you want.
Features
Graph Visualization
See how your notes are connected via a
graph
with the
Foam: Show Graph
command.
Link Autocompletion
Foam helps you create the connections between your notes, and your placeholders as well.
Sync links on file rename
Foam updates the links to renamed files, so your notes stay consistent.
Unique identifiers across directories
Foam supports files with the same name in multiple directories.
It will use the minimum identifier required, and even report and help you fix existing ambiguous wikilinks.
Link Preview and Navigation
Go to definition, Peek References
See where a note is being referenced in your knowledge base.
Navigation in Preview
Navigate your rendered notes in the VS Code preview panel.
Note embed
Embed the content from other notes.
Support for sections
Foam supports autocompletion, navigation, embedding and diagnostics for note sections.
Just use the standard wiki syntax of
[[resource#Section Title]]
.
Link Alias
Foam supports link aliasing, so you can have a
[[wikilink]]
, or a
[[wikilink|alias]]
.
Templates
Use
custom templates
to have avoid repetitve work on your notes.
Backlinks Panel
Quickly check which notes are referencing the currently active note.
See for each occurrence the context in which it lives, as well as a preview of the note.
Tag Explorer Panel
Tag your notes and navigate them with the
Tag Explorer
.
Foam also supports hierarchical tags.
Orphans and Placeholder Panels
Orphans are notes that have no inbound nor outbound links.
Placeholders are dangling links, or notes without content.
Keep them under control, and your knowledge base in a better state, by using this panel.
Syntax highlight
Foam highlights wikilinks and placeholder differently, to help you visualize your knowledge base.
Daily note
Create a journal with
daily notes
.
Generate references for your wikilinks
Create markdown
references
for
[[wikilinks]]
, to use your notes in a non-Foam workspace.
With references you can also make your notes navigable both in GitHub UI as well as GitHub Pages.
Commands
Explore your knowledge base with the
Foam: Open Random Note
command
Access your daily note with the
Foam: Open Daily Note
command
Create a new note with the
Foam: Create New Note
command
This becomes very powerful when combined with
note templates
and the
Foam: Create New Note from Template
command
See your workspace as a connected graph with the
Foam: Show Graph
command
Recipes
People use Foam in different ways for different use cases, check out the
recipes
page for inspiration!
Getting started
Whether you want to build a
Second Brain
or a
Zettelkasten
, write a book, or just get better at long-term learning,
Foam
can help you organise your thoughts if you follow these simple rules:
Create a single
Foam
workspace for all your knowledge and research following the [[Getting started]] guide.
Write your thoughts in markdown documents (I like to call them
Bubbles
, but that might be more than a little twee). These documents should be atomic: Put things that belong together into a single document, and limit its content to that single topic. (
source
)
Use Foam's shortcuts and autocompletions to link your thoughts together with
[[wikilinks]]
, and navigate between them to explore your knowledge graph.
Get an overview of your
Foam
workspace using the [[Graph Visualisation]], and discover relationships between your thoughts with the use of [
Backlinking
].

data.title: Dr. Sbaitso
data.author: bovermyer
data.article_summary: 《Dr. Sbaitso》是1991年由Creative Labs发布的早期人工智能程序，运行于MS-DOS系统，模拟心理治疗对话，让用户与虚拟心理医生互动。该程序通过文本界面与用户交流，依据输入内容作出预设回应，类似于心理咨询，尽管简单，但展示了早期AI的潜力。其直观的键盘和鼠标操作以及全屏模式为用户提供了友好的体验。《Dr. Sbaitso》作为AI发展的重要里程碑，展示了AI在个性化用户体验方面的潜力，并激发了公众对人工智能技术的兴趣，为现代聊天机器人奠定了基础。该程序不仅是怀旧的经典，也代表了人机互动领域的早期创新。
