data.author: beardyw
data.article_summary: 根据Accenture的研究，英国科技职位空缺增加了21%，达到疫情前的高峰，尤其在人工智能（AI）领域需求激增，AI相关职位需求同比增长近200%。伦敦占据了全国AI职位发布的80%，而近三分之二的科技职位空缺也在伦敦。尽管有169万人自称具备科技技能，但区域间AI技能提升的差距引发对数字鸿沟的担忧。伦敦公司计划将五分之一的科技预算用于AI，而其他地区如英格兰东北部、苏格兰和威尔士的投入较少。PwC的研究显示，AI应用较多的行业，如软件行业，实现了更高的生产率和工资增长。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：英国技术岗位的就业市场情况，特别是薪资水平和就业机会的质量。

不同观点：
• [tetris11] 认为虽然开放的岗位在增加，但薪资和长期合同并没有相应增长。他指出，同样的职位会在LinkedIn上反复出现，可能是虚假的招聘信息，或者这些工作变成了临时合同。对于入门级技术人员来说，职位要求仍然很高，求职者可能需要夸大自己的能力或接受降薪才能获得工作。

• [rgavuliak] 同意英国的技术岗位薪资较低，尤其是在伦敦的公司，考虑到生活成本后，薪资显得更加不理想。

• [jpgvm] 指出英国拥有深厚的AI和数学人才储备，以及大量的硬件和FPGA人才。他认为相对于湾区的薪资水平，更多AI专注的公司应该在伦敦设立卫星办公室，但目前这种情况并不多见。

• [dyl000] 则认为英国的技术岗位市场相对美国要好得多，并表示美国的情况更糟糕，对美国的求职者表示同情。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于英国技术岗位市场的真实状况，特别是薪资水平和就业机会的质量。一些评论者（如[tetris11]和[rgavuliak]）认为薪资较低且合同不稳定，而另一些评论者（如[jpgvm]和[dyl000]）则认为英国市场拥有良好的发展潜力和相对较好的就业机会。

• 对于入门级技术人员来说，职位要求高和薪资不匹配是一个主要问题，这使得新进入市场的求职者面临更大的挑战。

• 讨论还涉及国际比较，特别是与美国和湾区的比较，表明英国技术岗位市场的表现可能在国际背景下有不同的评价。

44190120.article_content:
AI + ML
2
UK tech job openings climb 21% to pre-pandemic highs
2
Accenture points to AI hiring spree, with London dominating demand
Lindsay Clark
Thu 5 Jun 2025
//
09:48 UTC
UK tech vacancies are up by 21 percent to hit their highest levels since before the pandemic, according to research from Accenture.
... regions outside of London will also need to compete for talent and infrastructure
The global consultancy found a surge in demand for AI skills, which increased nearly 200 percent in a year. London accounted for 80 percent of AI-related job postings across the UK, while nearly two-thirds of technology vacancies as a whole were in London.
Accenture collected data from LinkedIn in the first and second week of February 2025, and supplemented the results with a survey of more than 4,000 respondents conducted by research firm YouGov between July and August 2024.
The research found a 53 percent annual increase in those describing themselves as having tech skills, amounting to 1.69 million people reporting skills in disciplines including cyber, data, and robotics.
Accenture tech lead Emma Kendrew commented: "The UK has a golden opportunity to establish itself as a global AI leader, and London is at the epicenter. The UK is seeing hotspots of tech talent emerge which we expect to grow as AI is more widely adopted.
"However, to fully capitalize on the economic potential of AI, regions outside of London will also need to compete for talent and infrastructure to achieve sustainable growth and unlock opportunities. The disparity in regional upskilling in AI raises concerns about a growing digital divide in the UK and could hurt long-term competitiveness."
AI hype fuels pay rise – but only if you're in the right gig
What will UK government workers do with an extra 26 minutes a day?
Best pricing model for AI? Work in progress, says Salesforce
Barclays Bank signs 100k license Copilot deal with Microsoft
The research found that London-based companies said they would allocate a fifth of their tech budgets to AI this year, compared to 13 percent who said the same and were based in North East England, Scotland, and Wales.
Earlier this week,
research by rival consultancy PwC
found that sectors where AI can be readily used for some tasks – including the software industry – are achieving higher productivity and wage growth than others.
Growth in revenue per employee increased during the period when LLMs emerged, from 7 percent annually between 2018 and 2022 to 27 percent between 2018 and 2024. Meanwhile, growth in the same measure fell slightly in industries less affected by AI, such as mining and hospitality, the researchers said. ®

data.title: Changing Directions
data.author: speckx
data.article_summary: 作者宣布将离开科技行业，并调整其博客的内容方向。他对科技行业的幻想破灭，感到精疲力竭，决定转向其他兴趣领域，如农场项目、野外探险和急救医学。作者强调，这一决定是个人选择，不批评其他选择留在科技行业的人。虽然不再全职从事科技工作，但作者计划继续参与Django社区和有限度的顾问工作。未来，他将接受急救员培训并参与搜救志愿工作，可能进一步成为 paramedic。博客内容将不再局限于科技，而会涵盖更多个人兴趣和经历，给予作者更大的写作自由。读者可自行选择是否继续关注。

• xwowsersx对科技行业的全盘否定提出异议。他认为科技行业虽然存在问题，如“监控资本主义”和剥削性的零工经济模式，但也带来了许多积极的变化，如免费教育、加速医学突破、连接偏远地区的人群等。他主张应看到科技的全面影响，而不是只关注其负面。

• roenxi指出，将工作与道德挂钩会导致失望，因为经济系统优化的是物质结果，而非道德结果。他建议寻找一种道德原则，以避免在工作中感到道德困境。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于科技行业的本质及其社会影响。一些人认为科技带来了许多负面影响，如监控资本主义和剥削性经济模式，而另一些人则强调其积极贡献和潜在的社会益处。

• 职业倦怠和对职业的重新评估是另一个重要主题。不同评论者分享了应对倦怠的策略，如减少行业参与、制作个人作品、参与社区服务等。

• 对紧急医疗服务行业的看法也存在分歧，一些人强调其 rewarding 的一面，而另一些人则指出其面临的挫折和挑战。

44172659.article_content:
Changing Directions
I have two important announcements:
I’m leaving the tech industry. Hopefully “for good”; if not, at least “for now”.
As such, the content on this blog is going to shift, perhaps dramatically. I’m going to be writing about a broader range of topics that interest me (projects around my hobby farm, wilderness trips, emergency medicine) – more writing for
me
, less writing for some imagined audience. (I’ll probably still end up writing about some of the same topics as I’ve been covering since 2020, just less often.)
I’m writing this post mostly to give myself permission to make that change, and to give readers the opportunity to unsubscribe/unfollow if they’re not interested.
If you’re interested in more details about why I’m leaving the industry and what’s next for me and this blog, read on.
Leaving the tech industry
I left what I hope will be my last tech job in October. In many ways it was the perfect job: work I enjoyed, great clients, co-workers I loved (and still miss), at a company whose mission and ethics I aligned with. And despite all that I found myself increasingly burnt out. I started telling people that “I love my job, but I hate my career.”
I’ve been working in tech more or less non-stop for more than 25 years, and in that time my feeling about the industry has changed dramatically. When I began, I held straightforwardly techno-utopian ideas: I believed that technology was an unalloyed force for Good, that the computer revolution would bring about a more just and equitable society. I thought the industry was going to create a Star Trek-esque post-scarcity society.
I cringe at past-Jacob’s naiveté. It’s been incredibly demoralizing to discover what the tech industry actually did was to invent surveillance capitalism, create exploitative “gig economy” business models, create a new generation of robber barons, enable the rise of global fascism,
facilitate genocide
, and I could go on but Christ I’m exhausted.
I’ve been thinking about leaving the industry since at least 2016, but haven’t been brave enough to do so. This career pays really well for easy work (physically, at least), and it’s all I’m good at. Doing something different is terrifying. But I’m able to afford a change in direction, despite the massive pay cut, so I’m doing it.
I want to be super-clear about this:
I’m in no way criticizing anyone who makes a different decision
. Leaving a good tech career is a
terrible
financial decision, and I absolutely won’t criticize people who’re unable or unwilling to make such a bad decision. This is about
me
: I’m able to make this move, so I’m going to. There’s no judgement of anyone else here, explicit or implied.
I still find computers themselves incredibly exciting. When I first learn to program, being able to make a computer do whatever I wanted felt like a superpower – and it still does! I’m not planning a total exit from anything computer related; I don’t think I could. I plan on continuing to be involved in the Django community and with the Django Software Foundation. I’m continuing on as an advisor to a couple of small companies I’ve been working with (with a change: I’ll step down if/when those companies do a traditional VC raise). I’m remaining open to limited advising/consulting work – though, I’m going to be pretty picky about who it’s for. And I’m sure I’ll always write software, it’s just too fun and useful a skill.
My plan is to go into emergency medicine: I’ll be training as an EMT this fall, and I’m starting to volunteer with our local county Search and Rescue team. I plan to work as a EMT for a year or so, and then perhaps work towards becoming a Paramedic.
I don’t know if this’ll work out. It might not. But I’m giving it a shot.
Changing the focus of my writing
I’ve been writing here since 2005. At first, this was a typical early-2000s personal blog: I wrote whatever I wanted – technical posts, recipes, live updates, whatever. Then there a long fallow period starting around 2010 when I wrote sporadically, just a few posts a year.
In 2020 I rebooted the blog, with a very specific editorial focus: tech leadership, focused on software engineering and security. I wrote with a fairly specific audience in mind: engineering managers and technical leads, working in software development and information security. Mostly the theme was: things I wish someone had told me before I messed it all up. I put a concerted effort into building an audience for this content, and I think I’ve been pretty successful at it. I’m happy with the results, at least. I’m sure I’ll keep writing about these topics – I remain fascinated by risk decisions, and will almost certainly continue my
Thinking About Risk
series.
But as I step away from tech, I find the things I’ve been writing about since 2020 less and less interesting. I’ve been wanting to write about a broader range of topics for well over a year, but have felt constrained by my own editorial choices. So a large part of writing this po

• 对紧急医疗服务行业的看法也存在分歧，一些人强调其 rewarding 的一面，而另一些人则指出其面临的挫折和挑战。

data.title: Twitter's new encrypted DMs aren't better than the old ones
data.author: tabletcorry
data.article_summary: 本文提到用户在进行某些请求时被随机选中需要完成CAPTCHA验证。页面提供了一个登录表单，包括账户名、密码输入框以及"记住我"选项。此外，还有找回密码和使用OpenID登录的替代选项。用户需先完成CAPTCHA验证才能继续。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：新推出的加密聊天功能及其安全性、技术实现和与历史技术（如Signal、Bitcoin）的关系

不同观点：
• [tptacek] 认为Signal在推进现代安全消息传递实践方面起到了重要作用，尤其是前向安全性（forward secrecy）和可否认性（repudiability）。他对当前一些新推出的消息系统表示不满，认为它们在安全性上倒退到了2001年之前的水平。
• [b0a04gl] 质疑所谓的“比特币风格加密”究竟是什么，尤其是当该系统不具备前向安全性和交互记录时，如何能与比特币的加密技术相提并论。
• [zzo38computer] 主张使用独立的加密软件，并通过面对面获取公钥，认为这种方式比依赖现有社交平台的加密方案更安全。
• [diggan] 进一步探讨“比特币风格加密”的定义，指出比特币主要依赖于加密签名，而非通常意义上的加密，质疑该术语的使用是否准确。
• [yndoendo] 从法律角度提出问题，询问如果XChat与X-Twitter之间存在名称侵权问题，是否可以提起诉讼。
• [pityJuke] 引用了一个实验性库的自述文件，指出该库尽管是Libsodium的包装，但仍可能引入新的攻击面和问题，因此不应在生产环境中使用，直到社区对其进行审查。
• [romaaeterna] 担心Signal通过更新推送新二进制文件，可能存在收集用户信息的风险，质疑其安全性。
• [baby] 对加密功能不太关心，更希望聊天功能本身能够改进。
• [lenerdenator] 对Twitter等社交媒体平台的信任度极低，认为这些平台本质上是为了数据收集，且无法审计其代码库，假设所有通过这些平台发送的信息都是不安全的。此外，还对Twitter的运营现状和环境进行了批评。
• [1oooqooq] 质疑为何人们继续使用旧名称给新平台赋予正面评价。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是“比特币风格加密”这一术语的准确性和实际意义。
• 另一个争议点是新推出的加密聊天系统是否真的具备前向安全性以及是否比现有的安全消息系统（如Signal）更落后。
• 讨论中还涉及到对特定平台（如Twitter）的不信任，以及对整个社交媒体生态系统的批评。

data.title: The impossible predicament of the death newts
data.author: bdr
data.article_summary:
这篇文章介绍了世界上最毒的蝾螈——粗糙皮肤蝾螈（*Taricha granulosa*），它生活于北美太平洋西北地区，其毒素足以杀死多个成年人。尽管这种蝾螈有剧毒，但它是“有毒”而非“有毒液”，只要接触后彻底洗手，就不会有危险。

这种蝾螈的剧毒源于与食虫蛇（*Thamnophis sirtalis*）之间的进化军备竞赛。蛇逐渐进化出对河豚毒素（tetrodotoxin）的抵抗力，而蝾螈则进化得更具毒性，形成反馈循环。然而，这种毒性也给蝾螈带来了代谢负担，而蛇的抵抗力进化也有代价，可能影响其神经系统。

尽管食虫蛇对毒素有抵抗力，进食这些蝾螈仍会让它们不适，但蛇仍坚持捕食蝾螈，因为它们能将毒素储存在肝脏中，作为防御天敌的手段。因此，蛇更倾向于捕食有毒蝾螈，以维持自身毒性防御。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕蛇对河豚毒素抵抗力的进化成本及相关自然选择机制的讨论，以及对蛇与蝾螈之间捕食关系的探讨。

不同观点：
• arp242认为，进化出对河豚毒素的抵抗力可能有代价，否则更多生物会进化出这种特性。然而，自然选择没有预见性，仅根据繁殖需求运作，许多动物因为没有面临毒素威胁，所以没有进化出抵抗力的必要，例如大多数区域的蛇。同时，arp242质疑这种抵抗力是否真的存在进化成本。
• k__幽默地提到一种危险植物（水百合），尽管这与主话题无直接关联，但引发了对自然界其他潜在威胁的讨论。
• atentaten对蛇如何识别蝾螈毒性强弱提出疑问，质疑蛇是否会挑选猎物，还是随机捕食，以及强毒蝾螈是否能在蛇的捕食中存活。这涉及到捕食者与猎物之间的进化“军备竞赛”。
• jakey_bakey和UncleOxidant对蛇存储河豚毒素在肝脏中的防御机制展开讨论。jakey_bakey认为这种二阶效应非常有趣，而UncleOxidant则质疑这种机制的即时性和有效性，因为相比蝾螈皮肤上的毒素，肝脏中的毒素无法在捕食过程中直接起到威慑作用。

补充讨论：
• 部分评论如ryukoposting和ednite偏离了主要讨论点，转而谈论与文章标题、内容相关的个人感受或联想，如蛇的颜色和文学作品中的蝾螈形象。
• 链接分享如alkyon和onlypassingthru提供了与文章相关的扩展阅读材料，丰富了讨论内容。
• titanomachy和rufus_foreman基于个人经验对蝾螈毒性的实际影响提出看法，认为人类遭遇剧毒蝾螈的情况罕见，且在日常生活中这些生物相对无害。
• steve_adams_86分享了自己儿时接触这些生物的经历，增添了对野生动物保护和饲养的个人视角。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于蛇进化出抵抗河豚毒素的潜在代价及其防御机制的有效性。一方面，arp242和UncleOxidant质疑这种进化是否有明确的代价或劣势；另一方面，jakey_bakey等人则对蛇的毒素存储机制表现出兴趣，认为其具有独特的生态意义。

总结：讨论围绕蛇与蝾螈之间的捕食与反捕食进化展开，涉及到自然选择的运作机制、毒素抵抗力的潜在代价以及具体防御机制的有效性。部分评论也提供了个人经验和额外信息，扩展了话题的广度。

44191620.article_content:
So a few days ago I
posted about newts
, and I mentioned that there was an American newt that was ridiculously toxic. But then (I said) there wasn’t space or time to go into why.  And of course I was immediately bombarded by many* comments and e-mails asking why.
*three
Well, fine.  The world’s most toxic newt is
Taricha granulosa
, the Rough-Skinned Newt, a modest little amphibian native to the North American Pacific Northwest, west of the Cascades from around Santa Cruz, CA up to the Alaska Panhandle.
It’s so toxic that the poison from a single newt can easily kill several adult humans. You could literally die from licking this newt, just once.
(But note that the newt is toxic, not venomous. It doesn’t bite or sting. You could handle one safely, as long as you washed your hands thoroughly afterwards. Very, very thoroughly.)
Okay, but… why?  Lots of newts are mildly toxic.  Why is this particularly newt so
extremely
toxic?
Turns out this is a fairly deep rabbit hole!  I’ll try to teal deer it.
The simple version: the newt is in an arms race with the common garter snake,
Thamnophis sirtalis
.  The garter snake is a small-to-medium sized snake that is common all over North America.  It’s a slim, elegant little creature that is usually found in or near water.  And while it will eat pretty much anything it can catch, the garter snake particularly likes amphibians: small frogs, salamanders and newts.  And in the Pacific Northwest, it
really
likes snacking on the Rough-Skinned Newt.
So the garter snakes of the Pacific Northwest have been evolving resistance to tetrodotoxin.  (As you may recall, tetrodotoxin is the stuff that
makes the blue-ringed octopus so deadly
.  It’s produced by symbiotic bacteria that live in the newt’s body, mostly on its skin.)  And as the garter snakes evolve resistance, the newts have to evolve ever greater toxicity.  And as the newts get more toxic… right.  Feedback loop!  That’s the simple version.
Except this is biology, so of course it’s not that simple.
One thing to keep in mind is that nothing in nature is free. The newt’s toxicity comes with a cost: the metabolic load of supporting all those bacteria.  More toxicity means more bacteria means more load.  A very toxic newt has to consume more calories than its less-toxic cousin.
Meanwhile, evolving resistance also comes at a cost.  We don’t know that directly, but we can infer it pretty well.  If resistance to tetrodotoxin were cheap and easy, everything would evolve it.
There have actually been attempts to measure the effect on the snakes!  They haven’t found them, but keep in mind that tetrodotoxin is a neurotoxin.  To resist it, you have to make changes to the biochemistry of your nervous system.  Even a small snake has a very very complex nervous system, where those changes might show up in ways that are hard to measure.  Like, if the resistant snakes were clumsier or had slower reflexes, sure, we could see that.  But maybe they’re suffering from much more subtle neurological effects, like being prone to insomnia or hallucinations or sexual dysfunction.  Or maybe they’re just a bit dim.
We don’t know, but we’re pretty sure there must be something.   We know that
garter snakes outside of the Pacific Northwest are much less resistant to tetrodotoxin
.  They’ll drop dead from doses that their Oregon cousins simply ignore.  So evolving the resistance must have some cost or drawback.
(Note that this means the newt is double-whammied:  not only does it suffer the metabolic load of carrying around all those bacteria, but it also has to evolve resistance to tetrodotoxin, accepting whatever negative effects that brings.  And things are only going to get worse.)
Now: when the snakes eat Rough-Skinned Newts, they may sometimes show signs of discomfort. The snake may visibly gag.  It may writhe in obvious unease.  In some cases, it may go into respiratory distress.  Eating the newt looks pretty unpleasant.  Yet the snakes persist.
Okay then — if evolving toxin resistance carries a cost, and if
even with resistance
eating the newts is unpleasant, then why then do garter snakes insist on eating newts?  They cheerfully eat frogs, fish, and other non-toxic prey items.  Why don’t they just eat those, and leave the poor newts alone?
Turns out there is an answer:
the garter snakes sequester the tetrodotoxin
, storing it in their livers.  This makes them toxic to their own predators.  (Of which there are plenty.  They’re not large snakes, so they’re hunted by everything from raccoons to ravens.)  But they don’t harbor the bacteria, so they don’t produce tetrodotoxin of their own. So eventually, the toxin that they’ve ingested breaks down.  And then they need to eat another newt to refresh their defense.
(If you are That Guy:  now you can name a snake that is poisonous without being venomous.)
So this explains why the snakes go after the newts particularly, preferring them to less toxic prey.  They
want
to eat toxic newts.  And it explains why the

data.title: Experimenting with no-build Web Applications
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary:
文章介绍了作者重构其电子书生成工具 "Little Webby Press" 的过程和原因。最初的版本使用了Svelte 3、BrowserFS等技术，但由于作者对当前前端开发工具链（如转译、框架和依赖）的不满，决定重写该工具以去除构建步骤，实现“所写即所运行”的目标。

新版本采用Mithril替代Svelte，移除了BrowserFS和复杂的CSS框架，改用Pico CSS。代码更加简洁，所有依赖通过importMap从JsDelivr获取，以复用原有的书稿和网站生成逻辑。该应用无需构建步骤，直接在浏览器中运行，通过GitHub Pages部署。

书稿生成过程通过拖放文件夹或按钮触发，生成EPUB和网站的逻辑类似，都是基于Handlebars模板和JsZip打包。配置文件采用TOML格式，用户还可以自定义模板用于生成。最终输出为ZIP文件，包含生成的电子书和网站。

整个项目旨在简化开发流程，去除不必要的复杂性，让工具更易用和直观。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于无构建步骤的Web应用程序开发方式及其优劣的讨论

不同观点：
• **wackget的观点**：认为现代文章对Web开发的描述令人困惑，传统Web开发不需要构建步骤，直接使用HTML、CSS、JavaScript即可完成开发。使用框架只会增加学习曲线和认知负担。作为有20年经验的开发者，他一直使用基础的Web技术构建应用。

• **bob1029的观点**：强调尽量避免使用JavaScript，只有在HTML和CSS无法满足需求时才使用。他提倡服务端渲染，并批评NPM/Node带来的复杂性，特别是对于非DOM环境的使用。他建议尝试零JavaScript项目，看看仅使用HTML和CSS能走多远。

• **hu3的观点**：支持无构建和无编译工具的开发方式，使用PHP、Bun、Go等工具实现快速反馈。他开发了自定义单元测试库以提高效率，并通过声音反馈减少视觉负担，从而降低认知负荷。这种方法受到其他开发者的积极反馈。

• **rcarmo的观点**：赞同尽量减少使用npm和构建工具，偏好直接使用普通的JavaScript文件。如果需要外部库，他会优先选择可以直接从CDN获取的资源。

• **velomash的观点**：指出许多开发者因为热爱编码而对AI辅助开发感到不满，认为重写能带来乐趣。他个人享受编码过程，同时也在学习如何在保证质量的前提下利用AI辅助工具。

• **seanw265的观点**：对使用导入地图（import maps）提出 caution，指出其在实践中可能带来的问题，包括包的兼容性、广告拦截器的干扰以及不同CDN之间的兼容性问题。他建议在使用时要固定版本，并注意生态系统的脆弱性。

• **mozanunal的观点**：讨论了现代前端开发的复杂性和变化，提出了“无构建客户端岛屿”的开发方法，旨在减少对快速变化的生态系统的依赖，使用小型稳定的库和原生ES模块，实现无构建步骤的开发方式。

补充讨论：
• **christophilus和jslakro的评论**：属于个别项目和工具推荐，没有直接参与主要讨论，但反映了开发者在项目中寻找合适工具的过程。

• **sirjaz的建议**：提出将Web应用打包为桌面应用的想法，属于对开发方式的另一种扩展思考。

• **mock-possum的观点**：表示只有在工作需要时才会使用有构建步骤的工具链，个人项目中偏好简单的拖放HTML文件直接运行的方式，呼应了其他开发者对简化开发流程的偏好。

• 是否需要使用现代框架和构建工具，以及JavaScript在Web开发中的必要性和适用范围。

44190371.article_content:
Experimenting with no-build Web Applications
Some years ago I build an eBook generator called
Little Webby Press
. It would pick a folder with
Markdown
files and turn them into an EPUB3 non-DRM eBook file and also a zip containing a static website for your book.
The cool thing about Little Webby Press is that all the workflow happens on the client-side. There's no back end, no database, no user accounts. You drag and drop a folder, press a button, and it works.
I used it to make some niche technical books in the past and since I don't keep analytics, I have no idea how many people have used it.
Old version of LWP.
I spent the recent years without writing any book, but recently, after developing
BlogCat
and writing
The Web Should Be A Conversation
, I have an itch to write a book about
WebExtensions
. Of course, I'd like to use my own eBook generator to write this book, and that is how I nerdsnipped myself into making a new eBook generator.
There was nothing wrong with the old version of Little Webby Press. It was built by leveraging the following stack:
Svelte 3 for the UI.
BrowserFS to have a browser-side filesystem so I could leverage NodeJS file handling routines.
Handlebars for the templates used by both eBook and website generation.
JsZip to create the EPUB and the zip containing the website.
Rollup and a gazillion plugins
Taildwind and Daisy for CSS
All in all a very common setup for like five years ago. The problem is that I don't like the current version of Svelte and I really dislike the current web development ecosystem with its reliance on transpilation and too many frameworks and dependencies and build steps. Feels like we're developing in a fantasy version of JS that no engine is really able to run. I hate that.
So instead of writing the book I want to write, I decided to rewrite Little Webby Press in a stack that is more suitable to my own enjoyment.
New LWP.
The new Little Webby Press
My main objective with the new version was to eliminate the build step. I wanted a no-build system in which the JS I write is exactly what runs on the browser.
Instead of implementing everything from scratch, I kept many of the NodeJS-based dependencies but used an
importMap
to get them from
JsDelivr
. This was done so I could reuse the majority of the book and website generation code.
Don't want to read this blog post, you can go check
the source code
.
I switched from Svelte to
Mithril
â which is my favourite JS lib to make UIs â and completely removed BrowserFS. Instead I created my own
file handling routines
which have the same arguments as the NodeJS ones but different names. Instead of a full-blown filesystem implementation, it is just an object where the keys are the paths and the property content is the file content. Can't be any more naive than that.
I also removed all the CSS stuff and just replaced it with
Pico CSS
.
LWP showing the information about Moby Dick.
The code became a lot smaller than the previous version and what is written is exactly what the browser runs. There's no JSX, no Svelte templates, no JS features that the browser doesn't understand.
The repository is the actual app that is run, Github Pages is just set to serve from the root of the repo. Any change there is a new deployment, no github actions, no scripts to run.
It is so refreshing.
Press play to it in action.
How does it actually work
It is a simple Mithril application with a router in
app.js
and three routes. One for the book generation app, one for the documentation, and one for a simple about.
The book generation needs a source folder. You can either drag and drop a folder, or, use the
Load manuscript folder
button. That will trigger a routine that will read all files in that folder and create a gigantic object with all the paths and contents.
Both the ebook and the website generation functions are massive waterfalls (don't we all think that waterfalls are beautiful?) that make multiple loops over all the files assembling a resulting file tree by copying things around and using handlebars to generate HTML and other files.
Once the resulting file tree is ready, it is added to zip file using
JsZip
and that file is downloaded from the browser into the downloads folder.
EPUBs are zip files. So both the ebook and the website generation are almost the same waterfall but using different templates.
The output can be configured with a
TOML control file
that has a ton of features and switches.
Both documentation books for Little Webby Press were generated with Little Webby Press, check out
Getting Started
and
Book Configuration Specification
.
The templates used are in a zip file that is loaded when the application loads. They contents of that zip file are placed in the same enourmous object with a
/templates/
prefix for the prop name (remember we're mimicking a filesystem).
Because the template is loaded via XHR that means that someone wanting to generate a book and a website can actually use their own template as well by creati
44190371.article_summary:
文章介绍了作者重构其电子书生成工具 "Little Webby Press" 的过程和原因。最初的版本使用了Svelte 3、BrowserFS等技术，但由于作者对当前前端开发工具链（如转译、框架和依赖）的不满，决定重写该工具以去除构建步骤，实现“所写即所运行”的目标。

新版本采用Mithril替代Svelte，移除了BrowserFS和复杂的CSS框架，改用Pico CSS。代码更加简洁，所有依赖通过importMap从JsDelivr获取，以复用原有的书稿和网站生成逻辑。该应用无需构建步骤，直接在浏览器中运行，通过GitHub Pages部署。

书稿生成过程通过拖放文件夹或按钮触发，生成EPUB和网站的逻辑类似，都是基于Handlebars模板和JsZip打包。配置文件采用TOML格式，用户还可以自定义模板用于生成。最终输出为ZIP文件，包含生成的电子书和网站。

整个项目旨在简化开发流程，去除不必要的复杂性，让工具更易用和直观。

data.title: Apple Notes Will Gain Markdown Export at WWDC, and, I Have Thoughts
data.author: robenkleene
data.article_summary: John Gruber评论了9to5Mac关于Apple Notes将增加Markdown导出功能的报道。他指出，虽然这一功能对技术爱好者来说很有吸引力，但他不希望Apple Notes变成一个“Markdown编辑器”。Gruber强调，Markdown最初是为了web写作和简化HTML标记设计的，而Apple Notes的优势在于其简洁的富文本编辑界面和有限的格式选项。他支持Markdown导出功能，因为这可以方便地将笔记转换为更通用的格式，但不应让Apple Notes完全变成Markdown应用，以免出现格式错误。同时，他对Apple Notes当前导出功能的简陋表示不满，期待改进。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Apple Notes 应用即将支持 Markdown 导出的功能，涉及 Markdown 的优缺点、应用场景以及技术实现的讨论。

不同观点：
• **Markdown 的优势**：[dotdi] 认为，Markdown 作为纯文本格式，有助于避免供应商锁定，并减少专有格式带来的问题，尤其在开源应用中非常有价值。即使 Markdown 有不足之处，它的广泛使用仍有助于数据的可移植性。
• **Apple Messages 中的应用场景**：[Eric_WVGG] 提到，希望在 Apple Messages 中使用 Markdown，特别是用 `backticks` 包裹链接，以防止自动生成的大图形破坏信息的表达。
• **与 LaTeX 的对比**：[bee_rider] 质疑为何要导出为 Markdown，而不是更专业的格式如 LaTeX。他认为在导出场景下，Markdown 的优势并不明显，因为计算机可以轻松处理复杂的语法。
• **UI/UX 的不确定性**：[diggan] 认为，在尚未了解 Markdown 支持的具体实现（如是否为完整的 WYSIWYG 编辑器）之前，过早发表意见是不明智的。他指出，目前传闻仅提及 "导出为 Markdown" 功能。
• **对专有格式的困扰**：[mcdow] 表达了对 Apple Notes 目前使用的专有格式的困扰，并期待通过 Markdown 支持来解决数据迁移问题。

补充讨论：
• **其他应用的期待**：[anentropic] 希望 Microsoft OneNote 也能支持 Markdown，表明 Markdown 的需求不仅限于 Apple 生态。
• **LLM 的影响**：[perbu] 提到，Markdown 是大语言模型的原生格式，未来几年其支持将无处不在，暗示 LLMs 可能是推动这一功能需求的主要因素。
• **技术细节与用户体验问题**：[nonethewiser] 提到 Apple Notes 的缩进问题，表明在实际使用中，WYSIWYG 编辑器有时不如 Markdown 直观，特别是对熟悉 Markdown 的用户而言。

争议焦点：
• **Markdown 是否适合作为导出格式**：部分用户如 [bee_rider] 认为在导出场景下，Markdown 并不是最佳选择，而应选择更专业的格式如 LaTeX。
• **具体实现方式的未知**：[diggan] 指出，目前关于 Markdown 支持的具体 UI/UX 实现尚不明确，讨论的某些内容可能基于不准确的假设。

总的来说，讨论围绕 Markdown 的优缺点、应用场景、技术实现以及其在不同应用中的需求展开。

By
John Gruber
Archive

Dithering
Projects
Contact
Colophon
Feeds / Social

WorkOS
: Scalable, secure authentication, trusted by OpenAI, Cursor, Perplexity, and Vercel.
9to5Mac Reports Apple Notes Will Gain Markdown Export at WWDC, and, You’ll Be Unsurprised to Know, I Have Thoughts
Marcus Mendes, in a piece at 9to5Mac with multiple spoilers for next week’s keynote:
Apple is working on supporting the ability to export notes in
Markdown from Apple Notes, which is something third-party apps
have supported for years. Granted, this is a niche feature, but as
a fierce participant in the niche, I can confirm: this is huge.
When this story first started spreading this morning, it was getting repeated as Notes “gaining Markdown support”, which implied something like
Bear
or
Obsidian
, where you can type Markdown syntax characters while editing, and perhaps optionally see the Markdown syntax in your notes. “Markdown notes app” is really like a class of notes apps unto itself.
Some people find this surprising, but I personally don’t want to use a Markdown notes app.
I created Markdown two decades ago
and have used it ever since for one thing and one thing only: writing for the web at Daring Fireball. My
original description
of what it is still stands: “Markdown is a text-to-HTML conversion tool for web writers.” Perhaps an even better description of Markdown is Matthew Butterick’s,
from the documentation for Pollen
: “Markdown is a simplified notation system for HTML.”
The other great use case for Markdown is in a context where you either
need
or just
want
to be saving to a plain text file or database field. That’s not what Apple Notes is or should be. I can see why many technically-minded people want to use Markdown “everywhere”. It’s quite gratifying that Markdown has not only become so popular, but
after 21 years
, seemingly continues to grow in popularity, to the point now where there clearly are a lot of people who seemingly enjoy writing in Markdown more than even I do. But I think it would be a huge mistake for Apple to make Apple Notes a “Markdown editor”, even as an option. It’s trivial to create malformed Markdown syntax; it shouldn’t be possible to have a malformed note in Apple Notes. I
craft
posts for Daring Fireball; I dash off notes in Apple Notes.
Apple Notes offers a great WYSIWYG rich text editing interface that works great on an iPhone and even better on a Mac, which I think is exactly appropriate. Particularly clever are the limited formatting options, where you don’t pick a font per se, but rather only from a set of predefined styles, like headings, lists, and block quote. It’s not nerdy at all. That’s the Macintosh way. (But that’s why I think Apple Notes’s use of hashtags, rather than real tokenized tags
like in the Finder
, was an enormous mistake on Apple’s part. Real tokenized tags can contain spaces (so a multi-word tag can just be “Words Written Naturally” not “#WordsCrammedTogether”) and don’t need to be prefixed with an ugly, nerdy-looking
#
character. Notes using hashtags is like if the Finder disallowed spaces and uppercase letters in filenames.)
But Markdown
export
from Notes? That sounds awesome. Frankly, perhaps the biggest problem with Apple Notes is that its export functionality is rather crude —
PDF and, of all formats, Pages
. Exporting and/or copying the selected text as Markdown would be pretty cool. Very curious to see how they handle images though, if this rumor is true.
★
Wednesday, 4 June 2025

data.title: City halts police license plate reader program after public pushback
data.article_summary: Austin has decided to halt its police department's automated license plate reader (ALPR) program following public pushback and concerns over privacy and data sharing. The program, which was set to be extended after a one-year pilot, faced opposition from city council members and community groups who argued it represented surveillance overreach. Critics highlighted risks associated with the city's contract with Flock Safety, a public safety technology company, particularly regarding data sharing with federal agencies like U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). Despite police asserting the technology helped solve crimes, the city manager withdrew the program extension from the council agenda to address concerns. Opponents emphasized the need to protect civil liberties and personal privacy.

The Austin Police Department's use of dozens of automated license plate readers, or ALPRs, will end this month following community
pushback

City Council was scheduled to vote on June 5 to indefinitely continue an ALPR
pilot program
that started last March and was temporarily
extended
this spring. However, City Manager T.C. Broadnax moved to withdraw the item after council's
recent review
of the city's program

and a June 3 discussion that drew dozens of people to City Hall
against the item
.
APD leaders including Chief Lisa Davis said ALPRs have proven to be a key crime-fighting tool that helped the short-staffed police department investigate and solve dozens of cases since early 2024, and that officers are properly using the system within council-imposed guardrails. Opponents on the council dais and in the community have said the cameras represent surveillance overreach, and that Austin's contract with public safety technology company
Flock Safety
allows for unwanted data-sharing with other private sources or federal agencies like U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement.
Despite having confidence in APD's responsible use of the camera system, Broadnax said he was pulling the
proposed
program extension from council's June 5 agenda in response to negative public reactions.
"Given concerns expressed today, I have decided to withdraw this item from the agenda at this time to provide more opportunities to address council members’ questions and do our due diligence to alleviate concerns prior to bringing this item back to City Council for consideration," he said in a June 3 message to city leaders.

The revival of police ALPR use in Austin was first
considered
back in 2022 after the program's 2020 suspension. Since the $114,000 pilot officially launched last year, city auditors found dozens of arrests had been made under the program based on tens of millions of license plates scans.

Because we can’t just take their verbal assurances, right? Once we looked at the contract with Flock, we realized that Austin’s data was being put at risk," he said.

44190838.article_summary: Austin has decided to halt its police department's automated license plate reader (ALPR) program following public pushback and concerns over privacy and data sharing. The program, which was set to be extended after a one-year pilot, faced opposition from city council members and community groups who argued it represented surveillance overreach. Critics highlighted risks associated with the city's contract with Flock Safety, a public safety technology company, particularly regarding data sharing with federal agencies like U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). data.title: Quarkdown: A modern Markdown-based typesetting system
data.author: asicsp
data.article_summary: Quarkdown 是一个现代的、基于 Markdown 的排版系统，具有强大的扩展功能，可以将项目编译成印刷书籍或互动演示文稿。它扩展了 CommonMark 和 GFM，支持函数调用、变量定义和丰富的语法扩展，提供布局构建、I/O、数学计算、条件语句和循环等功能。Quarkdown 还支持创建复杂的动态内容，并兼容 HTML、PDF 等多种输出格式，适用于书籍、文章和幻灯片制作。系统提供快速编译和实时预览功能，易于学习和使用，同时具备高度的文档控制能力。通过其标准库和自定义函数支持，用户可以创建丰富的文档和演示文稿。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：KeenWrite及其他Markdown排版系统的比较与争议

不同观点：
• **支持KeenWrite及其功能**：thangalin介绍了自己开发的FOSS文本编辑器KeenWrite，通过处理链（Markdown -> XHTML -> TeX -> PDF）帮助撰写科幻小说，并提供了教程和脚本基础设施的描述。该用户对KeenWrite的功能和架构持积极态度。

• **与Typst的比较**：structural提到Typst最近受到很多关注，但在KeenWrite的功能对比表中完全没有提及，令人感到意外。

• **质疑比较表的准确性**：blenderob质疑比较表的准确性，特别指出LaTeX的全脚本能力，以及对Quarkdown语法和学习曲线的质疑。他还提到LaTeX通过tex4ht可以生成HTML。

• **与Quarto的比较**：account-5提到Quarto，认为KeenWrite和Quarto在名称、扩展名和目标上相似，但目前功能较少。

• **模板语言和多语言切换的困扰**：looneysquash对模板语言增加函数调用持怀疑态度，认为这会造成多语言切换的困扰，并偏好使用JSX或JavaScript的 tagged template literals。

• **对不同类型排版系统的需求**：rendaw指出Typst和类似系统主要关注论文排版，而对表单、传单等其他文档类型支持不足。

• **与reStructuredText的比较**：cbarrick认为KeenWrite的语法与reStructuredText相似。

• **对现代Markdown排版系统的需求与批评**：krick表示希望有一种现代的Markdown排版系统来替代LaTeX，但对KeenWrite的JVM依赖、语法和无缝使用体验持批评态度。

• **商标问题**：Lammy提到使用“Quark”这个词在出版界可能有风险，因为QuarkXPress已经注册了商标。

• **标准化问题**：AmazingTurtle对Markdown、Quarkdown、Typst等工具的多样性和缺乏标准化感到困惑，并选择回到HTML+CSS。

• **语法建议**：silvestrov建议更改函数调用语法，以避免与现有文档中的函数名冲突。

• **Markdown内容与布局的分离**：TheEdonian喜欢KeenWrite作为Markdown的扩展层，但强调Markdown只应关注内容，而布局应由CSS/JS等工具处理。

• **LaTeX的局限与希望**：bryanhogan对Markdown的局限性感到失望，转向LaTeX，但希望未来有基于Markdown的系统能替代LaTeX。

• **现有工作流的满意度**：ryukoposting对其使用LaTeX和Pandoc的工作流感到满意，因为工具的成熟度保证了文档的长期可编译性。

• **对JVM语言的CLI工具的批评**：francislavoie对KeenWrite使用JVM语言开发CLI工具表示不满，偏好静态二进制文件。

补充讨论：
1. **争议焦点**：KeenWrite与其他排版系统（如Typst、Quarto、LaTeX）的功能对比和语法差异。
2. **用户需求多样性**：不同用户对排版系统的需求和偏好各异，有的关注论文排版，有的关注其他文档类型，还有的对语法和无缝使用体验有较高要求。
3. **技术实现的讨论**：包括JVM依赖、语法设计、商标问题和标准化问题等技术实现和使用体验方面的讨论。

About
Quarkdown is a modern Markdown-based typesetting system, designed around the key concept of
versatility
, by seamlessly compiling a project
into a print-ready book or an interactive presentation.
All through an incredibly powerful Turing-complete extension of Markdown, ensuring your ideas flow automatically into paper.
Original credits:
Attention Is All You Need
Born as an extension of CommonMark and GFM, the Quarkdown Flavor brings
functions
to Markdown, along with many other syntax extensions.
This is a function call:
.somefunction {arg1} {arg2}
Body argument
Possibilities are unlimited
thanks to an ever-expanding
standard library
,
which offers layout builders, I/O, math, conditional statements and loops.
Not enough?
You can still define your own functions and variables — all within Markdown.
You can even create awesome libraries for everyone to use.
.function {greet}
to from:
**Hello, .to** from .from!
.greet {world} from:{iamgio}
Result:
Hello, world
from iamgio!
This out-of-the-box scripting support opens doors to complex and dynamic content that would be otherwise impossible
to achieve with vanilla Markdown.
Combined with live preview and ⚡ fast compilation speed, Quarkdown simply gets the work done.
Check the
wiki
to learn more about the language and its features.
Check out the demo presentation
here
Built with Quarkdown itself —
source code
(Desktop view is suggested)
As simple as you expect...
Inspired by:
X-ray flashes from a nearby supermassive black hole accelerate mysteriously
...as complex as you need.

HTML
✅ Plain output (default)
✅ Slides
via
reveal.js
✅ Paged (books, articles)
via
paged.js
Paged documents require a webserver to render in the browser. See the
-p
option below.
PDF
✅ All document types and features supported by HTML are also supported when exporting to PDF.
Check the wiki's
PDF export
page to learn more.
The desired document type can be set by calling the
.doctype
function
within the source itself:
.doctype {slides}
.doctype {paged}

主要讨论点：生酮饮食与酮体补充对身体和大脑的影响

不同观点：
• [客观陈述] **caleb-allen** 提到研究中一名研究者与一家开发酮体营养产品的公司有关联，暗示潜在的利益冲突。
• [健康风险] **kirykl** 担心长期生酮饮食可能对肾脏造成负担，暗示生酮饮食对肾脏有潜在风险。
• [方法质疑] **casenmgreen** 对研究方法提出质疑，指出研究仅观察了一次大剂量酮体摄入的效果，而非长期摄入，并计算出如果每日摄入，成本高达900美元，质疑实际应用的可行性。
• [个人体验支持] **Kiyo-Lynn** 分享个人经验，表示在进行生酮饮食几周后，感受到精神上的清晰和整体状态的改善，支持酮体对大脑能量供应的积极作用。
• [寻求替代] **anonzzzies** 表示无法维持生酮饮食，询问是否有其他补充剂可以替代。
• [批评] **cmiller1** 强烈批评研究结论，认为其是将机械性推测伪装成因果推论，暗示这是借生酮概念牟利的行为。

data.title: MonsterUI: Python library for building front end UIs quickly in FastHTML apps
data.author: indigodaddy
data.article_summary:
**文章主要内容总结：**

现代Web开发中，创建美观的用户界面需要复杂的依赖和大量样板代码，涉及多种语言，导致开发过程繁琐。为此，MonsterUI应运而生，旨在简化这一过程。它基于FastHTML，结合了HTMX、Starlette等技术，同时解决了美学设计难题。MonsterUI提供预先设计好的组件和智能默认设置，开发者无需编写CSS即可实现美观、响应式的UI组件，专注于功能开发。其核心是FrankenUI，一个无框架的UI库，结合了Tailwind等现代库的优势，同时保持灵活性。MonsterUI已在实际生产环境中得到验证，适用于复杂对话框和动态内容渲染等场景。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕FastHTML和MonsterUI的评价与争议

不同观点：
• **支持传统与功能性组件的开发者观点**：[jph00] 作为FastHTML的创建者，认为FastHTML回到了网络开发的基础，利用功能性组件与HTML标签直接映射，对于熟悉HTML和功能性编程的开发者来说无需学习新知识。他强调这种方法在实际应用中表现良好，尤其是在处理如SSE和WebSockets等复杂交互时。

• **对新语法和学习曲线的担忧**：[johnfn] 认为FastHTML的语法（如DivLAligned、DivFullySpaced等）比传统的HTML/CSS更复杂，且与现有的Flexbox和Tailwind等工具相比，文档和社区支持不足。他担心这是用不同名字重新发明了已有的CSS工具。

• **对所谓“高级抽象”的质疑**：[boxed] 批评MonsterUI所谓的“高级抽象”实际上与HTML的抽象层次相同，并未提供真正的简化。他以自己开发的iommi框架为例，认为真正的抽象应更具创新和简化。

• **实用性与灵活性的权衡**：[mushufasa] 认为FastHTML等框架对希望专注于数据处理的开发者有吸引力，但在需要精细调整前端时可能不足，导致需要重写功能。这种工具在内部工具或概念验证阶段有用，但在实际应用中可能不够灵活。

• **对多重抽象层和调试难度的担忧**：[pacifika] 指出FastHTML及其依赖的多个抽象层（如HTMX、Starlette）增加了调试的复杂性，认为这种多层抽象可能导致更多的边缘情况和调试困难。

• **历史经验的反思**：[AsthmaBoy] 分享了早年使用PL/SQL生成HTML的经历，认为回到这种方法是倒退，并质疑为何在2025年还会有人选择这种方案。

• **教育工具的有效性**：[acbart] 介绍了自己的教育库Drafter，利用类似的方法让学生用Python开发Web应用，认为这种方法在教育环境中有效。

• **对纯Python前端解决方案的需求**：[vFunct] 表达了对纯Python声明式HTML组件/CSS/JS框架的需求，希望能避免使用HTML/CSS/JS。

• **通用组件库的推广**：[kissgyorgy] 介绍了自己开发的通用Python组件库，支持混合匹配和Bootstrap v5，并有展示工具。

• **模板语言的比较**：[danpalmer] 质疑为何不直接使用模板语言，认为基本HTML加少量占位符更易于理解和使用。

• **对项目开放性与资金来源的疑问**：[dcreater] 询问MonsterUI的开发模式是否开放源代码，以及Answer.ai的资金来源。

补充讨论：
• **对特定方法的强烈反对意见**：[atparinas] 强烈反对这种类似Elm的方法，预见其可能带来的问题。

争议焦点：FastHTML和MonsterUI的实用性、语法复杂性、多重抽象层的调试难度以及与现有工具和方法的比较。

44162814.article_content:
Modern web development requires complicated dependencies and extensive boilerplate spread over multiple languages to make good UI.
MonsterUI
is here to fix that.
The Problem with Web UI Development
Building attractive web applications has always been complicated.
FastHTML
simplifies web app development by bringing HTMX, Starlette, HTML, and HTTP fundamentals together.
Getting the aesthetics right is still too hard. It requires either extensive
CSS
, a framework with long inline class strings, or both. You might try
Bootstrap
or
Tailwind
CSS. Now, you’re managing class names, remembering utility patterns, and checking docs for boilerplate class strings. This leads to code that is hard to build, maintain, and change for anyone who is not an expert designer.
A typical app has many components: nav bars, forms, modals, cards, and more. Each requires careful consideration of styling, responsive behavior, and interactive states. As your application grows, managing these styles consistently becomes more and more challenging.
This became apparent to me while I was developing web apps. I found myself copying and pasting class strings and maintaining complex styling logic across multiple components. FastHTML made the application logic development a joy, but the styling side remained a constant source of friction.
If you’re tired of context-switching between HTML, CSS, and Python just to build basic web UIs,
MonsterUI
might be for you.
Real-World Example: Building a Blog
Introducing MonsterUI
MonsterUI
lets anyone build high-quality, modern web apps in pure Python without sacrificing design quality.
Built with MonsterUI, styled with FrankenUI, based on design by Shadcn
MonsterUI
is a layer on top of FastHTML that provides pre-styled components and smart defaults based on modern libraries (such as Tailwind, FrankenUI, DaisyUI) while maintaining full access to Tailwind CSS when you need it. MonsterUI:
Brings FastHTML’s simplicity to web styling.
Provides beautiful, responsive components without writing a single CSS class.
Lets you focus on building features instead of remembering utility classes.

What MonsterUI does for you
MonsterUI
is based on a simple principle: provide smart defaults while allowing full flexibility.
We’ve done this by builing upon proven approaches from some of the most innovative projects in modern web development, carefully selecting components that address the pain points of raw HTML/CSS while maintaining mature, battle-tested strategies.
MonsterUI’s core is
FrankenUI
, an innovative framework-free UI library by
sveltecult
that uses beautiful HTML-first components. FrankenUI itself was inspired by
shadcn/ui
by
shadcn
which pioneered the concept of copy-pasteable UI components for React.
Raw HTML and CSS present two key challenges: dated visual aesthetics and complex layout management. By combining FrankenUI’s framework-agnostic approach with FastHTML, MonsterUI delivers modern, beautiful components that integrate seamlessly with HTMX’s progressive enhancement paradigm - all while maintaining clean, readable code.
This isn’t just theory - we’re using
MonsterUI
in production for new applications we’re testing with preview customers, where it powers everything from complex dialog interfaces to dynamic content rendering. The library has been proven robust and maintainable in real-world enterprise setti

主要讨论点：Clearspace应用及其相关API的功能、隐私、可用性及潜在改进

不同观点：
• **功能改进建议**：
  - TrueGeek：希望能够自定义使用更多的应用，而不是减少使用。他的语言学习应用被错误地锁定。
  - Drag0s：支持添加React Native SDK，并希望通过API控制屏幕时间。
  - Beggi：询问是否计划通过API限制应用使用。
  - Roycebranning：提议建立超时自动扣款服务。

• **隐私与数据安全**：
  - Codethief：对应用需要连接Google账户和网络权限表示担忧，担心数据被出售。
  - Abletonlive：虽然认为概念很酷，但因隐私问题不愿使用，强调了对数据处理的担忧。

• **技术与兼容性**：
  - Awaseem：询问API是否为开源，并表示可能将其集成到Foqos（开源限制应用）中。
  - Kovek：询问是否有MacOS上的类似解决方案。
  - Mikaoj85：指出iOS网页显示问题，质疑是否是故意设计。

• **积极反馈与兴趣**：
  - Navs：对应用在心理健康数据监测中的潜力表示兴奋，并提到目前手动导入数据的实践。
  - Alexdanilowicz：支持减少手机使用时间的理念，分享了自己严格控制屏幕时间的做法。
  - Jdamon96：对尝试使用该应用表示期待。

• **其他**：
  - Handfuloflight：询问设备数据如何通过API传输，是否需要安装额外组件。
  - Aziaziazi：对应用UI表示赞赏，并询问是否使用了公共CSS框架/主题。

补充讨论：
• **访问权限**：
  - Noleary：询问是否可以通过链接向所有人开放访问权限。

争议焦点：
• **隐私问题**：部分用户对数据隐私和安全表示担忧，特别是应用权限和数据处理方式。
• **功能局限**：部分用户对应用自动锁定某些应用的功能感到不便，希望有更多自定义选项。

这些观点反映了用户对Clearspace应用的功能、隐私、技术实现及用户体验的多方面关注和建议。

不同观点：
• **[jjkaczor]** 分享了自己在清仓拍卖店的经历，起初能以极低价格买到高质量商品，但随着更多人参与，价格上涨，商品质量下降，甚至一些店铺已经关闭。他认为整体经济放缓可能是导致商品减少的原因。
• **[mdip]** 描述了自己所在地区类似的店铺，认为这些店铺依然有大量库存，并且能以较低价格买到高价值商品，尽管需要花费更多时间和精力。
• **[neilv]** 提出这些店铺可能在挑选有价值的商品放在自己的线上商店出售，而不是全部放在实体店中，这种做法可能影响消费者的购物体验。
• **[nancyminusone]** 对店铺中的商品质量持批评态度，认为大部分商品都是垃圾，难以理解为什么会有人购买。
• **[tra3]** 表达了对退货行为的不适感，宁愿不买也不愿意退货，这与其他人对购物和退货的态度形成对比。
• **[jccalhoun]** 也认为这些店铺中的商品多为廉价和无用的物品，导致店铺难以维持经营。
• **[chime]** 引用视频讨论了这些商品处理背后的环境影响，质疑这些商品是否真的避免了进入垃圾填埋场。
• **[bravesoul2]** 认为在清仓店省钱需要极大的耐心和纪律，建议有计划地购物以避免买到无用商品。
• **[twright]** 通过在亚马逊套利公司的实习经历，指出这些店铺提供了一个寻找已生产商品的场所。
• **[tantalor]** 讨论了关税对进口商品和清仓店可能产生的影响，认为经济冲击可能会促进二手经济的发展。
• **[ryukoposting]** 提到自己当地的 surplus 店通过 GoFundMe 筹集资金，担心这种模式会取代传统店铺。
• **[twic]** 和 **[jp57]** 则分别以幽默的方式对店铺的定价策略和购物体验进行了评论。

补充讨论：
• 商品的来源和店铺的运营模式是讨论的重点，包括店铺如何挑选商品以及潜在的环境影响。
• 价格策略和经济环境的变化对这些店铺的影响也是讨论的核心，涉及到买家费用、关税和整体经济放缓等因素。
• 争议的焦点在于这些店铺的商品质量和价格是否值得消费者花费时间和精力去寻找和购买。

Jen Kinney
Capital
Seven Days At The Bin Store
By
Jen Kinney
9:02 AM EDT on June 4, 2025
Share on Bluesky
Share on Reddit
Share on WhatsApp
Share on Email
150
Comments
This spring, a new business opened on the main drag of my West Philadelphia neighborhood, provoking both excitement and trepidation.
“I saw it just the other day and feared it,” one friend texted. “Like what the actual fuck is that shit,” said another. “Why?!!!” said a third. “Who is that for?”
Until last summer, the corner storefront at Baltimore Avenue and S. Melville Street was a moderately overpriced hipster vintage store. After it closed, it sat empty for nearly a year. Then, in March, it sprang to life.
A “grand opening” banner went up over the door. A miniature wacky inflatable tube man flailed around outside. Posters with the logos for Walmart, Amazon, Costco, and Best Buy covered the windows, declaring “CRAZY DEALS, AMAZING BINZ.” I had to check it out.
AMAZING BINZ is on the first floor of a rowhome, narrow and long. There’s one central aisle, and on either side, big wooden tray tables—the proverbial binz—overflowing with undifferentiated piles of consumer
stuff
: unopened Halloween costumes, an ice mold shaped like a penis, a banner of many glittery penises wearing grass skirts, a staggering number of “reusable hot and cold gel compression sleeve[s] for elbow,” a single loose pregnancy test, something called Wokaar for “waxing the nose beard.”
At least half the products are still in boxes, and there are signs on the walls warning customers to NOT OPEN THE BOXES, so you have to scan the barcode with your phone or decipher clipped product descriptions: “module stool,” “gratitude journal,” “Xmas tea light green.” But the great innovation of Amazing Binz is its pricing structure, which is splashed across the facade in Spanish and English and makes good on the promise of CRAZY DEALS. On Fridays, when the bins are freshly stocked, everything costs $10. On Saturdays, $8. Sundays: $6. Mondays: $4. Tuesdays: $2. Wednesdays: $1. Thursday is bin store Sabbath, when the shop is closed and restocked.
The store is like nothing else on the block, which boasts, among other things, a yoga studio, two vape shops, a volunteer-run book store
and
a Marxist reading room, and no fewer than four Ethiopian joints.
Where did all this stuff come from? Who opened this store, and why? Is it profitable? What does it mean for the uneven gentrification of Baltimore Avenue and West Philadelphia? I decided to spend a week visiting Amazing Binz every day. Here is what I found.
Thursday: Restock Day
On Thursdays, Amazing Binz is closed. One of the owners, Ahmed, has graciously allowed me to observe the restock. Overall, Ahmed has been very gracious about my fixation on his store.
When I arrive at 10:30 a.m., he’s smoking a cigarette and nervously awaiting a delivery truck with 18 pallets of mixed merchandise from Target. Amazing Binz gets its inventory from major corporations’ overstock and returned products, taking advantage of the vast weird world of “reverse logistics.”
“ You've got the front end, where you order the product, it comes into the port, it goes to a warehouse, to a store, and then to our front door,” says Cathy Roberson, a researcher at the Reverse Logistics Association, an industry trade group. “What if once it hits our front door, we don't like it, or it's broken or something? That's the reverse part. ”
Returns, repairs, refurbished products, and even recalls fall into the purview of reverse logistics. They are joined there by products that never made it to a consumer because the season ended, or a box was a little dented, or the purchaser never picked up their order, or a retailer was just running out of room in their warehouse.
That pile of excess stuff is growing. About 17 percent of all merchandise gets returned, according to the National Retail Federation. That’s up from just eight percent in 2019. For online purchases, it’s almost 30 percent.
Liquidators are nothing new: T.J. Maxx, Ocean State Job Lot, Nordstrom Rack. But as the scale of the excess grows, the reverse logistics industry is expanding, and methods of disposal are diversifying. Some corporations, like Amazon, do their own reselling through a
bulk liquidation page
. There are middlemen like
B-Stock
, an eBay-like site where anyone can shop for truckloads of unwanted stuff. Influencers are buying pallets to unbox on stream, capitalizing on both the goods and the views. It’s a whole universe of brokers, wholesalers, and secondhand retail all trying to claw back a little bit of money from the growing pile. That’s where Amazing Binz comes in.
“The goal for all the reverse logistics stuff,” says Roberson, “is to keep things out of the landfill.”
Today, Ahmed is expecting half a truckload with about 3,500 to 4,500 individual pieces, ranging from kitchen appliances to toys to clothing; he doesn’t know exactly what. The semi-truck pulls up right on time, and Ahmed unloads it with a forklif

data.title: Show HN: ClickStack – Open-source Datadog alternative by ClickHouse and HyperDX
data.author: mikeshi42
data.article_summary: HyperDX 是一个开源的可观测性平台，集成了会话回放、日志、指标、 traces 和错误监控，基于 ClickHouse 和 OpenTelemetry 构建，帮助工程师快速解决生产环境问题。它支持在 ClickHouse 集群上轻松搜索和可视化日志及 traces，提供直观的全文本搜索和属性搜索，支持设置警报和分析异常趋势。HyperDX 可以通过 Docker 快速部署，兼容 OpenTelemetry，支持多种语言和平台的应用监控。平台文档、贡献指南和部署选项详见其官网和文档。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：HyperDX及相关技术工具的用户体验、功能比较、技术集成及未来发展

不同观点：
• JimDabell认为HyperDX的用户界面（UI）设计不友好，存在显示错误和阅读困难的问题，尤其是字体和颜色搭配让使用体验变得糟糕。他建议采用更传统的设计风格，而非80年代的终端风格。
• theogravity对HyperDX的成本效益表示赞赏，并提到自己开发的LogLayer可以与HyperDX集成，同时希望合作推出新的集成方案。
• readdit对HyperDX的性价比表示认可，但担心原HyperDX产品是否会被弃用，是否需要迁移到ClickStack。
• regnerba运行的是Grafana技术栈，虽然对现有系统满意，但认为其组件过多，配置复杂，正在考虑是否转向HyperDX。
• hosh关心OpenTelemetry（Otel）在ClickStack中的应用，尤其是其是否支持statsd数据摄入、跨 traces、logging、metrics 的关联分析，以及UI是否支持相关数据的链接。
• gigatexal认为Datadog虽然昂贵，但功能强大，尤其是其仪表盘和报警功能，可以节省工程时间，从而抵消成本。
• wiradikusuma和codegeek都提到Signoz与HyperDX的相似性，并询问两者之间的区别，尤其是在使用ClickHouse和UI设计上的不同。
• bilalq关注Clickhouse是否为该技术栈中唯一的状态存储部分，并建议增加与Rust的OTEL收集器Rotel的兼容性，以便在无服务器环境中使用。
• user3939382表示对众多日志聚合工具感到困惑，认为Datadog价格过高且UI混乱。
• ensignavenger关心HyperDX是否必须依赖MongoDB，并询问是否有其他开源文档存储可以替代。
• buserror对大量无意义的日志记录表示不满，认为许多日志记录并没有实际用途，且增加了不必要的成本。
• ah27182关心使用Docker容器时是否需要登录。

补充讨论：
• 关于Signoz与HyperDX的比较是一个反复出现的主题，多个用户询问了两者在功能、UI设计和后端技术上的区别。
• 技术集成问题也被多次提及，尤其是与OpenTelemetry、statsd数据摄入、以及与不同日志收集工具的兼容性。
• 用户对成本和性能的关注显著，尤其是Datadog的高价格与HyperDX的性价比之间的对比。
• 一些用户担心HyperDX的未来发展，特别是产品是否会被弃用以及是否需要迁移到新的技术栈。

争议焦点：
• HyperDX的UI设计是否合理及其对用户体验的影响。
• 大量日志记录的实际价值和成本效益问题。
• Signoz和HyperDX之间的功能和性能比较。

总体来看，讨论围绕HyperDX的功能、用户体验、技术集成及其与竞争对手的比较展开，用户对成本、性能和未来发展的关注较为显著。

http://localhost:8080
to access the HyperDX UI.
If you already have an existing ClickHouse instance, want to use a single
container locally, or are looking for production deployment instructions, you
can view the different deployment options in our
deployment docs
.
If your server is behind a firewall, you'll need to open/forward port 8080,
8000 and 4318 on your firewall for the UI, API and OTel collector
respectively.
We recommend at least 4GB of RAM and 2 cores for testing.
Hosted ClickHouse Cloud
You can also deploy HyperDX with ClickHouse Cloud, you can
sign up for free
and get started in
just minutes.
Instrumenting Your App
To get logs, metrics, traces, session replay, etc into HyperDX, you'll need to
instrument your app to collect and send telemetry data over to your HyperDX
instance.
We provide a set of SDKs and integration options to make it easier to get
started with HyperDX, such as
Browser
,
Node.js
,
and
Python
You can find the full list in
our docs
.
OpenTelemetry
Additionally, HyperDX is compatible with
OpenTelemetry
, a vendor-neutral standard for
instrumenting your application backed by CNCF. Supported languages/platforms
include:
Kubernetes
Javascript
Python
Java
Go
Ruby
PHP
.NET
Elixir
Rust
(Full list
here
)
Once HyperDX is running, you can point your OpenTelemetry SDK to the
OpenTelemetry collector spun up at
http://localhost:4318
.
Contributing
We welcome all contributions! There's many ways to contribute to the project,
including but not limited to:
Opening a PR (
Contribution Guide
)
Submitting feature requests or bugs
Improving our product or contribution documentation
Voting on
open issues
or
contributing use cases to a feature request
Motivation
Our mission is to help engineers ship reliable software. To enable that, we
believe every engineer needs to be able to easily leverage production telemetry
to quickly solve burning production issues.
However, in our experience, the existing tools we've used tend to fall short in
a few ways:
They're expensive, and the pricing has failed to scale with TBs of telemetry
becoming the norm, leading to teams aggressively cutting the amount of data
they can collect.
They're hard to use, requiring full-time SREs to set up, and domain experts
to use confidently.
They requiring hopping from tool to tool (logs, session replay, APM,
exceptions, etc.) to stitch together the clues yourself.
We hope you give HyperDX in ClickStack a try an

data.title: Google restricts Android sideloading
data.author: fsflover
data.article_summary: Google近期通过限制Android系统的侧载功能，以增强安全性、防止诈骗和恶意软件。在新加坡的试点项目中，通过网页浏览器、消息应用或文件管理器侧载的某些请求敏感权限的应用将被阻止安装。同时，Google推出了Play Integrity API，允许开发者限制侧载应用的功能，鼓励用户通过Google Play商店安装应用。这些举措引发了对用户自主权、创新限制和市场竞争的担忧，批评者认为此举使Android更接近苹果iOS的封闭生态。对此，Purism推出运行PureOS的Librem 5手机，提供安全、隐私尊重和数据自主的替代方案，不依赖企业应用商店和侵入式API。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Google在部分地区和情况下限制 sideloading 应用的功能，引发了关于用户自由、安全性以及技术实现的讨论。

不同观点：
• tdeck：认为一些评论忽视了普通用户的技术水平，高级用户可以通过技术手段解决限制，但普通用户很难做到。对普通用户来说，限制 sideloading 是有意义的，因为这可以防止恶意软件和诈骗。
• Aurornis：指出限制主要针对新加坡的一个试点项目，且仅限于某些敏感权限的应用。高级用户仍然可以找到方法 sideload 应用，这不算对自由的严重侵犯，更多的是对普通用户的保护。
• jeroenhd：认为这个限制早在一年多前就已宣布，质疑相关博客文章的发布时机。提到可以通过关闭 Play Protect 绕过限制，但同时也引用了新加坡警方的案例，说明诈骗犯如何利用 sideloaded 应用进行诈骗。
• gbin：虽然主张用户应有对自己设备的最大控制权，但也提到 DJI 强制用户 sideload 应用的例子，指出这种做法可能带来的安全隐患。
• Zigurd：认为 Google 的设计是合理且有意义的，限制 sideloading 只是增加了恶意软件运行的难度，而不是完全禁止。
• danieldk：指出 GrapheneOS 提供了 Google Android 的安全优势，但 Google 拒绝让其使用 Play Integrity API 的硬件认证功能，导致某些应用无法使用，批评 Google 的双重标准。
• londons_explore：解释新加坡的特殊情况，指出诈骗和身份交易问题严重，限制敏感权限的应用是必要的。
• rafram：认为相关讨论是软文，没有具体分析。
• nikodunk：主张支持开源项目如 postmarketOS，认为继续 fork Android 不是长久之计。
• AstralStorm：建议仅在调试模式和用户明确许可的情况下允许 sideloading，认为这是更安全的方案。
• mfuzzey：关心替代应用商店如 F-droid 是否会受到影响，提到 Ingress 玩家常用的非官方应用。
• throitallaway：认为 Google 应专注于完善沙盒和权限模型，而不是限制应用来源。
• qbane：个人习惯 sideload 应用，无法想象无法 sideload 的情况，可能会因此而 root 设备。
• EwanToo：指出相关新闻早在2024年就已发布，质疑讨论的时效性。
• mcflubbins：关心 Librem 5 手机的基本功能和可靠性，特别是短信和通话功能以及电池寿命。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于用户自由与设备安全的平衡。高级用户认为限制不应存在，普通用户则可能从限制中受益。
• 具体技术实现如 GrapheneOS 和 Play Integrity API 的使用问题也被提及，显示出对 Google 政策的不满。
• 新加坡的试点项目被多次提到，显示出该项目在讨论中的重要性。
• 对 sideloading 的安全风险有多个例子支持，如 DJI 应用和诈骗案例。
• 对替代方案如 postmarketOS 和 Librem 5 的讨论显示出社区对开放性和安全性的持续关注。

data.title: Programming language Dino and its implementation
data.author: 90s_dev
data.article_summary: Dino是一种高级脚本编程语言，结合了面向对象和函数式编程的特性。它由Vladimir Makarov开发，最初于1993年为俄罗斯游戏公司ANIMATEK设计，之后经过多次修订。Dino具有多精度整数、异构可扩展数组、关联表、数组切片、模式匹配、Unicode 8支持等特性。其并发处理通过纤维（fiber）实现，类似于绿色线程，比OS线程更快且具有确定性行为。Dino的类是一种特殊函数，支持多重继承和动态调度。其字节码编译器和解释器支持JIT和类型推断，性能可与Python、Ruby、JavaScript等语言媲美。Dino的实现包括多种工具和优化，目标是提供一种高效、安全且易用的编程语言。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对Animatek以及相关技术（如OCaml）的评价与比较

不同观点：
• **[johnisgood]** 对基准测试数据表示困惑，认为OCaml速度应该很快，但数据似乎显示其不如Python或Ruby。他质疑是否实现上有严重问题，并希望查看代码以进一步理解。
  - 论据：OCaml通常速度很快，因此对基准测试结果表示怀疑；如果真的比Python或Ruby慢很多，可能是实现问题。
  
• **[ghurtado]** 认为Animatek在功能上看起来非常现代化和完整，具备一些独特功能，可能特别吸引Python用户，因为填补了Python的一些已知缺陷。
  - 论据：Animatek具有独特且现代的功能，对Python用户有吸引力，能够解决某些语言层面的不足。

• **[Lerc]** 对Animatek这一名称在多年后再次出现感到意外，并表达了一种情感上的反应，可能带有些许怀旧或遗憾，建议在遇到困难时寻求帮助。
  - 论据：情感反应，可能涉及对过去经历的回忆或对该技术重现的感慨；建议寻求帮助，可能暗示该技术或团队面临挑战。

• **[bravesoul2]** 对Animatek持调侃态度，称其为“1993年的golike”，并提到其名称与现代某个JavaScript运行器相似。
  - 论据：通过对比1993年的技术与现代技术，暗示Animatek可能有些过时或与现代技术有某种相似性；名称上的巧合也被提及。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点：对Animatek性能和功能的评价存在分歧。johnisgood对性能数据表示怀疑，而ghurtado则对其功能表示肯定。
- 其他值得注意的讨论点：Lerc的情感反应和建议，以及bravesoul2的调侃态度，显示出对该技术名称和历史的不同看法。

Programming language Dino and its implementation
Develepment version of future release 0.98
Vladimir Makarov,
vmakarov@gcc.gnu.org
Apr 2, 2016
Description Layout
Introduction to Dino
History
Dino as a high-level scripting language
Dino as a functional language
Dino as an object-oriented language
Dino Implementation
Overall Structure
Used implementation tools
Byte code compiler (optimizations)
Byte code Interpreter (GC, Concurrency, REPL)
JIT, Type inference
Performance comparison with Python, PyPy, Ruby, JS, Scala, OCAML
on x86-64, AARH64, ARM, PPC64.
Some history
1993: Original language design and implementation
Was used in russian computer game company ANIMATEK as a simple
scripting language for describing dinosaurus movements
1998, 2002, 2007, 2016 : Major language and implementation revisions
This document describes the current state of Dino language and
its implementation.
The first taste of Dino
Eratosthenes sieve:
var i, prime, k, count = 0, SieveSize = 8191, flags = [SieveSize : 1];
for (i = 0; i < SieveSize; i++)
if (flags[i]) {
prime = i + i + 3;
k = i + prime;
for (;;) {
if (k >= SieveSize)
break;
flags[k] = 0;
k += prime;
}
count++;
}
putln (count);
DINO as a scripting language
Dino aims to look like C language
High-Level scripting object-oriented language:
Multi-precision integers
Heterogeneous extensible arrays, array slices
Associative tables with possibility to delete elements
Powerful and safe class composition operation for (multiple)
inheritance and traits description
First class functions, classes, and fibers with closures,
anonymous functions, classes, fibers
Exception handling
Concurrency
Pattern matching
Unicode 8 support
Arrays and Tables
Associative tables
elements can be added and deleted
elements can be any values, e.g. other tables
Implemented as hash tables without buckets for compactness
and data locality
Secondary hash for conflict resolutions
Murmur hash function for most values
Array Slices
Eratosthenes sieve with slices:
var i, prime, count = 0, SieveSize = 8191, flags = [SieveSize : 1];
for (i = 0; i < SieveSize; i++)
if (flags[i]) {
prime = i + i + 3;
flags[i + prime:SieveSize:prime] = 0;
count++;
}
putln (count);
Functions
Example:
fun even;
fun odd  (i) {i == 0 ? 0 : even (i - 1);}
fun even (i) {i == 0 ? 1 : odd (i - 1);}
putln (odd (1_000_000));
Anonymous functions:
filter (fun (a) {a > 0;}, v);
fold (fun (a, b) {a * b;}, v, 1);
Function closures:
fun incr (base) {fun (incr) {base + incr;}}
Threads
Fiber: a function with concurrent execution
fiber t (n) {for (var i = 0; i < n; i++) putln (i);}
t(100); // the following code don't wait for t finish
for (var i = 0; i < 1000; i++) putln (“main”, i);
Implemented as green threads:
Much faster than OS threads with Global Interpreter Lock (Python/Ruby)
Deterministic behaviour and automatic deadlock recognition
Plans to implement through OS threads without GIL for parallelism
There is a low level sync-statement wait
wait (cond) [stmt];
Simple statements are atomic
Object orientation
Class is just a special type of function:
Returns closure, public visibility by default
class num (i) {fun print {put (i);}}
class binop (l, r) { fun print_op;
fun print {l.print(); print_op (); r.print ();}
}
Special class/function composition:
emulates (multiple) inheritance, traits, and dynamic dispatching
class add (l, r) {
use binop former l, r later print_op;
fun print_op {put (“ + “);}
}
Object orientation -- continuation
A safe and powerful way to support object orientation

44193965.article_summary: Dino是一种高级脚本编程语言，结合了面向对象和函数式编程的特性。它由Vladimir Makarov开发，最初于1993年为俄罗斯游戏公司ANIMATEK设计，之后经过多次修订。Dino具有多精度整数、异构可扩展数组、关联表、数组切片、模式匹配、Unicode 8支持等特性。其并发处理通过纤维（fiber）实现，类似于绿色线程，比OS线程更快且具有确定性行为。Dino的类是一种特殊函数，支持多重继承和动态调度。其字节码编译器和解释器支持JIT和类型推断，性能可与Python、Ruby、JavaScript等语言媲美。Dino的实现包括多种工具和优化，目标是提供一种高效、安全且易用的编程语言。

• **[ghurtado]** 认为Animatek在功能上看起来非常现代化和完整，具备一些独特功能，可能特别吸引Python用户，因为填补了Python的一些已知缺陷。
  - 论据：Animatek具有独特且现代的功能，对Python用户有吸引力，能够解决某些语言层面的不足。

• **[Lerc]** 对Animatek这一名称在多年后再次出现感到意外，并表达了一种情感上的反应，可能带有些许怀旧或遗憾，建议在遇到困难时寻求帮助。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：微软Aurora天气预测模型的发布及其相关技术与应用

不同观点：
• magicalhippo：对深度神经网络在解决量子物理问题上的成功表示认可，并认为其在天气预测中的良好表现并不意外。同时提供了Aurora模型相关的发布链接和资源。
   
• sieste：认为AI基础模型不应被简单宣传为传统物理预测的替代品，强调AI天气模型依赖于ERA5再分析数据（结合观测和数值模型预测），建议更多强调AI与物理模型的协同作用，而非单纯比较优劣。

• xnx：提问Aurora模型是否与谷歌的模型类似，并附上了谷歌相关研究的链接。

• scottcha：基于使用经验，对Aurora模型的优点进行了总结，包括开源、可配置性强、免费非商业使用、与开发者互动良好等。

• goochphd：提到了一些关于Aurora项目的演示，指出其在中小尺度天气现象和极端天气预测上的优势，以及在训练高分辨率数据空间方面的技术突破。

• dmillard：提到Aurora系统的两位原作者离开微软创立了Silurian.ai，建议关注这一新项目。

• croemer：提供了与Aurora相关的Nature论文链接。

• Lyngbakr：指出AI天气模型（如GraphCast、Aardvark、NeuralGCM、Aurora等）的研发团队常包括微软和谷歌的员工，质疑这些公司内部的跨团队合作是否促进了技术进步，或者这些模型开发是否完全独立。

• nxobject：提出Aurora模型是否可以用于制作沙盒模拟游戏的设想。

• waltbosz：提到Aurora模型的命名让他联想到阿西莫夫的小说《基地与地球》中的行星Aurora。

• roger_：表示一直关注GitHub上的wesselb，很高兴看到其工作获得更多关注。

• dunkeltaenzer：质疑为何在讨论中为付费墙内容打广告。

补充讨论：
• 关于Aurora模型与谷歌模型的比较（xnx和goochphd的观点）。
• 关于AI模型与传统物理模型关系的争议（sieste的观点）。
• 对Aurora模型技术细节和应用潜力的探讨（goochphd和scottcha的观点）。
• 对Aurora模型团队成员流动及新项目成立的关注（dmillard的观点）。
• 对模型命名与文化作品关联的联想（waltbosz的观点）。
• 对付费墙内容在讨论中出现的质疑（dunkeltaenzer的观点）。

data.title: Understanding the PURL Specification (Package URL)
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: Package URL (PURL) 是一个开放标准，用于跨不同软件生态系统唯一标识软件包。PURL 由 Philippe Ombredanne 于 2017 年创建，是一种特殊格式的 URL，描述软件包在注册表中的位置或身份。其结构类似于网页 URL，包含类型、名称、命名空间、版本、限定符和子路径等字段。PURL 已成为软件物料清单（SBOM）的重要组成部分，用于唯一标识软件组件。它支持多种编程语言和包管理器，如 npm、PyPI、Maven、Docker 等，并可在 SBOM 中作为组件的唯一标识符。尽管某些字段是可选的，但在实际使用中对唯一标识包至关重要。

主要讨论点：PURL（Package URL）标准的实用性及其在不同场景下的适用性

不同观点：
• alcroito认为PURL在跟踪非托管在Conan.io或Linux发行版注册表上的C/C++原生库方面不够完善，特别是自托管在如GitLab或特定项目托管平台上的库（如Qt、KDE）。他指出当前缺乏对GitLab或自定义托管库的标准支持，且开放工具和数据库不支持此类自定义C++生态系统，使得漏洞跟踪困难。

• dedicate认为PURL使得软件物料清单（SBOMs）在开源软件中更加实用，而不仅仅是基于CPE的“最佳猜测”。

• emddudley澄清了PURL与Internet Archive管理的PURL（持久URL）无关。

• kdeldycke分享了其项目Meta Package Manager对PURL的支持，并提供了使用示例和项目链接。

• zzo38computer指出了PURL的一些问题，包括缺乏加密哈希、未区分接口和实现、以及某些包类型的限定符示例不明确。

• quibono认为PURL比CPE更易用，特别是在处理不符合传统供应商/产品划分结构的软件时。

• RS-232对PURL的命名空间属性持批评态度，认为其使用点号（dot notation）而非连字符（kebab case）是不合理的。

• heavenlyhash提出了关于包名称包含斜杠的处理问题，特别是Go语言包的命名方式。

• rahkiin询问了PURL如何处理未托管在Docker上的Docker镜像或自定义npm注册表。

• CodingKing认为PURL混淆了URL（有位置）和URN（有身份）的概念，建议应使用注册的URN。

• donenext批评了`generic`类型的滥用，认为这是工具偷懒的结果，并呼吁改进PURL规范的实用性。

补充讨论：
• 90s_dev幽默地提到了xkcd 927，暗示标准化问题在软件社区中具有普遍性和共鸣。

争议焦点：
• PURL在处理自托管库、特定语言包（如Go）、以及不同命名空间格式方面的有效性和适用性。
• `generic`类型的使用是否削弱了PURL规范的实用性，以及如何改进以支持更多自定义和特定场景的包管理需求。

The Package URL (PURL) specification is an open standard for uniquely identifying software packages across different ecosystems. It was
created in 2017
by Philippe Ombredanne, an open source tooling maintainer who needed a better way to standardize references to software packages.
A PURL is a specially formatted URL that describes a software package's location or identity in a package registry. It encodes the package type (e.g. npm, Maven, PyPI), the name (and optional group or namespace), version, and other qualifiers in a single string.
PURL's purpose is to provide a simple, universal identifier for software components, making it easy to track and share what components are in your software. Although PURL has several important use cases, the combination of its universal properties and machine-readability in particular have made it an essential part of enabling the modern SBOM landscape.
In this blog, we'll explain in more depth how PURL works (including differences in different ecosystems), how it’s used in
SBOMs
, how it compares to CPE and other component identifiers, and more.
How PURL Works
A Package URL is structured similarly to a web URL, with multiple components separated by specific symbols. The general syntax is:
pkg:<type>/
<namespace>/
<name>@<version>
?<qualifiers>#<subpath>
Each part of this string has a specific meaning, which we'll outline below; you can also reference the
PURL Spec’s GitHub README
and
PURL Types page
for additional context.
Required Fields
scheme
:
The scheme is always
pkg
, indicating a package URL (just like
http
or
https
in web URLs). This constant prefix helps tools recognize a PURL immediately.
type
:
The package
type
or ecosystem, such as
npm
,
maven
,
pypi
,
nuget
,
gem
(RubyGems), etc.
name
:
The name of the package (artifact or module name).
Optional Fields
namespace
:
An optional namespace or group for the package, which is specific to the ecosystem. For example, in Maven, this would be the groupId (
org.apache.logging.log4j
), in Docker it might be an image owner, or in GitHub it could be an organization/user. Not all ecosystems have namespaces.
version
:
The version of the package (if applicable). Not all PURLs include a version (e.g. if you want to refer to a package in general), but typically an SBOM or vulnerability reference will include a specific version here.
qualifiers
:
Additional key-value pairs to further qualify the package, prefixed by
?
and separated by
&
. Qualifiers are optional and depend on the package type.
subpath
:
An optional subpath within the package, appended after a
#
. This can point to a specific file or directory inside the package. It's used when you need to reference a particular piece of a package's content.
It's important to note that while the above fields are optional when determining whether a PURL is valid, in practice, they play very important roles in making it possible to uniquely identify a package. Specifically, namespace and version are important for all ecosystems, and qualifier and subpath are important in particular for Linux ecosystems.
To help bring everything together, let's consider an example PURL for a Maven Central artifact:
pkg:maven/
org.apache.logging.log4j/
log4j-core@2.14.1
This identifies the Apache Log4j Core library version 2.14.1 from the Maven ecosystem (groupId org.apache.logging.log4j, artifactId log4j-core).
PURL Ecosystem Coverage
PURL supports a broad array of programming language ecosystems and package managers out of the box. Common types include
npm
(Node.js/JavaScript packages),
pypi
(Python packages),
maven
(Java artifacts),
nuget
(.NET packages),
gem
(Ruby Gems),
golang
(Go modules),
cargo
(Rust crates),
docker
(container images), and system packages like
deb
(Debian/Ubuntu) or
rpm
(Fedora/RedHat).
Each type definition specifies how to interpret the namespace and qualifiers for that ecosystem. For instance, Docker PURLs use the image name as the name and tag or digest as the version (e.g.
pkg:docker/nginx@1.21.0
or by digest), and may use a qualifier for the registry URL.
There's even a
generic
type as a catch-all for things that don't fit an existing ecosystem (for example, a proprietary or legacy component) or for ecosystems that build custom distributions, such as yocto or buildroot. We should note, however, that SBOM and software composition analysis tools vary widely in their ability to understand generic PURLs, so we do recommend you talk to your current (or prospective) vendor if this is an important feature for you.
PURL and SBOMs
The most common Package URL use case that we see today is the role it plays in enabling the SBOM (software bill of materials) ecosystem. SBOMs are essentially a list of components (libraries, frameworks, modules, etc.) that make up a software product, and PURLs play a critical role in SBOMs by acting as the unique identifiers for each component.

data.article_summary: 文章主要探讨了技术创新之间的相互关联，特别是枪械与相机之间的联系。作者Étienne Fortier-Dubois解释了相机和枪械共享一些术语（如“装载”、“瞄准”、“射击”）的原因，可能源于人们将枪械操作的语言用于描述操作相似的相机。文章追溯了电影摄影技术的起源，指出托马斯·爱迪生和其实验室发明的电影摄影机（kinetograph）受到了法国科学家艾蒂安-朱尔·马雷的瞬时摄影研究启发，而马雷的设计又受到了天文学家皮埃尔·詹森的“摄影左轮”启发。詹森的设备借鉴了左轮手枪的旋转机制，而这种机制可追溯到16世纪的枪械技术。作者强调，许多技术创新看似无关，实则彼此联系，并介绍了自己正在进行的项目——构建一个展示主要技术创新及其相互联系的时间线，称为“历史技术树”（historical tech tree）。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：

• [garrettgarcia] 对早期科技发明的时间线表示兴趣，尤其是那些在智人出现之前就被发明的技术。

44161607.article_content:
The Universal Tech Tree
Étienne Fortier-Dubois
When we try and pick out any technology in isolation, we find it hitched, in some way, to every innovation that preceded it. (Except for the Oldowan hand axe. We had to start somewhere.)
What do firearms and cameras have in common? One answer is shared vocabulary: load, aim, shoot. The etymological origins of this relatedness are murky. People likely borrowed language about firearms — which are over 500 years older than photography — to talk about cameras, which are operated in a similar manner.  But in the case of the movie camera, the connection is concrete.
The first movie camera is generally considered to be the kinetograph, invented in 1891 by Thomas Edison and William Kennedy Dickson, an inventor at the Edison lab. Two years earlier, Edison had travelled to Paris to the Exposition Universelle of 1889, a world’s fair, to showcase his company’s phonograph. There, he met with Étienne-Jules Marey, a French scientist who had begun his career studying blood circulation, and who had developed an interest in chronophotography partly out of his work on physiology. Chronophotography consists of taking multiple photographs in quick succession to capture movement.
A famous early achievement of the technique is
The Horse in Motion
, a series of photographs taken by Eadweard Muybridge in 1878 that proved something Marey had asserted years earlier: For a brief moment in gallop, a horse has all four hooves off the ground. Encouraged by Muybridge, Marey developed an improved device to take chronophotographs. The resulting design, the “photographic gun,” featured a long barrel derived from existing firearms. We don’t know what transpired between Marey and Edison, but it seems likely that Marey’s design inspired the kinetograph. Coincidentally (or not), the Online Etymology Dictionary’s entry for “
shoot
” claims “the meaning ‘to photograph’ (especially a movie) is from 1890” — around the time of the kinetograph’s invention.
Marey himself had been inspired by the invention of another Frenchman, the astronomer Pierre Janssen. In 1874, hoping to capture images of the transit of Venus, Janssen created a device he called the “photographic revolver.” It looked like a large telescope. Inside, it hosted a complex camera that used a revolving apparatus to take several images in quick succession. The resulting eight seconds of the black dot of Venus moving across the sun disk are often recognized as the first motion picture in history.
1
Prior to Jansenn’s invention, revolving components had not been used in photography or astronomy. They came from the Colt Paterson revolver, a handgun popular in the U.S. since its mid-19th century creation by Samuel Colt. Thus, we can reconstruct a genealogical succession of ideas: Colt inspired Janssen, who inspired Marey, who likely inspired Edison (who then inspired the Lumière brothers and further developments in filmmaking).
We can go further back still. Colt improved the revolver and made its mass production commercially viable, but he did not invent it. Nor was it a particularly recent development: Guns with a revolving barrel have existed since the 16th century. A
German revolver
dates from 1597, but there are even older specimens. The
xun lei chong
, a Chinese revolving musket, also dates from this period.
It makes sense: The 1500s were a time of great innovation in firing mechanisms for muskets and arquebuses, with developments like the wheellock (which used a spinning metal wheel against pyrite to create sparks), snaplock (which struck flint against steel using a spring-loaded arm), and flintlock (which improved on the snaplock with a combined hammer-flint holder). Volley guns made of multiple cannons existed in England since at least the 1330s. These were descendants, in turn, of simpler cannons that stem from the invention of gunpowder in China in the 800s. It stands to reason that eventually
someone
in Europe would think of making a spinning mechanism to allow a weapon to fire multiple shots in quick succession.
And yet, if you’re anything like me, most of what you just read was probably surprising. We don’t typically associate revolvers with the 1500s, or, for that matter, with movie cameras.
The reason I learned about this — and dozens of anecdotes around other inventions — is that I have been working on a quixotic project to place all major technological innovations in history on a timeline, together with the connections between them. The goal is to situate stories like that of the revolver and camera in their historical context, notice patterns, and understand the logic of the history of technology. The result is an interactive visualization that I call
the historical tech tree
.
Étienne-Jules Marey, Bird Flight, Pelican, 1886.

data.title: Rare black iceberg spotted off Labrador coast could be 100k years old
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 2025年5月中旬，纽芬兰省卡博尼尔的渔民哈鲁尔·安东尼森在拉布拉多海岸捕虾时拍摄到了一座罕见的黑色冰山，引发社交媒体热议。这座冰山距离拉布拉多海岸超过100公里，呈现独特的钻石形状和黑色纹理。纪念大学的物理海洋学教授莱夫·塔拉索夫推测，这座冰山可能有上千年的历史，甚至可能达到10万年之久。他表示，冰山可能含有火山灰或千年积累的尘土，显示了冰的动态变化过程。冰流从格陵兰内部移动到海岸，形成冰山并最终漂至纽芬兰和拉布拉多。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：黑色冰山的特征、成因、科学价值以及相关术语和表述的讨论。

不同观点：
• [tickerticker] 认为暴露在外的部分是接近球形的，而水下的部分由于对称性应该是巨大的，才能支撑露出部分保持直立状态。
• [scoot] 提出疑问，这是否仅仅是一个引起兴趣的现象，还是对科学家、地质学家、气候学家等专业人士有潜在价值，可以通过采样获取有用的数据。
• [morkalork] 关心冰山断裂后的年龄问题，询问这些断裂的冰山是否会变得越来越老。
• [IncreasePosts] 认为由于冰山颜色较暗，可能会因为太阳辐射而快速融化，并质疑其年龄是否更接近100年而非100,000年。
• [tromp] 对媒体使用“指数级”一词表示不满，认为媒体错误地使用了“指数级”来表示“很多”，并质疑是否应该接受这种用法。

补充讨论：
• [tantalor] 幽默地提到是否可以在冰山周围找到“超级样本”。
• [bee_rider] 以幽默的方式询问黑色拉布拉多冰山是否像狗一样有蹼足以更好地游泳。
• [dylan604] 表示对“鱼类收获者”（fish harvester）这一术语不熟悉，质疑是否因为捕鱼量大而改变了术语。
• [m3kw9] 以幽默的方式询问这些冰山什么时候会变成饮品出售。

争议焦点：
• 冰山的年龄问题：[IncreasePosts] 和 [tromp] 都对冰山年龄的表述表示质疑，尤其是[IncreasePosts] 认为冰山由于颜色深会快速融化，从而不可能有100,000年的历史。[tromp] 则对媒体使用“指数级”来形容年龄感到不满。

这些观点展示了人们对冰山现象的多角度关注，包括科学、术语、幽默和批判性思考。

44193120.article_content:
NL
Rare black iceberg spotted off Labrador coast could be 100,000 years old, prof says
A fish harvester from Carbonear, N.L., snapped a photo of a black iceberg while fishing for shrimp of the coast of Labrador in mid May. It caused a sensation on social media, and impressed a Memorial University professor who says it's likely a very old piece of ice dating back thousands of years.
Berg may contain ice coloured by millennia of dirt — or even a meteorite strike
John Gaudi
·
CBC News
·
Posted: Jun 04, 2025 11:28 AM EDT | Last Updated: June 4
This black iceberg was spotted more than 100 kilometres off the coast of Labrador in mid-May. Fisher Hallur Antoniussen took a photo of it to show crewmates, but it quickly took off after being posted on social media.
(Submitted by Hallur Antoniussen)
Social Sharing
A rare black iceberg spotted off the coast of Labrador is making a splash on social media after a fish harvester living in Carbonear, N.L., took a photo of it while fishing for shrimp last month.
Originally from the Faroe Islands, Hallur Antoniussen was working with a crew on board the Saputi factory freezer trawler off the coast of Labrador in mid-May.
He'd never seen an iceberg like this one before.
"I have seen icebergs that are rolled, what they say have rolled in the beach with some rocks in it. This one here is completely different. It's not only that he is all black. He is almost ... in a diamond shape," Antoniussen said in an interview with CBC Radio's
Labrador Morning
.
He spotted the berg after going up the ship's crane when they were more than 100 kilometres offshore in the Hopedale channel, located between Nain and Hopedale.
A crew member had counted 47 icebergs in the area just the day before.
Antoniussen doesn't think it's a berg that tipped over — or rolled on the beach — picking up dirt and rocks after getting grounded. He's seen a lot of icebergs over his 50 years of fishing off of Greenland, and more recently off the Labrador coast since 1989.
The 64-year-old said it was hard to estimate the size of the iceberg at sea but figured it was at least three times the size of a regular bungalow.
He took a picture from roughly six kilometres away.
"It's something you don't see very often, and a camera is not something I run around [with] when I'm working. So, I just ran to my room and took my phone and snapped this picture," he said.
Memorial professor Lev Tarasov says ice from all over Greenland is converging toward its coastline, and then breaks off to form icebergs after reaching the water. Pictured here is the Kangerlussuaq Fjord outlet in Greenland.
(Submitted by Lev Tarasov )
Antoniussen said the berg looked like a rock with lots of really dark greys and black veins in it, and quickly ruled out that a shadow was being cast on it.
He took the photo to show other crew members on the fishing boat. Then Antoniussen posted it on Facebook, and it soon took off, garnering hundreds of comments after being shared around.
Commenters have mused about everything from aliens to precious metals, and even dinosaurs being hidden in the ice.
"It's an Oil Berg," said one poster.
"Looks like a giant [woolly] mammoth!" exclaimed another.
Antoniessen is clear: this is a real photo.
Other people wondered if the iceberg has volcanic ash in it, a result of some ancient eruption.
An impressive iceberg
Lev Tarasov, a Memorial University professor of physical oceanography, doesn't rule that last theory out completely.
Tarasov says there are volcanoes beneath the ice caps of Iceland, and while he's not exactly sure about volcanoes in Greenland, he added that scientists have measured hotspots in the landmass's central region.
Like Antoniussen, he hasn't seen an iceberg quite like this one before.
Tarasov observed smaller versions of the black iceberg during his fieldwork on the Kangerlussuaq Fjord in Greenland last summer — just not as impressive, he said.
Memorial University's Lev Tarasov is shown here conducted fieldwork in Greenland last summer. The professor says the black iceberg might contain ice that's more than 100,000 years old.
(Submitted by Lev Tarasov)
He guesses the ice in the berg is at least 1,000 years old, but could also be exponentially more ancient — even formed as many as 100,000 years ago.
Tarasov said ice from all over Greenland is slowly converging toward its coastline, and when it gets there, it breaks off to form icebergs.
Those icebergs can take one to three years before reaching the Newfoundland and Labrador coastline.
A terrestrial journey
Tarasov says it's a reminder just how dynamic ice can be.
Ice streams, also known as outlet glaciers, move much faster than other parts of the ice sheet; they carry ice from the interior, traveling through deep valleys or channels out to the coast.
They pick up rocks and dirt along the way.
"There's parts of the ice that are actually flowing up to 20 kilometres per year, which would mean that ... the ice is moving maybe a few metres every hour," Tarasov said.

• [tickerticker] 认为暴露在外的部分是接近球形的，而水下的部分由于对称性应该是巨大的，才能支撑露出部分保持直立状态。
• [scoot] 提出疑问，这是否仅仅是一个引起兴趣的现象，还是对科学家、地质学家、气候学家等专业人士有潜在价值，可以通过采样获取有用的数据。
• [morkalork] 关心冰山断裂后的年龄问题，询问这些断裂的冰山是否会变得越来越老。
• [IncreasePosts] 认为由于冰山颜色较暗，可能会因为太阳辐射而快速融化，并质疑其年龄是否更接近100年而非100,000年。
• [tromp] 对媒体使用“指数级”一词表示不满，认为媒体错误地使用了“指数级”来表示“很多”，并质疑是否应该接受这种用法。

补充讨论：
• [tantalor] 幽默地提到是否可以在冰山周围找到“超级样本”。
• [bee_rider] 以幽默的方式询问黑色拉布拉多冰山是否像狗一样有蹼足以更好地游泳。
• [dylan604] 表示对“鱼类收获者”（fish harvester）这一术语不熟悉，质疑是否因为捕鱼量大而改变了术语。
• [m3kw9] 以幽默的方式询问这些冰山什么时候会变成饮品出售。

争议焦点：
• 冰山的年龄问题：[IncreasePosts] 和 [tromp] 都对冰山年龄的表述表示质疑，尤其是[IncreasePosts] 认为冰山由于颜色深会快速融化，从而不可能有100,000年的历史。[tromp] 则对媒体使用“指数级”来形容年龄感到不满。

这些观点展示了人们对冰山现象的多角度关注，包括科学、术语、幽默和批判性思考。
