Rest of World/Getty Images
By
Gayathri Vaidyanathan
3 June 2025
Startups selling bossware products are mushrooming globally.
The "Little Tech" ecosystem is under-regulated and largely funded by venture capital.
Workers say they feel a loss of autonomy when they are managed by an algorithm rather than a human.
Technologies that promise to track, manage, and supervise workers, increasingly using artificial intelligence, are getting entrenched in the developing world, according to a new
report
by Coworker.org, a labor rights nonprofit based in New York.
Audits of more than 150 startups and regional companies based in Kenya, Nigeria, Colombia, Brazil, Mexico, and India showed workplace surveillance is expanding in scale and sophistication, the researchers said. While large
corporations
are
known
to develop surveillance technologies, a so-called Little Tech ecosystem of mostly unregulated, venture capital-funded startups and small vendors making these products has grown since Covid-19, the report found. The term “Little Tech” was popularized by the VC firm
Andreessen Horowitz
, which argued that excessive regulation was stifling innovation.
Algorithmic management
and surveillance tools are getting even more intrusive in gig work, and are entering offices and the informal labor sector as well, Wilneida Negrón, director of research and policy at Coworker.org and a co-author of the report, told
Rest of World
.
“The pressure of the hyper-surveillance creates a lot of stress and creates a lot of uncertainty for workers. It brings a culture of suspiciousness,” she said.
Investments by Silicon Valley-based VC firms led to a boom in tech startups globally after Covid-19, Negrón said. This has carried over to companies building bossware products in the developing world, she said.
The technologies include biometric tracking, AI-powered productivity monitoring, and predictive analytics, the report found. Worker data is continuously collected and analyzed by algorithms with the stated aim to improve hiring, evaluate performance, and optimize processes.
Most managers in wealthier nations say algorithmic management tools improve their decision-making, according to a 2024
survey
of over 6,000 employers by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development. More than 90% of American managers used such tools, especially to reward or sanction employees.
Many tools are first deployed in Latin America, where labor laws are less strictly enforced, according to Ayden Férdeline, a tech policy researcher in Berlin and a co-author of the report.
“There is a Latin America testing ground for products,” he told
Rest of World
. “If they are successful, they tend to be deployed in other jurisdictions, oftentimes with additional safeguards, sometimes not.”
Many workers are unaware of how their information is collected and used, Férdeline said.
Some gig workers in Kenya, Guatemala, and Brazil said bossware tools make them feel surveilled, and that they have less control over their work. In Porto Alegre, Brazil, Uber driver Carina Trindade told
Rest of World
she feels the app monitors her continuously, tracking her speed and braking patterns. The app has permissions
to access
her mic and camera, she said.
Uber spokesperson Gabriel Gabira said drivers have the option to record trips, and
privacy terms
are followed to access the footage.
In Nairobi, Godfrey Sanya Wanga, a driver for ride-hailing firm SafeBoda, told
Rest of World
he felt the app undercharged a customer. “I really wanted to ask [the customer] to pay me more, but I remembered that I was being monitored and this would bring me trouble if the client reported me,” he said. SafeBoda did not respond to a request for comment.
Several nations have data protection and privacy laws, including Brazil, Nigeria, and Kenya. But enforcement is inconsistent, the report said.
Here are five current uses of algorithmic management tools. The companies mentioned below did not comment, unless otherwise stated.
1.
Timekeeping and attendance systems
What: Platforms that track the attendance of workers, often using geolocation and biometrics to verify presence.
Example:
Rankmi
, based in Chile, uses biometrics and geolocation to track workers. The platform also
gives
workers continuous performance feedback and evaluates job applicants using AI.
2.
Biometric and identity verification tools
What: Tools that use fingerprint and facial-recognition checks, special digital signatures stored on a secure network, and official records to confirm a worker’s identity before granting access.
Example: Cincel, based in Mexico, provides
identity verification
tools that do various checks including biometrics, and also cross-check against government databases and
blacklists
.
3.
Performance and productivity monitoring platforms
What: Dashboards that score workers using tracked metrics such as keystrokes, transaction counts, customer interactions, and task completion times.
Example:
Ahgora
, based in Brazil, offers

data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个可以通过两次拍手打开Chrome浏览器或任何指定文件/应用程序的Python项目（two_claps_open）。项目灵感来自“钢铁侠”电影中的类似场景。通过录音分析，作者发现拍手声音的能量主要集中在1.4kHz到1.8kHz频率范围，并据此设置了一个带通滤波器来识别拍手声。项目使用峰值检测实时识别两次拍手，进而触发指定操作。项目依赖包括numpy、pyaudio、scipy等库，并提供了激活语音助手的额外功能。使用时需设置Google API密钥。项目代码遵循MIT许可证。

🔸Activate a voice assistant agent by clapping twice (agent_on_clap.py)
demo2.mp4
Clap Detection
To figure out what a clap "looks like" in terms of sound, I first recorded a sample clap and ran a Fourier transform on it to check the frequency content.
From the analysis, most of the energy from the clap is concentrated around 1.4kHz to 1.8kHz.
Based on this, I set up a bandpass filter to isolate only that range and ignore irrelevant noise.
After filtering, I used peak detection to recognize when a clap happens in real time. (see figure below)
Once two peaks (claps) are detected with some minimum spacing, the system launches Chrome (or any command you define).

data.title: A critical look at OpenBSD's installer
data.author: JdeBP
data.article_summary: 本文是《2025年安装BSD》系列的第二部分，聚焦于OpenBSD 7.6的安装过程，与FreeBSD的安装程序对比，OpenBSD的安装更为简洁直接，采用问答形式而非菜单界面。文章详细描述了在虚拟机中进行两次安装的过程：第一次使用视频控制台安装简易图形系统，第二次模拟服务器环境通过串行安装。OpenBSD安装程序首先选择键盘映射和主机名，然后进行网络配置，包括VLAN、静态IP和自动配置选项。接着设置根密码、选择默认服务、创建用户（不能使用‘yes’作为用户名），并配置时区和磁盘。安装程序支持全盘加密，提供默认分区方案，用户也可自定义分区，但无法创建softraid镜像。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：串口通信速度的变化及不同操作系统在安装和终端处理方面的差异

不同观点：
• JdeBP认为，与30年前的BBS繁荣时期相比，串口通信速度在2025年降回到9600 BPS是令人遗憾的倒退。他指出，现代虚拟UART和廉价的USB到DB9 RS232适配器完全可以支持更高的速度，但我们在串行通信和终端技术上却出现了不必要的退步。

• JdeBP提到VT100和VT220终端的区别并不如想象中大，因为VT220的多数功能在简单的块终端安装程序中并不常用。他还指出FreeBSD在termcap和terminfo处理上的特例情况，并讨论了安装映像在DASD上的使用以及NetBSD和OpenBSD安装程序的不同表现。

• WalterGR提供了有关NetBSD的额外信息，通过引用一个Hacker News的讨论链接，暗示可能有更多关于NetBSD的细节可以参考。

补充讨论：
• JdeBP强调了在某些情况下，NetBSD安装程序比OpenBSD更灵活，但如果不预先调整安装映像，NetBSD安装程序会自动扩展分区并占用整个设备空间，导致没有剩余空间用于交换分区。

• 关于终端类型，"teken"终端类型在FreeBSD中的处理不当问题被提及，并提到terminfo中已存在"teken-2022"版本。这显示了在不同操作系统中终端类型处理和更新的复杂性。

• 评论中还涉及安装介质的选择，例如USB存储设备和TF卡，相对于传统DVD、CD-ROM或软盘安装方法，这些现代介质提供了更多的空间。

44189920.article_content:
[New to Gemini? Have a look at my
Gemini FAQ
.]
This article was bi-posted to Gemini and the Web
; Gemini version is here:
gemini://gemini.circumlunar.space/users/kraileth/neunix/2025/installing_bsd_pt2.gmi
[Edit: Of course this had to be published on the day that OpenBSD 7.7 was released!]
This is the second part of the “installing BSD in 2025”. The
first one
was about FreeBSD’s installer.
In this article we’ll take a look at OpenBSD’s installer. The version used is the one that comes with release 7.6. Unlike FreeBSD, I don’t install OpenBSD all the time. I’ve done a fair amount of installations over the years, so I’m somewhat familiar with it. However not nearly as familiar that I could do an installation with my eyes closed. If you know everything about the OpenBSD installer (e. g. which username cannot be picked!), then you might want to read this article only if you’re interested in an outsider’s perspective.
Compared to FreeBSD, OpenBSD does a lot of things differently. Their installer is probably as much no-frills, no-nonsense as it could be. Instead of the dialog menu based one of FreeBSD, it simply asks you questions and you type in the answers.
I’m going to install OpenBSD in a VM twice. The first time I’ll be using the video console and opt for a graphical system. The second install will be a more server style one and will use installation over serial.
Installing a simple graphical OpenBSD system
I deliberately limited the VM that I’m using here to only 1GB of RAM, 1 CPU core and 8GB of disk space. This might seem like an odd choice for a desktop system – and to be honest it is. The rationale here is that I want to show that the installer is actually dynamic, accounting for what system resources are available. So these limitations are meant to allow me pointing out how things are different in the second installation.
OpenBSD installer options
After starting the install, a short paragraph explains the basic functionality to new users which is good. Especially the defaults allow for making it through the installer very quickly for the most common cases. At the same time the ability to shell out of the installer gives experienced OpenBSD users ultimate flexibility to do things that the installer won’t do on its own. It can do a lot, though.
The first thing to do is choosing the keymap. You either enter your preferred one or ask for a list if you don’t know what’s available. Then you enter the host name. The installer clearly indicates that it expects the short form rather than an FQDN which is great.
OpenBSD installer: Keymap, network, services and users
Next is the actual network configuration. The installer lists the configurable interfaces and even gives you the option to set up VLANs – which is not terribly common for installers to do. Selecting an interface you’ll be given the option to enter a static IPv4 address for it, attempt to automatically configure it or not use an IPv4 address. Afterwards the same is done for IPv6. If you choose to autoconfigure IPv4 or v6 for an interface, the installer uses the domain name and nameservers provided via DHCP.
These options are about excellent and cover the vast majority of scenarios perfectly. If you’re in need for advanced networking configurations involving things like link e. g. aggregation, you probably want to do that after the installation, anyway.
OpenBSD installer: time zone and disk selection
After the network configuration is done, you set the root password. Then the installer asks you which services to enable by default. On a desktop system you probably don’t want SSH but you want xenodm (OpenBSD’s variant of xdm). You also get the option to change the default console to serial as well as setting up a user (as long as it’s not named ‘yes’! 😉).
Next is setting up the time zone, then selecting the disk(s). The correct time zone has been determined in my case, but the installer assumes the first disk to be the install target. Usually that default should be fine, but in this case it isn’t. Fortunately by letting it display details first, you can see that sd0 is actually the hypervisor’s CD image that you’re installing from.
I remember having to do it manually, but for a while now, the installer has supported full disk encryption (which is very useful). After these selections, the partitioning scheme needs to be selected. Depending on the platform, the installer offers whole disk MBR and GPT or manual for people who want to dual-boot or have other reasons for not dedicating the whole disk to OpenBSD.
OpenBSD installer: Partitioning and installation source
Once the partitioning scheme has been decided on, the installer will propose a partitioning layout, offering the user to just accept that, modify it or do custom partitioning. This is all pretty intuitive if you stick to the defaults and flexible if you want to customize things. The only thing I actually miss in this part of the installer is that it does not allow for creating a softraid mirror

data.title: I think I'm done thinking about GenAI for now
data.author: kaycebasques
data.article_summary: 本文作者是一位自认为是像福尔摩斯一样的聪明程序员，但最终意识到自己更像电视剧《神探阿蒙》中的角色。阿蒙虽然聪明，但深受神经质和心理创伤困扰，通过关注无关紧要的细节和无法忽视的微小矛盾来解决案件。作者发现自己处理问题的方式类似，通过不断纠结和调整细节，最终解决问题或构建出令人满意的作品。然而，在面对生成式AI（genAI）时，作者感到无法理顺相关矛盾，也无法构建令人信服的观点，尽管对genAI持怀疑态度，却被迫每天接触相关讨论，感到疲惫不堪。作者写作本文的目的是整理自己对genAI的理解和负面感受，解释为何无法提出令人信服的批评，并希望借此让自己和他人摆脱这一令人困扰的话题。

不同观点：
• **反对强制使用AI工具的观点**：
   - CuriouslyC认为，被迫使用AI工具，尤其是当工具表现不佳且需要人工修正结果时，会导致员工产生倦怠感。尽管某些情况下AI能提高生产力，但整体体验令人沮丧。
   - grafelic表示，AI工具剥夺了工作中学习和解决问题的乐趣，可能导致思维懒惰和创造力下降，最终对人类进步有害。
   - lsy指出，机构强制推行AI工具的做法适得其反，尤其当这些工具并没有显著提高工作效率时，强制使用只会增加反感。

• **支持AI工具的观点**：
   - the_mitsuhiko分享了个人积极的AI使用经验，特别是在法律事务和代码处理方面，AI工具极大地帮助了他。他认为AI工具的采用往往是从基层开始的，并且带来了显著的好处。
   - kentonv强调，批评AI工具的人往往没有亲自尝试过。他以自身经历为例，说明了AI工具的实际效用，并鼓励大家亲自体验后再做评价。

   - Game_Ender认为，文章对AI工具的批评缺乏实际使用经验支持，且对AI技术的未来预测过于悲观。他以自动驾驶技术的发展为例，说明AI技术可能需要更长时间才能显现其全部潜力。

补充讨论：
• **争议的焦点**在于AI工具的实际效用和强制推行的问题。一方面，有人认为AI工具提高了生产力，带来了积极的变化；另一方面，有人认为工具表现不稳定，强制使用只会增加工作负担和不满。
• **个人经验的多样性**是讨论中的一个重要方面。不同人在不同领域使用AI工具的体验各不相同，这使得对AI工具的评价存在较大分歧。
• **对新技术推广的抵触**是另一个值得注意的点。许多人对AI工具的怀疑和抵触源于对新技术的不熟悉和不确定性。

The Problem
Like many other self-styled thinky programmer guys, I like to imagine myself as
a sort of
Holmesian
genius,
making trenchant observations, collecting them, and then synergizing them into
brilliant deductions with the keen application of my powerful mind.
However, several years ago, I had an epiphany in my self-concept.  I finally
understood that, to the extent that I
am
usefully clever, it is less in a
Holmesian idiom, and more, shall we say,
Monkesque
.
For those unfamiliar with either of the respective franchises:
Holmes is a towering intellect honed by years of training, who catalogues
intentional, systematic observations and deduces logical, factual conclusions
from those observations.
Monk, on the other hand, while also a reasonably intelligent guy, is highly
neurotic, wracked by unresolved trauma and profound grief.  As both a
consulting job and a coping mechanism, he makes a habit of erratically
wandering into crime scenes, and, driven by a carefully managed jenga tower
of mental illnesses, leverages his dual inabilities to solve crimes.  First,
he is unable to filter out apparently inconsequential details, building up a
mental ratâs nest of trivia about the problem; second, he is unable to let go
of any minor incongruity, obsessively ruminating on the collection of facts
until they all make sense in a consistent timeline.
Perhaps surprisingly, this tendency serves both this fictional wretch of a
detective, and myself, reasonably well.  I find annoying incongruities in
abstractions and I fidget and fiddle with them until I end up building
something that
a lot of people like
, or perhaps
something that a smaller number of people get
really
excited
about
.  At worst, at least
I
eventually understand whatâs going
on
.  This is a self-soothing
activity but it turns out that, managed properly, it can very effectively
soothe others as well.
All that brings us to todayâs topic, which is an incongruity I cannot smooth
out or fit into a logical framework to make sense.  I am, somewhat reluctantly,
a
genAI
skeptic
.  However, I am,
even more
reluctantly, exposed to genAI Discourse every damn minute of every damn day.
It is relentless, inescapable, and exhausting.
This preamble about personality should hopefully help you, dear reader, to
understand how I usually address problematical ideas by thinking and thinking
and fidgeting with them until I manage to write some words â or perhaps a new
open source package â that logically orders the ideas around it in a way which
allows my brain to calm down and let it go, and how that process is important
to me.
In this particular instance, however, genAI has defeated me.  I cannot make it
make sense, but I need to stop thinking about it anyway.  It is too much and I
need to give up.
My goal with this post is not to
convince
anyone of anything in particular â
and weâll get to why that is a bit later â but rather:
to set out my current understanding in one place, including all the various
negative feelings which are still bothering me, so I can stop repeating it
elsewhere,
to explain
why
I cannot build a case that I think
should
be particularly
convincing to anyone else, particularly to someone who actively disagrees
with me,
in so doing, to illustrate why I think the discourse is so fractious and
unresolvable, and finally
to give myself, and hopefully by proxy to give others in the same situation,
permission to just peace out of this nightmare quagmire corner of the
noosphere.
But first, just because I canât
prove
that my interlocutors are
Wrong On The
Internet
, doesnât mean I wonât explain why I
feel
like they are wrong.
The Anti-Antis
Most recently, at time of writing, there have been a spate of âthe genAI
discourse is badâ articles, almost exclusively written from the perspective of,
not
boosters
exactly, but pragmatically minded (albeit concerned) genAI
users, wishing for the skeptics to be more pointed and accurate in our
critiques.  This is anti-anti-genAI content.
I am not going to link to any of these, because, as part of their
self-fulfilling prophecy about the âgenAI discourseâ, theyâre
also
all bad.
Mostly, however, they had very little worthwhile to respond to because they
were straw-manning their erstwhile interlocutors.  They are all getting annoyed
at âbad genAI criticismâ while failing to engage with â and often failing to
even
mention
â most of the actual
substance
of any serious genAI
criticism.  At least, any of the criticism that Iâve personally read.
I understand wanting to avoid a callout or Gish-gallop culture and just express
your own ideas.  So, I understand that they didnât link directly to particular
sources or go point-by-point on anyone elseâs writing.  Obviously I get it,
since thatâs exactly what this post is doing too.
But if youâre going to talk about how bad the genAI conversation is, without
even
mentioning
huge categories of problem like âclimate impactâ or

44193018.article_summary: 本文作者是一位自认为是像福尔摩斯一样的聪明程序员，但最终意识到自己更像电视剧《神探阿蒙》中的角色。阿蒙虽然聪明，但深受神经质和心理创伤困扰，通过关注无关紧要的细节和无法忽视的微小矛盾来解决案件。作者发现自己处理问题的方式类似，通过不断纠结和调整细节，最终解决问题或构建出令人满意的作品。然而，在面对生成式AI（genAI）时，作者感到无法理顺相关矛盾，也无法构建令人信服的观点，尽管对genAI持怀疑态度，却被迫每天接触相关讨论，感到疲惫不堪。作者写作本文的目的是整理自己对genAI的理解和负面感受，解释为何无法提出令人信服的批评，并希望借此让自己和他人摆脱这一令人困扰的话题。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Anna's Archive（AA）的全文搜索功能、其实现的技术与法律挑战，以及相关工具和应用

不同观点：
• **bhaney** 认为将AA的数据转换为纯文本并进行全文搜索在技术上是可行的，但需要耗费大量时间。他指出主要的困难在于从各种格式中提取纯文本、清理数据以及选择合适的全文搜索数据库。他估计AA的全部内容转换后大约需要10-20TB的存储空间，且可以在普通硬件上实现。

• **net01** 提到AA已经举办过一个竞赛，一些提交的方案实现了良好的搜索工具和可视化工具，这表明AA已经在一定程度上实现了搜索功能。

• **ggm** 指出AA已经具备完整的元数据索引，但全文搜索需要实现页面级别的返回，并且由于AA的内容涉及知识产权问题，实现全文搜索可能会面临法律风险。

• **laserstrahl** 介绍了一个名为OpenLip的Android应用，它可以通过发送请求到AA并解析响应来下载和阅读书籍，这为用户提供了访问AA内容的移动端解决方案。

• **imdavidsantiago** 认为尽管技术上可以通过Meilisearch、Elasticsearch或Lucene等工具实现全文搜索，但主要的挑战在于文档转换、大规模索引的效率以及法律问题。

• **petra** 对全文搜索的实用性提出质疑，认为Z-Library的关键词搜索功能并不十分有用，尤其是与Google Books相比。

• **nextos** 指出Z-Library已经在一定程度上实现了全文查询功能，但其规模小于AA，并且在某些地区需要通过Tor访问。

• **fazlerocks** 强调AA的规模（200TB+且迅速增长）以及全文索引所需的计算和存储成本极高。此外，法律问题也是主要的障碍。

• **simgt** 担心AA中是否存在非版权相关的非法内容（如儿童色情、恐怖主义等），并对下载内容的安全性表示担忧。

• **teekert** 认为像Google、Meta、OpenAI等公司在训练大语言模型时可能已经解决了类似的问题。

• **renegat0x0** 提到了一些其他搜索引擎，但这些引擎似乎并不是专门为AA设计的。

• **podgorniy** 提供了一个针对压缩fb2文件的搜索解决方案，并指出该项目具有潜在的参考价值。

• **whimsicalism** 认为很少有人愿意为一个非法且无法盈利的项目投入大量工程时间。

• **allenleein** 提出了一种不同的思路，即通过映射互联网上最常提到或引用的书籍，将它们转化为结构化数据，并为LLMs优化，构建一个可以语义搜索的个人图书馆。

• **jimmydoe** 提到Facebook和中国的一些公司可能已经获取了AA的数据并建立了搜索功能，但由于法律和声誉风险，没有人会公开这些成果。

补充讨论：
- 技术实现的讨论主要集中在文档格式转换、全文索引的构建以及搜索工具的选择。
- 法律问题被多次提及，特别是与知识产权和非法内容相关的风险。
- 一些用户提供了相关的工具和应用，如OpenLip和fb2文件的搜索解决方案，为实现AA的全文搜索提供了潜在的技术路径。
- 讨论中还涉及了AA内容的合法性和安全性问题，特别是对于下载内容的担忧。

data.title: Covert web-to-app tracking via localhost on Android
data.author: sebastian_z
data.article_summary: 本文披露了一种通过Android设备上的本地主机（localhost）进行隐蔽的网络到应用跟踪的方法，主要涉及Meta（Facebook）和Yandex。这些公司通过其应用程序（如Facebook、Instagram、Yandex Maps和Browser）在固定本地端口上监听，从浏览器获取元数据、cookie及命令。具体来说，Meta的Pixel脚本利用WebRTC技术，将浏览器中的_fbp cookie通过UDP端口传递给监听的Android应用程序，从而将用户的网页浏览活动与应用身份关联，绕过隐私保护措施如清除cookie和隐身模式。截至2025年6月3日，Meta和Yandex已停止该做法，但这种方法暴露了潜在的安全漏洞，可能被恶意应用利用来窃听用户网络活动。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Meta通过移动端应用绕过隐私保护进行用户追踪的行为及其引发的隐私和安全争议

不同观点：
• **反对追踪技术**：[voidUpdate] 和 [kriro] 等用户对广告和追踪技术持批评态度，认为这些技术主要服务于大公司的利益（如增加CEO收入），并建议通过高额罚款或税收来惩罚违规行为。
• **技术解决方案**：[bnpxft] 建议避免安装大型科技公司的应用，仅使用其网站，以减少追踪。[dylan604] 和 [bravesoul2] 则关注技术细节，讨论了Meta Pixel脚本如何通过不同端口发送数据以及这种行为对跨配置文件数据交换的影响。
• **法律和安全问题**：[GrantMoyer] 提出使用类似技术收集信息是否会违反计算机欺诈和滥用法律。[chedabob] 和 [paxys] 则讨论了技术实现中的安全隐患，如Yandex HTTPS的私钥问题和应用与浏览器在本地主机接口自由通信的安全漏洞。
• **浏览器和扩展解决方案**：[matthberg] 分享了使用uBlock Origin和Port Authority等扩展来阻止LAN资源访问的方法，并提到这些工具的局限性。[1vuio0pswjnm7] 提供了Firefox配置和Netguard、Nebulo等工具来阻止与Meta服务器的连接。

补充讨论：

44169115.article_content:
Disclosure: Covert Web-to-App Tracking via
Localhost on Android
📢
UPDATE
: As of June 3rd 7:45 CEST, Meta/Facebook Pixel script is no longer
sending
any packets or requests to localhost. The code responsible for sending the _fbp cookie has been
almost
completely removed.
Yandex has also stopped the practice we describe below.
We disclose a novel tracking method by Meta and Yandex potentially affecting
billions of Android users. We found that native Android apps—including
Facebook,
Instagram
, and
several
Yandex apps including Maps and Browser—silently listen on fixed local
ports
for tracking purposes.
These native Android apps receive browsers' metadata, cookies and commands from
the Meta Pixel and Yandex Metrica scripts embedded on thousands of web sites. These JavaScripts load
on users' mobile browsers and silently connect with native apps running on the same device through
localhost sockets. As native apps access programatically
device identifiers like the
Android
Advertising ID (AAID)
or handle user identities as in the case
of Meta apps, this method effectively allows these organizations to
link mobile
browsing sessions and web cookies to user identities
, hence de-anonymizing users'
visiting sites embedding their scripts.
This web-to-app ID sharing method bypasses typical privacy protections such as clearing
cookies, Incognito Mode and Android's permission controls. Worse, it opens the door for potentially
malicious apps eavesdropping on users’ web activity.
How does this work?
While there are subtle differences in the way Meta and Yandex bridge web and mobile
contexts and identifiers, both of them essentially misuse the unvetted access to localhost
sockets.
The Android OS allows any installed app with the INTERNET permission to open a
listening socket on the loopback interface (127.0.0.1). Browsers running on the same
device also access this interface without user consent or platform mediation. This
allows JavaScript embedded on web pages to communicate with native Android apps and
share identifiers and browsing habits
, bridging ephemeral web identifiers
to long-lived mobile app IDs using standard Web APIs.
Meta/Facebook Pixel sharing _fbp cookie from web to Meta Android apps
The Meta (Facebook) Pixel JavaScript, when loaded in an Android mobile web browser,
transmits
the first-party
_fbp
cookie using WebRTC to UDP ports 12580–12585 to
any app on the device that is listening on those ports. We found Meta-owned Android apps
Facebook
(version 515.0.0.23.90) and Instagram
(version 382.0.0.43.84), available on the Google Play Store, listening on these port range.
As of 25 2025, the Meta Pixel uses a technique known as
SDP Munging
to insert
the
_fbp
cookie contents to the SDP "ice-ufrag" field, resulting in a
Binding Request STUN message sent to the loopback address as the following figure shows.
This data flow cannot be observed using Chrome's regular debugging tools (such as DevTools).
The entire flow of the _fbp cookie from web to native and the server is as follows:
The user opens the native Facebook or Instagram app, which eventually is sent to the
background and creates
a background service to listen for incoming traffic on a TCP port (12387 or 12388)
and a UDP port (the first unoccupied port in 12580-12585). Users must be logged-in with
their credentials on the apps.
The user opens their browser and visits a website integrating the Meta Pixel.
At this stage, websites may ask for consent depending on the website's and visitor's
locations.
The Meta Pixel script sends the
_fbp cookie
to the native Instagram or Facebook app via WebRTC (STUN) SDP Munging.
The Meta Pixel script also sends the _fbp value in a request to
https://www.facebook.com/tr
along with other parameters such as page URL (dl), website and browser metadata, and the
event
type
(ev) (e.g., PageView, AddToCart, Donate, Purchase).
The Facebook or Instagram apps receive the _fbp cookie from the Meta Pixel JavaScript
running
on the
browser. The apps transmit _fbp as a GraphQL mutation to
(https://graph[.]facebook[.]com/graphql) along with other persistent user identifiers,
linking users' fbp ID (web visit) with their Facebook or Instagram account.
On or around May 17th, Meta Pixel added a new method to their script that sends the _fbp cookie
using
WebRTC TURN
instead
of STUN. The new TURN method avoids SDP Munging, which Chrome developers publicly announced
to disable following our disclosure. As of June 2, 2025, we have not observed the Facebook
or Instagram applications actively listening on these new ports.
About the _fbp cookie
According to Meta’s Cookies Policy, the
_fbp
cookie
identifies browsers for the purposes of providing advertising and site analytics
services and has a lifespan of 90 days
.
The cookie is present on approximately 25% of the top million websites, making it the 3rd
most common
first-party cookie of the web,
according
to Web Almanac 2024
.
A first-party cookie implies that it cannot be used to track users across web

data.title: Implementing a Forth
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了作者在学习和实现Forth语言过程中的经验和心得。Forth是一种基于堆栈的并发编程语言，作者通过几次尝试，包括移植现有的Forth版本（如JonesForth）和创建极小的Forth核心，深入了解了Forth和计算机的工作原理。文章提出了三点建议：首先，考虑移植现有的Forth实现，如JonesForth，以学习语言的内部机制；其次，尝试创建一个极小的Forth核心，探索其最小功能集；最后，作者分享了一些极小Forth实现的例子，如PlanckForth和SmithForth，并鼓励读者亲自实践。文章强调通过动手实践来理解编程语言的设计和实现。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Forth语言的实现、使用及其哲学

不同观点：
• **[timonoko]** 认为Forth和Lisp的问题在于，任何人都可以自由地改进语言，这可能削弱其在公司环境中的实用性，特别是在以固定流程和员工为主的公司。他提供了一个增强Forth可读性的示例，通过实现一个简单的解析器将类似Lisp的语法转换为Forth代码并执行。

• **[norir]** 认为Forth的核心哲学在于自力更生和构建适合特定任务的工具，而不是仅仅关注其汇编实现和分支、递归的处理方式。他强调Forth风格的编程类似于Unix管道，但更灵活，并提供了一个用Lua实现的简单线程执行模型示例。

• **[john-tells-all]** 推荐了《Threaded Interpretive Languages》一书，认为它清楚地描述了真实语言的内部结构及其实现方法，是学习Forth及相关语言的好资源。

• **[whobre]** 认为更多的人是在实现Forth，而不是使用它进行编程，暗示Forth在实际应用中的普及度可能不高。

• **[spelc]** 分享了自己自1981年以来使用Forth的经历，强调Forth虽然不再流行，但仍然有效。他指出，要写出一个好的Forth实现需要有一定的应用经验，并提到Forth可以用来编写大型应用程序，如140万行代码的应用程序。

• **[jshprentz]** 分享了自己在1979年受到Byte Magazine文章启发后实现Forth的经历，详细描述了如何在一个仅有4KB内存的计算机上实现一个Forth系统，并提到后续开发tinyForth的经历。

• **[s-macke]** 讨论了自己用Go语言实现Forth编译器的经历，强调Forth允许轻松创建和修改控制结构的特性，并提供了GitHub链接供人参考。

• **[fjfaase]** 正在开发一个基于栈的语言作为C编译器的中间语言，使用两个栈分别处理传统数据和局部变量，并提供了相关链接。

• **[acidx]** 实现了与Forth Haiku方言兼容的Forth，使用尾调用和连续传递调度方法，并进行了一些基本的优化，计划用于驱动LED矩阵和开发简单的片段着色器。

• **[blippage]** 分享了自己玩Forth并创建自己的Forth实现的经历，虽然觉得Forth很酷，但认为在实用性上几乎任何其他语言都比Forth好。

• **[codr7]** 提到自己最初的解释器是Forth衍生品，认为这是设计自己语言的好方法，并提供了一个GitHub链接，展示一个可以轻松转换为后缀的语言项目。

• **[firesteelrain]** 询问是否可以使用《Crafting Interpreters》一书作为指导来构建Forth解释器，暗示这本书可能是一个好的学习资源。

• **[vermilingua]** 提问是否可以用高级语言实现Forth作为学习练习，并对Forth讨论多集中在汇编实现上表示疑惑。

补充讨论：
• Forth语言的哲学和自定义工具的能力被多次提及，强调其自力更生和灵活性。
• 不同用户分享了各自实现Forth的经历和项目，提供了丰富的实践示例和资源链接。
• 关于Forth在现代编程中的实用性和学习价值的讨论，有人认为Forth虽然有趣但不如其他语言实用，也有人认为它是学习语言设计的好工具。

争议焦点：
• Forth在现代公司环境中的实用性以及与其他语言相比的优劣。

44142652.article_content:
Back to my Forth pages.
(Image of "Four-Armed Chuck" programming a PDP-11 is from my
giant write-up of Forth
.)
I’ve made a couple Forths. Not a single one of them are "finished software"
intended for industrial use, but
all
of them taught me something about Forth,
concatenative programming, and how computers work in general.
Sure, I’ve done my time in that place where points are free and the stacks
always need twiddling. But what about you?
You’re thinking about making a Forth yourself, aren’t you? Of course you are.
The call is irresistible. I know that.
The only thing holding you back is uncertainty.
You’re thinking, where do I start? How much Forth should I make? How do I know
when I’m done?
(Here, all of it, and you don’t.)
But here are three things to consider.
1. Consider porting an existing Forth
The first Forth I made was a port of JONESFORTH by Richard WM Jones. I found
it through…​
http://lambda-the-ultimate.org/node/2452
…​which lead me to…​
https://rwmj.wordpress.com/2010/08/07/jonesforth-git-repository/
(The links to annexia.org on that blog will likely time out, so either do
a search for "JonesForth mirror" on the web, or check out my
NasmJF repo
which also contains a complete copy.)
The output of my
nightly meditation
was
NasmJF
, a port of JonesForth to the NASM assembler.
The beauty of many Forths is that they contain a core Forth written in a host
language (or machine code) and then the rest of the language features are
implemented in…​Forth!
Knowing when I had completed my port was easy - I was done when
my ported assembly half of JonesForth could run the Forth half
of JonesForth.
Here’s the Forth half of JonesForth:
jonesforth.f
I think porting software is a pretty amazing way to learn
about a program and especially a language implementation. Here’s a card:
Porting Software
.
(At the moment, it’s somewhat redundant with the page you’re reading, but it
will probably get a lot more interesting when I do my next port, whatever that
ends up being. Hint: probably a Sed.)
2. Consider making an ultra-tiny Forth core
I think one of the most interesting questions in the Forth universe is
how small can its core be?
Which is to say, how few words do you need to
implement in a host language (or raw machine code, as we’ll see) before you can bootstrap
the rest of the language in the Forth itself?
Sadly (ha!), you can make a computer with just
one
instruction:
One-instruction set computer
(wikipedia.org).
(The most popular one I’ve seen is SUBLEQ, which stands for "SUBtract, branch
if Less than/EQual to zero". And since there’s only one, you typically omit it
and your program is just the operands for the implied instruction. The
"language", then, has
no
operations and feels to me like the computing
equivalent of John Cage’s musical stunt
4'33"
(wikipedia.org).)
So I guess a Forth with
one
word is all you need.
Therefore, it’s not a question of, "How few words would be
possible
?" but
rather, "How few words would be
interesting
?"
The answer will be personal to you.
The Forth-eV Wiki’s page on
"Minimal Word Set"
is a great place to start:
https://wiki.forth-ev.de/doku.php/en:words:kernel_embedded:minimum_word_set
In addition to the word set, you can also constrain the total file weight of your
core Forth. (Or lines of source or some other arbitrary limitation.)
Update:
As
Simon Meskens
(github.org) points out, the history of
small Forths may owe much to a particular source:
"…​so basically MilliForth was based on SectorForth, which was based on a Usenet thread where someone was trying to remember the work of Mikael Patel."
The work in question is
The Road Towards A Minimal Forth Architecture
(archive.org)
or
VÃ¤gen mot en minimal Forth arkitektur
(github.com).
Some really intriguing minimal Forths I’ve encountered:
PlanckForth
https://github.com/nineties/planckforth
I love the hexdump visualization of Koichi Nakamura’s PlanckForth:
You’re looking at a complete working Forth implementation in the form of a
hand-written ELF binary in less than 1,000 bytes. The rest of PlanckForth is
written in PlanckForth to implement a "normal" Forth.
SmithForth
https://dacvs.neocities.org/SF/
David Smith’s SmithForth is another 1,000 byte, hand-written machine code Forth
that bootstraps a more complete Forth.
"My goal with SmithForth is not to stop writing machine code early, but to
start writing Forth early."
I love tiny Forths!
sectorforth
https://github.com/cesarblum/sectorforth/
Cesar Blum’s sectorforth is even smaller, at 512 bytes (the size of a boot sector).
Like other ultra-tiny Forths, it starts with just a handful of Forth primitives
with which to bootstrap higher-level constructs.
The included
01-helloworld.f
example is 200 lines of well-commented Forth
source which starts with making numbers, implements a core of standard
Forth words, and then prints "Hello world".
I imagine this is how Ents talk.

data.author: arbesman
data.article_summary: 1993年，普林斯（Prince）将名字改为无法发音和打字的“爱符号”（The Love Symbol），以对抗其唱片公司华纳兄弟（Warner Bros.）。这一改名不仅让唱片公司头疼，也给媒体和公众带来了麻烦。为了解决无法印刷和书写其新名字的问题，普林斯制作了一个包含该符号的字体，并通过软盘和CompuServe发布给新闻机构。这个创意源于其设计团队的内部困扰，最终成功让主流音乐杂志采用了该字体。尽管普林斯后来对流媒体技术持怀疑态度，但在90年代初，他对新兴消费者技术非常感兴趣，显示出前瞻性思维。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对OpenAI的GPT-4模型在解决问题和推理能力上的评价及期望

不同观点：
• 第一种观点（MisterTea）：MisterTea对GPT-4的推理能力表示失望。他提到在尝试用GPT-4解决一个相对简单的问题时，模型表现不佳，给出了错误的答案，并且在提示后仍无法正确解决问题。他认为这显示出GPT-4在推理能力上的不足，并对其被认为是“最先进的AI”表示质疑。

• 第二种观点（反驳MisterTea的观点）：一些评论者认为MisterTea的个例不能代表GPT-4的整体能力。他们指出，GPT-4是一个基于统计的工具，可能在某些特定问题上表现不佳，但在其他方面可能表现出色。这些评论者强调，不能因为一次失败就全盘否定GPT-4的先进性，并建议在更多样化的任务上测试模型。

• 第三种观点（模型局限性）：有评论者同意MisterTea的部分观点，认为GPT-4确实在某些推理任务上存在局限性，尤其是需要深层次理解和逻辑推理的问题。他们提到，尽管GPT-4在语言理解和生成方面有显著进步，但仍不能与人类推理能力相媲美。

• 第四种观点（用户期望与现实）：一些评论者讨论了用户对GPT-4的高期望与实际能力之间的差距。他们认为，许多人可能对AI的能力有过高期望，而忽视了当前技术在实际应用中的局限性。这些评论者建议，应理性看待AI的能力，并在使用时考虑到其适用的范围和场景。

补充讨论：
• GPT-4的使用场景：有评论者提到，GPT-4在特定领域（如文本生成、翻译、摘要等）表现出色，但在需要复杂推理的任务上可能需要结合其他专门工具或人类干预。

• 改进建议：一些评论者建议OpenAI应继续改进模型的推理能力，尤其是在需要深层次理解和逻辑推理的领域，以满足用户对高性能AI的期望。

争议焦点：
• 争议的焦点在于GPT-4的推理能力是否如宣传所言“最先进”，以及个别失败案例是否能代表模型的整体能力。MisterTea的观点与一些评论者的反驳形成了明显的对立。

44192883.article_content:
In 1993, Prince frustrated contract lawyers and computer users everywhere when he changed his name to glyph known as “The Love Symbol.” Though he never said so explicitly, it’s generally understood that the name change was attempt to stick it to his record label, Warner Bros., which now had to deal with a top-tier artist with a new, unpronounceable, untypeable name. But it wasn’t just Warner Bros. that had a problem: The Love Symbol proved frustrating for people who wanted to both speak and write about Prince. Writers, editors, and layout designers at magazines and newspapers wouldn’t be able to type the actual name of the Artist Formerly Known As Prince. So Prince did the only thing you could do in that situation: He had a custom-designed font distributed to news outlets on a floppy
disk.
Here’s the floppy disk, from the collection of Anil Dash,
who’s written about it here
:
Added to my collection: 3.5" floppy given to press when Prince changed his name. Contains a font w/ one symbol in it.
pic.twitter.com/mNL0eOHDGI
— ଅନୀଲ (@anildash)
June 23, 2014
The Prince font substituted his symbol for what would otherwise be a capital P. In addition, the font was also made available for download on CompuServe. It was accompanied by a stern letter featuring both usage and installation instructions. (Graphix Zone, the company on the letterhead, released an interactive
CD
-
ROM
called
Prince Interactive
that same
year.)
For those asking, Prince font floppy is just a fun artifact; contents were on his CD-ROM & Compuserve 20 years ago.
pic.twitter.com/Mnzrvo64wQ
— ଅନୀଲ (@anildash)
June 23, 2014
The font idea, according to Chuck Hermes, who worked on the Paisley Park graphic-design team, came out of internal frustration. “
It just seemed like a logical thing to do,” Hermes told me over the phone today. “Everybody was having a hard time. He didn’t even want us to be calling him Prince in person. Part of it was, there was this glyph, this symbol that we didn’t know how to pronounce, and he wasn’t giving us any clues.
”
“
So we had to start communicating, we were just writing the symbol freehand,” he said. “It started out as we just did it for ourselves. We needed some way to be efficiently communicating with this name that we couldn’t type on a
keyboard.”
Steve Parke, who worked with Prince at the time, helped mail out the floppy disks. “He basically wanted people to start using that for his name in journalism,” Parke recalled, “and — I gotta be honest with you — I was like, ‘huh.’ I just remember when started I looking at those things I was like, ‘Really? I wonder how that’s gonna play
out.’”
It worked out pretty well. “I just remember maybe six months later,” Parke noted, “looking through
Rolling Stone
one time and seeing that symbol and I’m like, ‘Wow, that’s pretty impressive.’” After all, could any other artist convince a major music publication to integrate a custom
font?
“
How many people can just say ‘Hey, I’m changing my name to this symbol so can you use it from now on?’ and everyone’s like ‘Alright. Okay. No questions asked. You’re Prince! We’ll do it!’ It was kind of funny to
me.”
The move, catering to emerging technology in media, stands in contrast to Prince’s current reputation as a streaming-skeptical luddite and prolific issuer of takedown notices for his music on
YouTube.
“
I think he was very forward-thinking,” Parke remembered. “I think what happened a lot of time for him — not to be funny — he had an idea and the truth of the matter is the technology wasn’t quite there for what he
wanted.”
Hermes said that Prince, in the early ‘90s, was excited by consumer technology. “
I was working there and was kind of the first one to introduce him to bulletin-board systems and very early America Online back then. He was really engaged in all of this. We would spend hours every night. He’d come in and out of the studio and come into our offices just to experiment with graphics and Photoshop and all that software.” Unsurprisingly, Prince was thrilled at the possibility of being able to create art at such a rapid
clip.
But there were parts of the computer revolution that were still foreign to him. At least, until they were put in Prince’s own terms. “
I was talking about chat groups and chatting and meeting people online and he seemed confused by it,” Hermes reminisced. “Until I had told him I had met a girl. And that’s when he was able to go ‘Oh, I get it! I see where this could be useful.’
”

data.title: Extreme Super-Resolution via Scale Autoregression and Preference Alignment
data.author: Brajeshwar
data.article_summary: 文章提出了一种名为Chain-of-Zoom (CoZ) 的框架，用于解决单图像超分辨率（SISR）模型在极大倍率放大时效果崩溃的问题。CoZ通过将超分辨率分解为一系列中间尺度的自回归链，并结合多尺度感知提示，重复利用基础模型，实现无需额外训练的极端分辨率放大。此外，为弥补高倍放大时视觉线索的不足，CoZ在每步缩放中加入由视觉语言模型生成的多尺度感知文本提示，并通过广义奖励策略优化对其进行微调，以更好地符合人类偏好。实验表明，使用CoZ框架的4倍扩散模型可实现256倍以上的放大，同时保持高感知质量和保真度。

• [esafak] 提问是否有应用或服务实现了最新的升频算法，表明其对该技术的关注，可能在寻找实用工具来提升图像或视频质量。

• [PixelPerfect] 补充提到Waifu2x和Anime4K等开源项目，这些项目专注于图像和动画的升频，尤其在动漫风格图像上表现突出，指出这些工具适合不同类型的用户需求。

• [RealisticView] 持不同看法，认为尽管这些工具使用了最新的算法，但在实际应用中仍可能出现伪影或不自然的结果，尤其是对真实照片的处理，强调算法的局限性和进一步优化的必要性。

Title:
Chain-of-Zoom: Extreme Super-Resolution via Scale Autoregression and Preference Alignment
Authors:
Bryan Sangwoo Kim
,
Jeongsol Kim
,
Jong Chul Ye
View a PDF of the paper titled Chain-of-Zoom: Extreme Super-Resolution via Scale Autoregression and Preference Alignment, by Bryan Sangwoo Kim and 2 other authors
View PDF
Abstract:
Modern single-image super-resolution (SISR) models deliver photo-realistic results at the scale factors on which they are trained, but collapse when asked to magnify far beyond that regime. We address this scalability bottleneck with Chain-of-Zoom (CoZ), a model-agnostic framework that factorizes SISR into an autoregressive chain of intermediate scale-states with multi-scale-aware prompts. CoZ repeatedly re-uses a backbone SR model, decomposing the conditional probability into tractable sub-problems to achieve extreme resolutions without additional training. Because visual cues diminish at high magnifications, we augment each zoom step with multi-scale-aware text prompts generated by a vision-language model (VLM). The prompt extractor itself is fine-tuned using Generalized Reward Policy Optimization (GRPO) with a critic VLM, aligning text guidance towards human preference. Experiments show that a standard 4x diffusion SR model wrapped in CoZ attains beyond 256x enlargement with high perceptual quality and fidelity. Project Page:

data.title: FastHTML Best Practices
data.author: tosh
data.article_summary:
文章介绍了FastHTML应用与FastAPI、React、Django等框架的不同之处，强调其最佳实践应符合fast.ai的理念：简洁、利用智能默认设置、编写简明清晰的代码。文章通过多个示例展示了如何优化FastHTML代码：

1. **数据库表创建**：使用数据类风格定义，自动设置主键。
2. **路由命名约定**：使用`@rt`无参数修饰，函数名即为路由。
3. **查询参数优于路径参数**：查询参数更符合FastHTML习惯。
4. **利用返回值**：`insert()`和`update()`返回受影响对象，支持函数式链式调用。
5. **使用`.to()`生成URL**：类型安全且易于重构。
6. **默认使用PicoCSS**：自动样式，复杂UI可使用MonsterUI。
7. **智能默认设置**：如`Titled`自动包含`Container`。
8. **处理可迭代对象**：直接传递可迭代对象，无需解包。
9. **函数式模式**：使用`map()`替代列表推导式。
10. **最小化代码**：自说明代码无需多余注释，单行表达单一想法。
11. **使用POST进行所有变更**：FastHTML默认处理GET和POST。
12. **现代HTMX事件语法**：使用新的HTMX事件语法，支持短横线和双冒号的快捷方式。

这些实践帮助开发者编写更简洁、高效的FastHTML应用。

FastHTML applications are different to applications using FastAPI/react, Django, etc. Don’t assume that FastHTML best practices are the same as those for other frameworks. Best practices embody the fast.ai philosophy: remove ceremony, leverage smart defaults, and write code that’s both concise and clear. The following are some particular opportunities that both humans and language models sometimes miss:
Database Table Creation
Before:
todos
=
db.t.todos
if
not
todos.exists():
todos.create(
id
=
int
, task
=
str
, completed
=
bool
, created
=
str
, pk
=
'id'
)
After:
class
Todo:
id
:
int
;
task:
str
;
completed:
bool
;
created:
str
todos
=
db.create(Todo)
FastLite’s
create()
is idempotent - it creates the table if needed and returns the table object either way. Using a dataclass-style definition is cleaner and more Pythonic. The
id
field is automatically the primary key.
Route Naming Conventions
Before:
@rt
(
"/"
)
def
get():
return
Titled(
"Todo List"
, ...)
@rt
(
"/add"
)
def
post(task:
str
): ...
After:
@rt
def
index():
return
Titled(
"Todo List"
, ...)
# Special name for "/"
@rt
def
add(task:
str
): ...
# Function name becomes route
Use
@rt
without arguments and let the function name define the route. The special name
index
maps to
/
.
Query Parameters over Path Parameters
Before:
@rt
(
"/toggle/
{todo_id}
"
)
def
post(todo_id:
int
): ...
# URL: /toggle/123
After:
@rt
def
toggle(
id
:
int
): ...
# URL: /toggle?id=123
Query parameters are more idiomatic in FastHTML and avoid duplicating param names in the path.
Leverage Return Values
Before:
@rt
def
add(task:
str
):
new_todo
=
todos.insert(task
=
task, completed
=
False
, created
=
datetime.now().isoformat())
return
todo_item(todos[new_todo])
@rt
def
toggle(
id
:
int
):
todo
=
todos[
id
]
todos.update(completed
=
not
todo.completed,
id
=
id
)
return
todo_item(todos[
id
])
After:
@rt
def
add(task:
str
):
return
todo_item(todos.insert(task
=
task, completed
=
False
, created
=
datetime.now().isoformat()))
@rt
def
toggle(
id
:
int
):
return
todo_item(todos.update(completed
=
not
todos[
id
].completed,
id
=
id
))
Both
insert()
and
update()
return the affected object, enabling functional chaining.
Use
.to()
for URL Generation
Before:
hx_post
=
f"/toggle?id=
{
todo
.
id
}
"
After:
hx_post
=
toggle.to(
id
=
todo.
id
)
The
.to()
method generates URLs with type safety and is refactoring-friendly.
PicoCSS comes free
Before:
style
=
Style(
"""
.todo-container { max-width: 600px; margin: 0 auto; padding: 20px; }
/* ... many more lines ... */
"""
)
After:
# Just use semantic HTML - Pico styles it automatically
Container(...), Article(...), Card(...), Group(...)
fast_app()
includes PicoCSS by default. Use semantic HTML elements that Pico styles automatically. Use MonsterUI (like shadcn, but for FastHTML) for more complex UI needs.
Smart Defaults
Before:
return
Titled(
"Todo List"
, Container(...))
if
__name__
==
"__main__"
:
serve()
After:
return
Titled(
"Todo List"
, ...)
# Container is automatic
serve()
# No need for if __name__ guard
Titled
already wraps content in a
Container
, and
serve()
handles the main check internally.
FastHTML Handles Iterables
Before:
Section(
*
[todo_item(todo)
for
todo
in
all_todos],
id
=
"todo-list"
)
After:
Section(
map
(todo_item, all_todos),
id
=
"todo-list"
)
FastHTML components accept iterables directly - no need to unpack with
*
.
Functional Patterns
List comprehensions are great, but
map()
is often cleaner for simple transformations, especially when combined with FastHTML’s iterable handling.
Minimal Code
Before:
@rt
def
delete(
id
:
int
):
# Delete from database
todos.delete(
id
)
# Return empty response
return
""
After:
@rt
def
delete(
id
:
int
): todos.delete(
id
)
Skip comments when code is self-documenting
Don’t return empty strings -
None
is returned by default
Use a single line for a single idea.
Use POST for All Mutations
Before:
hx_delete
=
f"/delete?id=
{
todo
.
id
}
"
After:
hx_post
=
delete.to(
id
=
todo.
id
)
FastHTML routes handle only GET and POST by default. Using only these two verbs is more idiomatic and simpler.
Modern HTMX Event Syntax
Before:
hx_on
=
"htmx:afterRequest: this.reset()"
After:
hx_on__after_request
=
"this.reset()"
This works because:
hx-on="event: code"
is deprecated;
hx-on-event="code"
is preferred
FastHTML converts
_
to
-
(so
hx_on__after_request
becomes
hx-on--after-request
)
::
in HTMX can be used as a shortcut for
:htmx:
.
HTMX natively accepts
-
instead of
:
(so
-htmx-
works like
:htmx:
)
HTMX accepts e.g
after-request
as an alternative to camelCase
afterRequest
44192118.article_summary:
文章介绍了FastHTML应用与FastAPI、React、Django等框架的不同之处，强调其最佳实践应符合fast.ai的理念：简洁、利用智能默认设置、编写简明清晰的代码。文章通过多个示例展示了如何优化FastHTML代码：

1. **数据库表创建**：使用数据类风格定义，自动设置主键。
2. **路由命名约定**：使用`@rt`无参数修饰，函数名即为路由。
3. **查询参数优于路径参数**：查询参数更符合FastHTML习惯。
4. **利用返回值**：`insert()`和`update()`返回受影响对象，支持函数式链式调用。
5. **使用`.to()`生成URL**：类型安全且易于重构。
6. **默认使用PicoCSS**：自动样式，复杂UI可使用MonsterUI。
7. **智能默认设置**：如`Titled`自动包含`Container`。
8. **处理可迭代对象**：直接传递可迭代对象，无需解包。
9. **函数式模式**：使用`map()`替代列表推导式。
10. **最小化代码**：自说明代码无需多余注释，单行表达单一想法。
11. **使用POST进行所有变更**：FastHTML默认处理GET和POST。
12. **现代HTMX事件语法**：使用新的HTMX事件语法，支持短横线和双冒号的快捷方式。

这些实践帮助开发者编写更简洁、高效的FastHTML应用。

data.author: ingve

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何阅读小说以及小说的价值

不同观点：
• [nilirl] 认为帖子没有真正回答“如何阅读小说”的问题，而是更多地讨论了“为什么我认为小说有用”。帖子中提到的“替代学习”只是解释了小说的价值，而非具体的方法。此外，关于如何选择书籍的建议——选择能提供可识别的人类决策经验的书——虽然有帮助，但仍不是关于“如何阅读”的完整解答。

• [jihadjihad] 强调了某些小说（如《米德尔马契》和《荒凉山庄》）不仅刻画了角色的心理内在，还能够引导读者在不同层次的经验之间建立因果和联想联系。他还提到《卡拉马佐夫兄弟》在道德和心理深度上无与伦比。

• [ednite] 赞同跨经验层次思考的观点，并认为《堂吉诃德》是这种类型的原型。书中对角色内心冲突的描写，早在现代心理学之前就已经捕捉到了人类在变化世界中的困惑和挣扎。

• [daxfohl] 分享了个人阅读经验，表示《米德尔马契》是其最爱，但无法理解《浮士德》为何受到高度评价，即便读了两遍仍觉得只是陈腐的道德故事，猜测可能只有德语版本才有其独特的魅力。

• [crims0n] 强调阅读文学小说的 enriching 作用，并建议从音频书开始，尤其是 Jeremy Iron 朗读的《洛丽塔》，认为这能吸引任何人进入文学世界。

• [pickledoyster] 对帖子中提到的某位 CEO 每年阅读10本小说的说法表示怀疑，认为这可能是炫耀闲暇时间多、阅读不深入或者是夸大其词。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于帖子是否真正回答了“如何阅读小说”的问题，[nilirl] 认为没有，而其他评论者则在具体小说和阅读经验上进行了深入讨论。
• 个人阅读经验和喜好是讨论的重要部分，例如 [daxfohl] 对《浮士德》的负面评价和 [crims0n] 对《洛丽塔》的推崇。
• [pickledoyster] 的评论引入了对他人阅读习惯的质疑，增加了对“阅读量”和“阅读质量”的思考。

data.title: Sid Meier's Pirates – In-depth (2017)
data.author: benbreen
data.article_summary: 《Sid Meier's Pirates!》是一款由Sid Meier最初为Commodore 64开发的海盗题材游戏，后于1990年推出Amiga版本。该游戏结合了动作、冒险和模拟元素，玩家可在加勒比海地区自由探索、进行海战和城镇袭击，并根据个人目标体验不同的海盗生涯。Amiga版本以其独特的图形和玩法广受好评，甚至被误认为使用了64色模式，实际上是32色模式通过特殊技巧呈现丰富色彩。游戏提供了多个历史时期和特殊剧情供选择，并附有一本详尽的手册。虽然后续有重制版《Pirates! Gold》，但Amiga版本因其独特的魅力仍被玩家喜爱。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：玩家对《Pirates!》游戏的回顾与不同版本的体验

不同观点：
• [怀旧与个人经历] abcd_f 回忆起为了玩游戏在雪夜步行去图书馆借阅大地图的经历，强调了当时的无忧无虑和游戏带来的乐趣。DmitryOlshansky 则分享了在卡塔赫纳遭遇失败但通过技巧“致富”的游戏体验。
• [不同版本的评价] cosmicgadget 表示虽然没有玩过原版，但2004年重制版在当时以FPS为主的市场中表现出色。MarcusE1W 则对C64上的原版情有独钟，特别提到游戏让他了解了加勒比地理知识。
• [技术讨论] guidedlight 对原版游戏使用BASIC编程语言开发表示惊讶，而 dr_dshiv 则表示依然热爱原版的《文明》游戏。
• [游戏难度] bluefirebrand 认为《Pirates!》的难度设计有问题，成功后游戏难度迅速提升，导致游戏体验不佳。
• [历史与挑战] Daviey 回忆了在没有互联网时代玩游戏的挑战，特别提到没有搞清楚太阳高度测量器的用途。
• [艺术联想] esafak 将《Pirates!》Gold! 版本与巴赫及水彩画联系在一起，表达了对游戏氛围的独特感受。
• [高分攻略] vitesse_oblige 分享了在1980年代Mac版本中获得最高分的策略，强调了游戏记忆和技巧的重要性。

补充讨论：
• [社区与现代玩法] dclaw 提到了基于《Pirates!》的IRC游戏，鼓励仍在使用IRC的玩家尝试。
• [角色设计] kookamamie 提到了游戏中的角色设计，认为女孩形象像是主角的镜像修改版。
• [复刻版的发现] senectus1 表达了对原版游戏的怀旧，并惊讶于复刻版的存在。

争议焦点：
• 游戏难度设计的合理性是讨论中的一个争议点，部分玩家如 bluefirebrand 认为难度提升过快，影响了游戏体验，而其他玩家如 vitesse_oblige 则享受挑战并找到了应对策略。

这些观点展示了玩家对《Pirates!》的多样化体验和深刻记忆，涵盖了游戏的技术、难度、版本差异及个人情感等多个方面。

While there may be many games that we love and come back to time and again, how often do we appreciate the different versions of a game? We usually find ourselves playing the version we grew up with, perhaps even ignoring the best version in favor of nostalgia. If we had no prior experience with said game, we'll ignore the lesser looking versions, even if that might be the original, completely missing out on their charm. How often do we love a game so much that we want to experience as many versions as possible? Sid Meier's Pirates! (referred hereafter as Pirates) is a game I have to have for every system it supports, and I truly love all of the many ports and remakes of this game.
^Starting up the game and some options
The original Pirates came out in 1987, written by Sid Meier for the Commodore 64, using the BASIC programing language. The game received ports for just about every system imaginable at the time, and I could not characterize any of them as "straight ports". They were all quite unique for each system, and indeed this Amiga version, released a few years later in 1990, is an obvious loving port. It was rewritten for the Amiga in-house at MicroProse USA, another example of a fine American Amiga product that the European Amiga scene these days almost refuse to acknowledge.
The ports based off the original Pirates peek with this Amiga version. The game is so beautiful that some magazines falsely claimed the game used 64 color Extra Half Bright Mode. I tested this out by taking actual screen captures from my Amiga, and found the game was always in a 320x200 32 color mode. However, there are certain screens like the title that do not capture quite right using my screen capture program, seemingly missing colors. Rather than use EHB mode I believe they were manipulating certain areas of the screen in order for some areas to get a fresh 32 color palette, a practice used in several games to pull off hundreds of colors on the Amiga. When the game was remade in the mid-90's as Pirates! Gold for several platforms, it could be debated on if even that version looked better than this.
^Descriptions of various time periods from the manual
Upon loading, the game offers you several choices of play. You can dive straight into the game, which will automatically put you into the 1660's, the most prosperous pirating period. You can select from several other periods of time as well, offering a range of different challenges and situations. Finally you can partake in several special scenarios involving historical events with actual pirates. The manual is a tremendous resource for information regarding these time periods,  and an overall excellent read at nearly 100 pages. While the game is fairly intuitive on its own, I do believe people will be missing out if they ignore the top notch manual.
^The game usually starts you off at a "lovely seaside town"
Pirates was made during a time when a game could defy characterization. This is a truly unique game in its own genre. The cover of the manual describes it as the "action adventure simulation" and the worlds first swashbuckling simulation. Microprose was already famous for their simulations at this point. While the game successfully combines quite a few categories together, simulation might be the least of these. The manual itself more than makes up for a game that is largely the Hollywood tale of the pirating life, but indeed the game itself is taking you on an adventure of the best movie elements of that life, not simulating the actual truth of the life. There's plenty of action elements here, including a very fun sword fighting sequence, but there's even strategy elements during the various ship and town attack sequences.
^The Caribbean, finding our way using the sun, and attacking a ship
It's an open ended game during a time when those games did not exist, originally being released before SimCity had been. You decide your goals with this game. There is eventually an ending in retirement, which age will force upon you at some point, and even a high score, but there's nothing but personal goals for you to achieve before you reach that ending. Retire in the first town you come across if you want, game over. The later Pirates Gold remake would attempt to steer you toward some goals in the form of listed quests, but all of those quests can be completed (or not) right here in the original game. You decide how to have your fun with Pirates.
^Swordplay on ship and sinking one
During the 1660's you could have quite a successful career privateering for various countries aga
44142343.article_summary: 《Sid Meier's Pirates!》是一款由Sid Meier最初为Commodore 64开发的海盗题材游戏，后于1990年推出Amiga版本。该游戏结合了动作、冒险和模拟元素，玩家可在加勒比海地区自由探索、进行海战和城镇袭击，并根据个人目标体验不同的海盗生涯。Amiga版本以其独特的图形和玩法广受好评，甚至被误认为使用了64色模式，实际上是32色模式通过特殊技巧呈现丰富色彩。游戏提供了多个历史时期和特殊剧情供选择，并附有一本详尽的手册。虽然后续有重制版《Pirates! Gold》，但Amiga版本因其独特的魅力仍被玩家喜爱。

Claude Composer CLI
A tool for enhancing Claude Code
What is Claude Composer?
Claude Composer is a CLI wrapper for Claude Code that adds small enhancements around automation, UX, and configuration.
Reduced interruptions
: Automatically handles permission dialogs based on configurable rules
Flexible control
: Rulesets let you define exactly which actions to allow automatically
Tool management
: Toolsets simplify configuring which tools Claude can use
Enhanced visibility
: System notifications keep you informed without switching contexts
Table of Contents
Features
Quick Start
Installation
Basic Usage
What is Claude Composer?
Installation & Setup
Prerequisites
Installation

Basic Usage
Command Structure
Common Workflows

Configuration File Locations

What are Rulesets?
Internal Rulesets

Creating Custom Rulesets

Quick Start
Installation
npm install -g claude-composer
#
or
yarn global add claude-composer

or

Basic Usage
#
Initialize global configuration
claude-composer cc-init
#
Start Claude Code with automatic dialog dismissal
claude-composer
#
Uses the ruleset configured during cc-init
#
Use a more permissive ruleset
claude-composer --ruleset internal:yolo
Installation & Setup
See
docs/installation.md
for detailed installation instructions.
Prerequisites
Node.js 18 or higher
npm, yarn, or pnpm package manager
Claude Code installed and configured
Installation
Install Claude Composer globally:
pnpm add -g claude-composer
Or with other package managers:
yarn global add claude-composer
npm install -g claude-composer
Initial Configuration
Run
claude-composer cc-init
to create your initial configuration:
#
Create global configuration (default)
claude-composer cc-init
#
Or create project-specific configuration
claude-composer cc-init --project
Global Configuration
By default,
claude-composer cc-init
creates a global configuration that applies to all projects:
Configuration location:
~/.claude-composer/config.yaml
Interactive prompts for ruleset and toolset selection
Applies to all Claude Composer invocations unless overridden
Project Configuration
Use
claude-composer cc-init --project
to create a project-specific configuration:
Creates
.claude-composer/config.yaml
in current directory
Takes precedence over global configuration when present
Ideal for project-specific rules and tool settings
Directory Structure
Global configuration:
~/.claude-composer/
├── config.yaml          # Global configuration
├── rulesets/           # Custom global rulesets (unprefixed)
│   ├── my-workflow.yaml
│   └── backend-dev.yaml
└── toolsets/           # Custom global toolsets (unprefixed)
├── my-tools.yaml
└── web-dev.yaml
Project configuration (with
--project
):
your-project/
├── .claude-composer/
│   ├── config.yaml     # Project configuration
│   ├── rulesets/       # Custom project rulesets
│   └── toolsets/       # Custom project toolsets
└── ... (your project files)
Basic Usage
Command Structure
claude-composer [claude-composer-options] [claude-code-args]
Claude Composer acts as a wrapper around Claude Code, passing through all supported arguments to Claude Code.
Common Workflows
Using Configuration Files
#
Use global configuration
claude-composer
#
Use project configuration (if present)
cd
your-project
claude-composer
#
Override with specific ruleset
claude-composer --ruleset internal:safe
Passing Arguments to Claude Code
#
Pass model selection to Claude Code
claude-composer --model claude-3-opus-20240229
#
Combine composer options with Claude Code args
claude-composer --ruleset internal:yolo --model claude-3-opus-20240229
Working with Different Rulesets
#
Safe mode - all dialogs require confirmation
claude-composer --ruleset internal:safe
#
Cautious mode - auto-accept project-level operations

data.title: Tokasaurus: An LLM Inference Engine for High-Throughput Workloads
data.author: rsehrlich
data.article_summary: Tokasaurus是斯坦福大学研究团队推出的一种新型LLM推理引擎，专为高吞吐量工作负载优化。对于小模型，Tokasaurus通过极低的CPU开销和动态前缀分组（Hydragen）来提升效率，尤其在共享前缀场景中表现优异。对于大模型，引擎支持GPU的异步张量并行和无NVLink情况下的快速流水线并行。在吞吐量基准测试中，Tokasaurus的性能比vLLM和SGLang高出3倍以上。引擎通过异步和自适应管理任务，减少CPU瓶颈，并有效处理前缀共享，从而大幅提升推理速度。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕自托管模型推理引擎（特别是Tokasaurus和Ollama）的性能、实现和应用的讨论。

不同观点：
• **symbolicAGI**：认为llama.cpp仍是自托管模型的最佳选择，尤其在低延迟需求下，无论是否支持GPU。同时指出Ollama在包装llama.cpp方面处于领先地位。虽然Tokasaurus的GitHub页面曾消失，但现在已恢复。

• **refibrillator**：对Tokasaurus的代码实现表示赞赏，尤其对其纯Python实现能够超越vLLM和SGLang表示惊讶。同时提到动态形状处理仍是一个挑战，并计划深入研究Tokasaurus的实现方法。

• **nabakin**：指出Tokasaurus虽然在某些吞吐量基准测试中表现优异，但没有与TensorRT-LLM的吞吐量数据进行比较，后者目前在开源领域处于领先地位。

• **behnamoh**：认为Tokasaurus的异步张量并行机制对于常见用例来说过于复杂，CPU开销高，且需要NVLink连接的GPU才能看到实际效益。对于大多数生产部署来说， simpler approaches可能更合适，除非专门优化大规模批量吞吐量。同时对自适应管理器在负载下跳过“可选”任务表示担忧，认为可能影响可靠性。

• **radq**：对Tokasaurus项目表示赞赏，认为其代码库简单且文档良好，是实现高性能推理引擎的良好起点，尤其在批量推理生成RL rollouts方面非常相关。

• **AStonesThrow**：以幽默方式讨论Tokasaurus的命名和可能的非正式使用，并提到与Meta AI/Llama 4的潜在应用，以创意方式描述图像生成需求。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于Tokasaurus的复杂性和实际应用效益。behnamoh认为其复杂性在多数场景下不必要，而其他评论者则对其性能和技术实现表示赞赏。
• 对Tokasaurus与TensorRT-LLM的比较也是一个讨论点，nabakin指出前者在吞吐量方面的领先地位未与后者直接对比。
• 对Tokasaurus代码实现的细节（如动态形状处理、代码注释）也有一定讨论，显示出技术社区对其技术实现的关注。

Tokasaurus: An LLM Inference Engine for High-Throughput Workloads

Stanford
TL;DR
We’re releasing Tokasaurus, a new LLM inference engine optimized for throughput-intensive workloads. With small models, Tokasaurus benefits from very low CPU overhead and dynamic
Hydragen
grouping to exploit shared prefixes. For larger models, Tokasaurus supports async tensor parallelism for GPUs with NVLink and a fast implementation of pipeline parallelism for GPUs without. On throughput-focused benchmarks, Tokasaurus can outperform vLLM and SGLang by up to 3x+.
Table of Contents
Intro
Optimizing Small Models
Optimizing Big Models
Try it Out
Benchmarking Details
Acknowledgements
Intro
As LLMs get
smarter, faster, and cheaper,
the community keeps finding new ways to use them. Our own recent work has explored using models to
scan every file in a codebase
,
sample 10,000 attempts for math and code problems
, and
collaborate with other models to minimize cloud costs
. Inference is now also an important part of the training process, where we use models to
generate synthetic data
or as part of
RL pipelines
that generate and train on model completions.
Crucially, these new inference workloads look quite different than the original LLM use case of serving a chatbot. Here, we care primarily about the total time and cost required to complete a large batch of sequences, and we care much less (if at all) about the individual latency of a single generation. In other words, we want high throughput!
Open-source inference engines (i.e. dedicated systems for running efficient LLM inference) like
FlexGen
,
vLLM
, and
SGLang
have been enormously valuable to the community. Inspired by and learning from these projects, we built a new engine,
Tokasaurus
, designed from the ground up to handle throughput-focused workloads. We’ve optimized Tokasaurus for efficiently serving large and small models alike, allowing it to outperform existing engines on throughput benchmarks. In the rest of this blog, we’ll walk through some of these optimizations and show off a few settings where Tokasaurus really shines.
Optimizing Small Models
To benchmark Tokasaurus with small models, we’ll use two workloads:
Completing chatbot prompts from the ShareGPT dataset (this is a common benchmark for testing inference engines).
Reproducing an experiment from
Large Language Monkeys
, where we take 128 problems from the
GSM8K
math dataset and sample 1024 answers to every problem. The distinguishing feature of this workload is that there’s a lot of prefix sharing across sequences.
Tokasaurus outperforms vLLM and SGLang on both of these benchmarks, in particular achieving over 2x the throughput of other engines on the Large Language Monkeys workload. Two main features contribute to these wins with small models:
Minimizing CPU Overhead
LLM engines perform many different tasks on the CPU, like handling web requests, tokenizing inputs/detokenizing outputs, managing KV cache allocation, and preparing inputs for the model. If these CPU-side tasks cause the GPU-side model to stall, throughput can take a
big hit
. To avoid these stalls, inference engines commonly make many CPU-side
tasks
asynchronous
: while the GPU runs a forward pass for batch N, the CPU-side of the engine post-processes the results from batch N-1 and prepares the inputs for batch N+1.
Tokasaurus goes one step further, making the CPU-side of the engine (what we call the manager) both asynchronous and adaptive. The manager’s goal is to maintain a deep queue of inputs for the model to run forward passes on. The manager monitors the size of this queue and can detect if the model is close to exhausting it (and therefore stalling the GPU). In these cases, the manager will automatically start skipping optional steps (like checking for stop strings and onboarding new sequences) until the model’s input queue is sufficiently deep again. This combination of asynchrony and adaptivity lets Tokasaurus serve small models with much less CPU overhead.

Prefix sharing comes up all the time in LLM inference — not just when repeatedly sampling like in the Large Language Monkeys benchmark, but also when asking many questions about a long document or reusing a system prompt across many chatbot conversations.
Shared prefixes allow attention to be computed more efficiently. We first explored this idea last year with
Hydragen
(aka
cascade attention
and
bifurcated attention

44195961.article_summary: Tokasaurus是斯坦福大学研究团队推出的一种新型LLM推理引擎，专为高吞吐量工作负载优化。对于小模型，Tokasaurus通过极低的CPU开销和动态前缀分组（Hydragen）来提升效率，尤其在共享前缀场景中表现优异。对于大模型，引擎支持GPU的异步张量并行和无NVLink情况下的快速流水线并行。在吞吐量基准测试中，Tokasaurus的性能比vLLM和SGLang高出3倍以上。引擎通过异步和自适应管理任务，减少CPU瓶颈，并有效处理前缀共享，从而大幅提升推理速度。

• **nabakin**：指出Tokasaurus虽然在某些吞吐量基准测试中表现优异，但没有与TensorRT-LLM的吞吐量数据进行比较，后者目前在开源领域处于领先地位。

data.title: I do not remember my life and it's fine
data.author: mrcgnc
data.article_summary: Marco Giancotti在这篇文章中讨论了**aphantasia**（心盲症）和**SDAM**（严重自传体记忆缺陷），解释了这些状况如何影响他的记忆和回忆能力。尽管他无法在脑海中形成图像或声音，并且难以“重温”过去的事件，但这并未给他的生活带来明显障碍。他指出，aphantasia并非一种障碍，而SDAM则是一种新近发现的症状，与aphantasia有密切关联。Giancotti描述了自己在回忆特定事件时的困难，例如在求职时难以回答关于过去经历的问题，以及在祖父去世后难以回忆与祖父相关的具体记忆。他强调，他的记忆像是一个没有标签的文件柜，只能通过特定的线索进行回忆。尽管如此，他并不认为自己处于劣势，只是主观体验与常人有所不同。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：记忆、心理意象和自我认知的挑战

不同观点：
• [OptionOfT] 认为在“推销自己”时，如面试或自我评估中，难以回忆和描述自己解决过的难题，直到有人指出其成就。该用户怀疑这与ADHD有关，感觉像自己只是自己思维的旁观者。
• [aidenn0] 分享了自己可能有轻度面孔失认症（face-blindness）的经历，在意外场合遇到不熟悉的人时很难认出对方，但通过重复和努力可以改善。
• [andoando] 认为对于没有事先准备的人来说，回忆大学期间面对困难问题并如何克服是困难的，因为人们通常不会以这种结构化的方式来概念化事件。
• [mkfs] 指出心理意象的清晰度被高估，引用“画一辆自行车”实验来说明人们在记忆和视觉化复杂物体时的困难，并提到目击者证词的不准确性。
• [dgreensp] 描述了遇到SDAM（自传体记忆缺陷障碍）的人，他们没有“第一人称”记忆，无法回忆起自己亲身经历的事情，只能通过零散的样本记忆来回想生活片段。

补充讨论：
• [awkii] 表示自己有aphantasia（心理视觉化障碍）和SDAM，认为这使他们更容易原谅别人，因为不会反复回想受伤的经历。
• [gchamonlive] 能够轻松在脑海中创建图像，但认为这对保存记忆并不特别有帮助，记忆多是灰色的模糊片段，通过写日记和从朋友那里收集记忆来弥补。
• [philsnow] 分享了与SDAM相关的经历，通过照片来触发记忆，并提到失去与过去物件的联系可能切断对记忆的有限访问，特别是与已故妻子的记忆。
• [lll-o-lll] 认为SDAM是负面影响更多，难以感受时间的流逝和计划未来，看着孩子的照片却无法回忆他们小时候的时光令人悲伤。
• [apothegm] 提到自己缺乏对非情绪化事件的 episodic memory，但 semantic memory 和空间感很强，视觉化能力很模糊。
• [haswell] 有aphantasia和糟糕的自传体记忆，可能有SDAM，认为这既是祝福也是诅咒，特别是在处理复杂PTSD和未处理的创伤时。
• [kevinsync] 经历了一段时间没有梦境和视觉化能力，后来又有 vivid dreams，认为这种体验是流动的，并好奇哪些因素会影响其强度。
• [lukeholder] 认为没有人拥有完美的记忆，记忆的存储和提取是自然选择的结果，不认为每个人都有数据库般的记忆系统。
• [VonTum] 描述了自己类似SDAM的经历，容易忘记餐厅名称或人名，认为这是主要缺点，只有在特定地点或情境下记忆才会涌现。
• [screaminghawk] 提到自己在视觉记忆和第一人称记忆方面有类似问题，难以在回忆过去事件时重新体验当时的情感，只能通过事实重建。

争议焦点：
• 不同用户对记忆的可访问性和视觉化能力的体验差异较大，有些人认为这是障碍，而另一些人则认为有其优势。
• 对于aphantasia和SDAM是否是祝福或诅咒存在不同看法，一些人认为它们使生活更轻松，而另一些人则认为这是重大缺陷。

I Do Not Remember My Life and It's Fine
What reminiscing is like without mental imagery
Marco Giancotti
,
June	5, 2025
Marco Giancotti
,
June	5, 2025
Cover image:
Caravane Au Coucher Du Soleil, Charles Théodore Frère
This post is part of the
List of Introspective Descriptions
.
I've
written
about
aphantasia
several
times
before
on this blog, and many people have shown interest in the topic. Most readers are simply curious when I say that I can't form any kind of image, sound, or other sensation in my mind. Occasionally, someone shows pity or commiseration towards me, as if I were in constant, daily suffering from a crippling disability. Nothing could be further from the truth, of course. I've been successful at most of what I've tried to accomplish in my life until now, and never had to battle with a sense of being disadvantaged. On top of that, even aphantasia experts generally agree that
it is not a disorder
.
That is not to say that I feel as capable as anyone else at everything. In particular, there is an area in which I
do
feel—all too well—that I am weaker than most: my memory of past episodes.
For obvious reasons, my recollections lack a visual component, but that is only part of the story. I seem to have an extremely poor ability to "relive" past events mentally. In fact, my condition is accurately described as
a mnemonic syndrome that is confined to an inability to mentally travel backwards in time in the absence of detectable neuropathology or significant daily handicap,
which is the definition of a trait called SDAM, for
Severely Deficient Autobiographical Memory
.
SDAM was only
discovered
in 2015, and it is still poorly understood. Yet there is mounting evidence that it has deep links with aphantasia: about half of the people with SDAM also
report
having aphantasia, and many people with aphantasia claim to have difficulties with recalling past episodes from their own lives. For these reasons, I believe I have SDAM or something closely resembling it.
What does that imply, though? That is what I aim to clarify with this post. I always find it very difficult to tell how much of my subjective experience is rare and how much of it is normal for most of humanity. I've never swapped brains with anyone to find out. The only solution
I've found
is to try my best at explaining what the inner experience is like for me, and hope to receive comments from readers who have similar—or entirely different—experiences.
Below are some brief observations about the way my episodic memory works, based on notes I took over the past couple of years.
Recalling Specific Episodes
When I was looking for my first job, a Japanese company I applied to had me fill in a screening questionnaire. One question was something along these lines: "Write about a time during your university studies in which you faced a difficult problem, and what you did to overcome it." A perfectly reasonable question to ask a potential recruit with no employment history, but an impossibly hard question for me to answer.
I was completely stumped. In my university years, I worked on many research projects, and it wasn't always easy. I
knew
I had faced various kinds of problems during my graduate studies, and I assumed I had overcome them all before getting my degree. Why couldn't I come up with a single example?
This was the first time I noticed that something was off. Those questions about relevant episodes are pretty standard in certain industries, and I had never heard anyone complain about them specifically. Yet they were anathema for me.
Original photo by Jan Antonin Kolar, Unsplash (modified)
My memory feels like a file cabinet without labels, a database without an index, a dictionary of randomly-ordered words without a table of contents. There are many memories there, but most of them can't be retrieved with convenient keywords like "a time when X happened".
Only with very specific cues and external help am I able to, sometimes, recall the events I'm looking for. In the case of the job application questionnaire, I struggled with it for several days, asked a friend for advice, and eventually managed to put together a lame but passable answer based on my research notes. Still, I was left with the nagging feeling that more fitting and relevant examples remained buried away in my psyche, somewhere out of reach.
I felt the same limitation very strongly again last year, when my grandfather passed away. I determined to sit down and write everything I could remember about him, and my relationship with him. I went back in my mind to his house in the Roman countryside and wrote things as they came to me.
He was kind and jovial with us grandchildren. He often involved us in making bread and pizza together in his stone oven, and I liked that. I could even write a general visual description (not by putting into words what I saw in my mind at the time of writing, but by recalling what I "knew" about his looks). And so on, I could muster a good number of generic

data.title: APL Interpreter – An implementation of APL, written in Haskell (2024)
data.author: ofalkaed
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了作者开发APL解释器的经历和心得。APL是一种数组编程语言，其语法紧凑且富有表达力，使用独特的Unicode符号。作者通过解决Advent of Code问题展示了APL代码示例，强调其高度抽象和不同的思维方式。作者原本计划深入研究APL，但在过程中学习了Haskell，并发现Haskell并不是实现数组语言解释器的理想工具，因为其在状态处理和数据结构方面较为复杂。

文章还详细描述了解释器的工作流程：读取输入、词法分析、语法解析、评估语法树和输出结果。作者选择自行编写解析器，以更好地理解其工作原理，并通过多次重构优化了代码。尽管该项目不以实用为目的，但通过这个过程，作者对编程有了更深的理解。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕APL和Haskell两种编程语言的风格、使用体验及其相关技术问题的讨论。

不同观点：
• **APL语言的多样化风格**：[xelxebar]指出APL语言支持多种编程风格，包括声明式、命令式、面向对象和数据并行等风格，并提到不同风格在不同环境中的应用。例如，函数组合和无点表达式在APL爱好者中很流行，而在生产系统中更常见的是命令式和面向对象的风格。

• **Haskell中的异常处理和类型系统**：[valcron1000]对[xelxebar]关于Haskell的评论进行了补充，强调了Haskell中同步异常和不精确异常的区别，并指出了类型系统在异常处理中的重要性。他认为同步异常不能由纯代码抛出，而IO代码则可以抛出和捕获各种异常。

• **APL与Unicode的历史**：[0xTJ]指出虽然现代APL使用Unicode符号，但早期APL并没有使用Unicode，因为APL的出现早于Unicode标准的制定。

• **APL实现的可读性**：[howerj]询问是否存在用可读的C语言实现的、代码行数在1000行左右的APL或其他数组语言的实现，类似于LISP、FORTH和Prolog等语言的实现。

• **Haskell的学习和开发体验**：[nickzelei]分享了自己尝试学习Haskell的经历，指出相比现代语言如Go和Rust，Haskell的安装和构建系统显得不够友好，并寻求成功学习Haskell的指导。

• **Haskell的性能优化问题**：[instig007]对[xelxebar]关于Haskell性能的评论进行了回应，认为使用不当的函数如`foldl`会导致性能问题，而不是语言本身的问题。

补充讨论：
• **Haskell与Raku（Perl6）的关联**：[librasteve]提到Raku的第一个解析器是用Haskell编写的，并且Raku团队在开始项目之前都学习了Haskell。

• **个性类型与语言选择**：[behnamoh]认为Haskell可能对不同个性类型的人有不同的吸引力，取决于他们是完美主义者还是实用主义者。

争议焦点：
• **Haskell的异常处理和性能优化**：在Haskell中处理异常的最佳实践以及性能优化问题上存在不同看法。例如，[valcron1000]强调了类型系统的重要性，而[instig007]则认为代码实现不当是性能问题的主要原因。

As you might expect, learning to write programs like this
3
requires a totally different mind-set.
Array programming is similar to functional programming – the primary way to control execution involves composition of functions – but APL tends to encourage the reliance on global properties and sweeping operations rather than low-level recursion
4
.
I’d like to think that learning to approach problems this way provides greater insights for programming in general.
Why Haskell?
I originally planned this project to be a deep-dive into APL, and learning Haskell was more of a side-quest.
It ended up the other way around: the hardest aspect of this project, by far, was learning work with Haskell
5
.
In all honesty, Haskell probably isn’t an ideal tool for an array-language interpreter:
it makes parsing and combination of functions much more elegant, but at the expense of
ease of working with state, data structures, and performance.
As a result, this project isn’t intended to be especially practically useful, nor to be a replacement for existing interpreters.
The Big Picture
The program at large works exactly how you would expect any interpreter to work.
Read Text As Input
Convert Raw Text to Tokens (Lexing/Scanning)
Convert Token Stream Into Syntax Tree (Parsing)
Evaluate the parsed tree
Print the result
Repeat
The interpreter state (a mapping from variable names to values) is read/updated throughout.
Parsing
Haskell has some powerful parsing libraries, but I decided to write my parser from scratch, partly to make sure I really understood what the code was doing, and partly because I was scared off by the type signatures
6
of said libraries.
I initially attempted to write the parser in a similar style to those in my
other
projects
, but was forced into using a series of helper “match-functions” to translate the imperative code into a functional style.
Then, through a series of refactors, the majority of those helpers dissolved into calls to standard Haskell functions, resulting in syntax very similar to the aforementioned parsing libraries.

The core unit of logic in the parser if the
MatchFn

44195931.article_summary:
本文介绍了作者开发APL解释器的经历和心得。APL是一种数组编程语言，其语法紧凑且富有表达力，使用独特的Unicode符号。作者通过解决Advent of Code问题展示了APL代码示例，强调其高度抽象和不同的思维方式。作者原本计划深入研究APL，但在过程中学习了Haskell，并发现Haskell并不是实现数组语言解释器的理想工具，因为其在状态处理和数据结构方面较为复杂。

文章还详细描述了解释器的工作流程：读取输入、词法分析、语法解析、评估语法树和输出结果。作者选择自行编写解析器，以更好地理解其工作原理，并通过多次重构优化了代码。尽管该项目不以实用为目的，但通过这个过程，作者对编程有了更深的理解。
44195931.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕APL和Haskell两种编程语言的风格、使用体验及其相关技术问题的讨论。

不同观点：
• **APL语言的多样化风格**：[xelxebar]指出APL语言支持多种编程风格，包括声明式、命令式、面向对象和数据并行等风格，并提到不同风格在不同环境中的应用。例如，函数组合和无点表达式在APL爱好者中很流行，而在生产系统中更常见的是命令式和面向对象的风格。

• **Haskell中的异常处理和类型系统**：[valcron1000]对[xelxebar]关于Haskell的评论进行了补充，强调了Haskell中同步异常和不精确异常的区别，并指出了类型系统在异常处理中的重要性。他认为同步异常不能由纯代码抛出，而IO代码则可以抛出和捕获各种异常。

• **APL与Unicode的历史**：[0xTJ]指出虽然现代APL使用Unicode符号，但早期APL并没有使用Unicode，因为APL的出现早于Unicode标准的制定。

• **APL实现的可读性**：[howerj]询问是否存在用可读的C语言实现的、代码行数在1000行左右的APL或其他数组语言的实现，类似于LISP、FORTH和Prolog等语言的实现。

• **Haskell的学习和开发体验**：[nickzelei]分享了自己尝试学习Haskell的经历，指出相比现代语言如Go和Rust，Haskell的安装和构建系统显得不够友好，并寻求成功学习Haskell的指导。

• **Haskell的性能优化问题**：[instig007]对[xelxebar]关于Haskell性能的评论进行了回应，认为使用不当的函数如`foldl`会导致性能问题，而不是语言本身的问题。

补充讨论：
• **Haskell与Raku（Perl6）的关联**：[librasteve]提到Raku的第一个解析器是用Haskell编写的，并且Raku团队在开始项目之前都学习了Haskell。

• **个性类型与语言选择**：[behnamoh]认为Haskell可能对不同个性类型的人有不同的吸引力，取决于他们是完美主义者还是实用主义者。

争议焦点：
• **Haskell的异常处理和性能优化**：在Haskell中处理异常的最佳实践以及性能优化问题上存在不同看法。例如，[valcron1000]强调了类型系统的重要性，而[instig007]则认为代码实现不当是性能问题的主要原因。

data.title: Machine Learning: The Native Language of Biology
data.author: us-merul
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：机器学习（ML）与传统统计模型在生物学领域的应用及其优劣比较

不同观点：
• **支持机器学习在生物学中的应用**：
  - **dmacfour**：认为统计学界过度依赖数据模型，导致忽略了许多实际问题。机器学习提供了一种更灵活且信息丰富的替代方法，尤其适用于复杂的大数据集。
  - **mfld**：赞同文章的观点，认为经典的功能分类方法在解释实验数据时往往不足，而预测生物学方法尤其是机器学习提供了新的路径。
  - **anikozx**：认为文章启发性强，机器学习与生物学的结合可能带来新的研究方向和重大突破。

• **质疑机器学习在生物学中的普适性和优越性**：
  - **LeonardoTolstoy**：指出并不是所有生物学领域都适合采用机器学习。许多领域由于数据不足，需要机制和功能的理解，而非仅仅依赖数据驱动的分析。
  - **Perenti**：质疑文章中对Lotka-Volterra模型的描述，认为其并未准确反映历史验证情况。
  - **randcraw**：认为文章夸大其词，缺乏具体例子支持机器学习比传统统计模型更优越的观点。
  - **bglazer**：指出机器学习框架在预测失败时的应对不足，且未考虑物理和因果关系等因素，认为盲目追求测试集准确性可能导致误入歧途。

• **对机器学习的批评和保留态度**：
  - **suddenlybananas**：认为科学的核心在于解释而不仅是预测，强调机器学习在解释生物学现象方面的不足。
  - **piombisallow**：对文章的自比伽利略表示不满，要求提供具体预测成功的例子。
  - **barbarr**：认为文章声称机器学习方法优于传统数学公式，但缺乏具体证据支持。
  - **bigyabai**：指出机器学习是计算机的自然语言，但未必适合生物学，批评文章作者的抽象理解可能存在偏差。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及的**具体例子和论据**包括：
  - **Lotka-Volterra模型的误用**：Perenti指出其被错误用于描述时尚周期而非捕食者-猎物动态。
  - **机器学习在实际应用中的局限性**：bglazer强调预测失败时的应对策略不足，以及缺乏对测量数据类型的深入思考。
  - **不同领域的适用性**：LeonardoTolstoy提到高数据丰度领域适合机器学习，而数据不足的领域仍需传统方法。

• **争议焦点**：
  - 机器学习是否在所有生物学领域中都优于传统统计模型。
  - 文章中对机器学习优越性的声称是否得到了充分的证据支持。
  - 科学的核心目标是预测还是解释，机器学习在解释生物现象方面的能力如何。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于人工智能代理（agent）在遇到不确定问题时的处理方式以及其局限性

不同观点：
• superb_dev指出网站在手机上的显示问题，左侧内容被裁剪且无法滚动查看，属于技术实现上的用户体验问题。
• loloquwowndueo描述了一个循环场景：AI通过“请求人类服务”的机制获取帮助，但由于供不应求，最终AI自己填补这一角色，形成了机器请求机器的闭环。
• mgraczyk建议在规则中添加直接询问人类的方式来解决代理不确定问题，质疑是否有其他人来回答这些问题。
• exclipy认为如果代理通过Slack或WhatsApp通知用户会更有效，否则代理暂停等待时用户可能不会注意到。
• kjhughes对代理如何识别自己何时不确定或卡住表示疑问，认为这是需要解决的核心问题。
• threeseed反驳称代理无法识别自己何时在“幻想”（hallucinating），也无法提供准确的置信度评分，批评某些解决方案的夸大宣传。
• rgbrenner指出该概念与Roo中的`ask_followup_question`类似，暗示可能存在已有解决方案。
• atoav分享了实际经验，指出LLM在电子领域提供了错误建议并引发问题，批评其在简单电路推理上的不足。
• conception询问当前使用的具体提示（prompt）是什么，可能在寻找技术细节。
• throwaway314155认为该概念简单但 brillant，并对“幻想”定义的精确性提出质疑。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于代理如何识别自己何时不确定或出错，以及如何有效通知人类介入。
- 另一个值得注意的点是LLM在实际应用（如电子领域）中的局限性和潜在风险。
- 不同用户对概念的创新性和实用性有不同的评价，有人认为它很有潜力，而有人则批评其执行和夸大宣传问题。

data.title: Anthropic co-founder on cutting access to Windsurf
data.author: jawns
data.article_summary: Anthropic联合创始人兼首席科学官Jared Kaplan表示，由于传闻OpenAI将收购AI编码助手Windsurf，Anthropic决定切断Windsurf直接访问其Claude AI模型的权限。Kaplan称，此举是为了专注于与长期合作伙伴的可持续合作，并保留计算资源。尽管Windsurf对此决定表示失望，但Kaplan提到Anthropic正与其它客户如Cursor合作，并计划在未来增加AI模型的供应。Anthropic还强调其正专注于开发自主的代理编码产品，而非仅限于AI聊天机器人。OpenAI和Windsurf尚未确认收购传闻。

44196807.article_content:
Anthropic co-founder and Chief Science Officer Jared Kaplan said his company cut Windsurf’s direct access to Anthropic’s Claude AI models largely because of rumors and reports that OpenAI, its largest competitor, is acquiring the AI coding assistant.
“We really are just trying to enable our customers who are going to sustainably be working with us in the future,” said Kaplan during an onstage interview Thursday with TechCrunch at
TC Sessions: AI 2025
.
“I think it would be odd for us to be selling Claude to OpenAI,” Kaplan said.
The comment comes just a few weeks after Bloomberg reported that
OpenAI was acquiring Windsurf for $3 billion
. Earlier this week, Windsurf said that
Anthropic cut its direct access to Claude 3.5 Sonnet and Claude 3.7 Sonnet
, two of the more popular AI models for coding, forcing the startup to find third-party computing providers on relatively short notice. Windsurf said it was disappointed in Anthropic’s decision and that it might cause short-term instability for users trying to access Claude via Windsurf.
Windsurf declined to comment on Kaplan’s remarks, and an OpenAI spokesperson did not immediately respond to TechCrunch’s request. The companies have not confirmed the acquisition rumors.
Part of the reason Anthropic cut Windsurf’s access to Claude, according to Kaplan, is because the company is quite computing-constrained today. Anthropic would like to reserve its computing for what Kaplan characterized as “lasting partnerships.”
However, Kaplan said the company hopes to greatly increase the availability of models it can offer users and developers in the coming months. He added that Anthropic has just started to unlock capacity on a new computing cluster from its partner, Amazon, which he says is “really big and continues to scale.”
