data.title: Self-hosting your own media considered harmful according to YouTube
data.author: DavideNL
data.article_summary: 本文作者分享了自己在YouTube上因展示如何使用LibreELEC和Jellyfin自建媒体库而收到社区指导违规的经历。尽管视频内容仅涉及自建合法媒体库，并未涉及任何盗版或绕过付费订阅的工具，YouTube仍以“危险或有害内容”为由删除了视频。这已不是作者第一次遇到此类问题，之前关于Jellyfin的视频也曾被下架，但上诉后恢复。此次上诉却被驳回，令作者感到困惑和沮丧。作者将视频重新上传至Internet Archive和Floatplane，并讨论了在其他平台如Peertube上发布内容的挑战，尤其是这些平台的受众规模较小，难以实现内容创作的可持续性。作者感谢Patreon、GitHub和Floatplane支持者，并希望未来能找到直接资助以持续支持其工作。同时，对YouTube的AI摘要功能可能用于其AI模型表示担忧。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：YouTube内容审核与删除、平台政策对创作者的影响、平台替代方案

不同观点：
• **关于内容审核和删除**：
  - [w14] 认为YouTube对与新冠相关内容的删除只是个开始，后续可能会有更多话题被纳入审查范围。特别提到Ofcom在英国实施的《在线安全法》可能会导致更多内容的审查，且平台会因为潜在的处罚而采取过于谨慎的内容删除策略。
  - [KurSix] 指出YouTube的审核机制不够精准，经常遗漏上下文，比如误删与开源和自托管相关的内容，而一些真正的盗版内容却长期存在。
  
• **关于平台政策对创作者的影响**：
  - [hardwaresofton] 提到YouTube的AdSense收入和广泛影响力像“金手铐”一样束缚着创作者。虽然对平台的依赖性在减弱，但要完全离开YouTube依然困难。同时，对未来互联网内容创作的新模式提出疑问，比如AI可能带来的改变。
  - [sp0ck] 和 [neepi] 都提到YouTube对特定内容（如枪支相关视频）的审核过于严格且模糊，导致合法内容的误删。创作者对此感到不满，并考虑其他方式观看或分发内容。

• **关于平台替代方案**：
  - [gloosx] 和 [neepi] 提到使用工具如yt-dlp下载YouTube视频，以此避免广告和内容限制。
  - [Helmut10001] 提出疑问，为什么还需要YouTube等视频托管平台，建议直接使用静态网页服务器托管视频。
  - [DavideNL] 和 [davedx] 提到Mastodon等去中心化平台和社区对内容创作和分享的影响，提到创作者可能转向其他平台。

补充讨论：
• **关于版权和盗版问题**：
  - [BLKNSLVR] 和 [qilo] 提到YouTube在版权检测方面的双重标准，比如误删合法内容，而盗版内容却长期存在。同时，对YouTube使用创作者内容训练AI模型的做法表示不满。
  - [boomboomsubban] 认为将某些内容标记为“危险或有害内容”是不合理的，特别是当这些内容并不鼓励盗版时。

争议焦点：YouTube内容审核的准确性和透明度、平台对创作者的限制与创作者自由之间的平衡、未来内容创作和分发的新模式。

44197932.article_content:
Self-hosting your own media considered harmful
I just received my
second community guidelines violation
for my video demonstrating the use of LibreELEC on a Raspberry Pi 5, for 4K video playback.
I purposefully avoid demonstrating any of the tools (with a suffix that rhymes with "car") that are popularly used to circumvent purchasing movie, TV, and other media content, or any tools that automatically slurp up YouTube content.
In fact, in my own house, for multiple decades, I've purchased physical media (CDs, DVDs, and more recently, Blu-Rays), and only have legally-acquired content on my NAS. Streaming services used to be a panacea but are now fragmented and mostly full of garbage—and lots of ads. We just wanted to be able to watch TV shows and movies without hassle (and I'm happy to pay for physical media that I want to watch).
But this morning, as I was finishing up work on a video about a new mini Pi cluster, I got a cheerful email from YouTube saying my video on LibreELEC on the Pi 5 was removed because it promoted:
Dangerous or Harmful Content
Content that describes how to get unauthorized or free access to audio or audiovisual content, software, subscription services, or games that usually require payment isn't allowed on YouTube.
I never described any of that stuff, only how to self-host your own media library.
This wasn't my first rodeo—in October last year, I got a
strike for showing people how to install Jellyfin
!
In
that
case, I was happy to see my appeal granted within an hour of the strike being placed on the channel. (Nevermind the fact the video had been live for
over two years
at that point, with nary a problem!)
So I thought, this case will be similar:
The video's been up for over a year, without issue
The video's had over half a million views
The video doesn't promote or highlight any tools used to circumvent copyright, get around paid subscriptions, or reproduce any content illegally
Slam-dunk, right? Well, not according to whomever reviewed my appeal. Apparently self-hosted open source media library management is harmful.
Who knew open source software could be so
subversive
?
The video
So along that theme, I've re-uploaded the video to Internet Archive, free for anyone to download and view at their leisure.
Yes, even those rebels running LibreELEC on their Raspberry Pis!
Here it is:
LibreELEC on the Raspberry Pi 5 - Internet Archive
.
I've also uploaded it
on Floatplane
, for subscribers.
Alternatives
I've been slowly uploading my back catalog to
my channel on Floatplane
, though not all my content is there yet.
Some in the fediverse ask why I'm not on Peertube. Here's the problem (and it's not insurmountable):
right now
, there's no easy path towards sustainable content production when the audience for the content is 100x smaller, and the number of patrons/sponsors remains proportionally the same.
I was never able to sustain my open source work based on patronage, and content production is the same—just more expensive to maintain to any standard (each video takes between 10-300 hours to produce, and I have a family to feed, and
US health insurance companies to fund
).
YouTube was, and still is, a creative anomaly. I'm hugely thankful to my
Patreon
,
GitHub
, and
Floatplane
supporters—and I hope to have direct funding fully able to support my work someday. But until that time, YouTube's AdSense revenue and vast reach is a kind of 'golden handcuff.'
The handcuff has been a bit tarnished of late, however, with Google recently adding AI summaries to videos—which
seems
to indicate maybe
Gemini is slurping up my content and using it in their AI models
?
Maybe the handcuffs are fools-gold, and I just don't see it yet.

44197932.article_summary: 本文作者分享了自己在YouTube上因展示如何使用LibreELEC和Jellyfin自建媒体库而收到社区指导违规的经历。尽管视频内容仅涉及自建合法媒体库，并未涉及任何盗版或绕过付费订阅的工具，YouTube仍以“危险或有害内容”为由删除了视频。这已不是作者第一次遇到此类问题，之前关于Jellyfin的视频也曾被下架，但上诉后恢复。此次上诉却被驳回，令作者感到困惑和沮丧。作者将视频重新上传至Internet Archive和Floatplane，并讨论了在其他平台如Peertube上发布内容的挑战，尤其是这些平台的受众规模较小，难以实现内容创作的可持续性。作者感谢Patreon、GitHub和Floatplane支持者，并希望未来能找到直接资助以持续支持其工作。同时，对YouTube的AI摘要功能可能用于其AI模型表示担忧。

• [ghushn3] 则提醒人们在开始家庭蒸馏之前要谨慎，因为这在世界上许多地方（包括美国的一些地区）是严格非法的。他/她的观点集中在法律风险上，警示潜在的兴趣爱好者。

data.title: Prompt engineering playbook for programmers
data.author: vinhnx
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于"提示工程"（prompt engineering）的定义、价值和必要性的讨论

不同观点：
• 支持提示工程：
  - **DebtDeflation**: 认为提示工程包括情境学习（In Context Learning）、思维链（Chain of Thought）和结构化输出等技术，强调明确语言描述的重要性，同时提及角色提示（Role Prompting）和RAG（检索增强生成）等方法。
  - **orochimaaru**: 通过科学编程课程中学到的验证方法来设计提示，认为正式指定输入、前提条件和后置条件可以生成有效的代码。
  
• 反对提示工程：
  - **bsoles**: 认为"提示工程"并非真正的工程，不过是写出合理句子的能力，质疑其专业性和必要性。
  - **leshow**: 认为使用"工程"一词描述写提示是不严肃的。
  - **jwr**: 认为提示工程不过是尝试和错误的过程，没有科学规律或法则，不属于科学或工程范畴。
  
• 对提示工程的实用性持怀疑态度：
  - **haolez**: 认为过于复杂和冗长的提示可能降低模型性能，主张使用简单和最小化的提示，通过少量迭代进行微调。
  - **heisenburgzero**: 认为如果问题本身无法由大型语言模型（LLM）解决，任何提示工程也无济于事，只有通过分解任务或示例部分解决。
  
• 对提示工程的替代方案：
  - **jorge_cab**: 认为开发者不应负责写"好提示"，建议通过中间层优化传递给LLM的信息，类似于Agentic IDEs正在做的。
  
• 对提示工程的心理抵触：
  - **BuyMyBitcoins**: 对用自然英语给出提示有心理障碍，认为应该像写SQL查询或提供可执行参数那样精确，但承认自然语言处理使工具更易访问。
  
• 彻底反对依赖提示工程：
  - **akkad33**: 宁愿自己写代码，也不愿依赖提示工程。
  
• 对软件工程行业现状的批评：
  - **nexoft**: 认为"提示工程"是痛苦的，并批评软件工程行业因过度追求薪酬而导致工程师质量下降，提示工程成为拐杖。

补充讨论：
• 提示工程的工具和实践：
  - **ColinEberhardt**: 认为目前过多的提示指南不必要，熟悉工具和其工作方式后，合适的提示自然会显现。
  
• 对提示工程的幽默和讽刺：
  - **air7**: 引用Sergey Brin的话，以幽默方式提到威胁模型以获得更好结果，反映出对提示工程的非传统看法。

争议焦点：
• 提示工程是否属于真正的工程范畴及其专业性。
• 提示工程的复杂性是否有助于提升模型性能或适得其反。
• 开发者是否应负责写提示或通过工具和中间层优化提示。

data.title: FFmpeg merges WebRTC support
data.author: Sean-Der
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了网站管理员为保护服务器免受AI公司大量抓取数据导致的宕机问题，而设置了一个名为Anubis的系统。Anubis采用了一种类似于Hashcash的“工作量证明”机制，旨在增加大规模数据抓取的成本。虽然对普通用户影响不大，但在面对大规模抓取时能有效增加其成本。Anubis是一个临时解决方案，旨在为更复杂的真实用户识别技术争取时间。需要注意的是，Anubis需要使用现代JavaScript功能，因此需要禁用如JShelter等插件。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：WebRTC广播及其相关技术（如WHIP协议）在不同场景中的应用和潜在问题。

不同观点：
• **支持与兴奋态度**：
   - [Sean-Der] 对WebRTC广播和WHIP协议的广泛支持感到兴奋，认为这是视频广播领域的一个重要里程碑，特别是在跨平台（移动、网页、嵌入式设备等）上的应用。
   - [msgodel] 认为这将使自托管流媒体或流媒体CDN变得更加容易，特别是如果熟悉FFmpeg的话，它是非常强大的媒体软件。
   - [FrostKiwi] 期待使用FFmpeg和WebRTC流来简化当前的远程控制项目，避免复杂的ExpressJS操作。

• **技术实现与未来发展**：
   - [jauntywundrkind] 提到虽然WHIP使用了WebRTC的SCTP协议，但更希望未来能转向基于QUIC或WebTransport的P2P协议，如Media-over-QUIC (MoQ)，因为QUIC能更好地处理UDP上的多路复用和复杂性。
   - [qwertox] 询问WHIP是否意味着网站可以直接连接到FFmpeg实例并接收音视频流，有人提供了FFmpeg WHIP相关信息的链接。

• **潜在问题与安全性担忧**：
   - [autoexec] 担心WebRTC的安全性问题，指出WebRTC的漏洞曾导致许多安全事件，通常会在安装浏览器后禁用它。
   - [throwpoaster] 关心FFmpeg的安全审计机制，认为其目前看起来较为被动。

• **具体应用场景与技术问题**：
   - [esbeeb] 提到Gajim（XMPP客户端）一直等待此功能以恢复其音视频通话功能，FFmpeg的WHIP支持将大大简化这一过程。

44182186.article_content:
Making sure you're not a bot!
Loading...
Why am I seeing this?
You are seeing this because the administrator of this website has set up
Anubis
to protect the server against the scourge of
AI companies aggressively scraping websites
. This can and does cause downtime for the websites, which makes their resources inaccessible for everyone.
Anubis is a compromise. Anubis uses a
Proof-of-Work
scheme in the vein of
Hashcash
, a proposed proof-of-work scheme for reducing email spam. The idea is that at individual scales the additional load is ignorable, but at mass scraper levels it adds up and makes scraping much more expensive.
Ultimately, this is a hack whose real purpose is to give a "good enough" placeholder solution so that more time can be spent on fingerprinting and identifying headless browsers (EG: via how they do font rendering) so that the challenge proof of work page doesn't need to be presented to users that are much more likely to be legitimate.
Please note that Anubis requires the use of modern JavaScript features that plugins like
JShelter
will disable. Please disable JShelter or other such plugins for this domain.
44182186.article_summary: 本文介绍了网站管理员为保护服务器免受AI公司大量抓取数据导致的宕机问题，而设置了一个名为Anubis的系统。Anubis采用了一种类似于Hashcash的“工作量证明”机制，旨在增加大规模数据抓取的成本。虽然对普通用户影响不大，但在面对大规模抓取时能有效增加其成本。Anubis是一个临时解决方案，旨在为更复杂的真实用户识别技术争取时间。需要注意的是，Anubis需要使用现代JavaScript功能，因此需要禁用如JShelter等插件。

data.title: Cursor 1.0
data.author: ecz
data.article_summary: Cursor 1.0发布，主要更新包括：引入BugBot进行自动代码审查，发现问题后可一键修复；Background Agent功能对所有用户开放，支持通过云图标或快捷键访问，隐私模式下也将 soon 支持；Background Agent现可在Jupyter Notebooks中使用，支持Sonnet模型；推出Memories功能，可记忆对话事实并在未来引用，目前为测试功能；MCP服务器支持一键安装和OAuth认证；聊天响应增强，支持Mermaid图表和Markdown表格；设置和仪表盘页面更新，提供使用统计和团队管理功能等。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Cursor（一个基于VSCode的AI辅助开发工具）的商业模式、技术问题、用户体验以及与VSCode和其它AI工具的竞争关系。

不同观点：
• [ai_assisted_dev] 认为 Cursor 的收费标准不切实际，尽管他个人通过使用 Cursor 提高了工作效率，但 Cursor 的高成本（尤其是API请求费用）让人担忧其盈利模式。他还提到希望增加异步请求等功能以提升效率。
• [BudaDude] 喜欢 Cursor，但担心其扩展更新速度慢以及多个MCP服务器实例导致内存占用过大的问题。
• [ashleynewman] 对那些与Cursor发布无关的抱怨表示不满，并特别关注BugBot的发布，希望它不仅仅是查看代码差异，还能利用完整的上下文进行代码审查。
• [vladstudio] 推荐了ampcode.com，并表示其使用Claude 4且无需设置，使用体验良好。
• [blixt] 提到Cursor与VSCode的兼容性问题，尤其是与微软开发的插件和容器化工具的兼容性问题，并指出Cursor逐渐偏离VSCode的设计。
• [jameslk] 提出Cursor的愿望清单，希望在代码审查中能更清楚地标识模型修改代码的原因，以减少调试困难。
• [jimrandomh] 批评Cursor作为闭源的VSCode分支，在插件支持上存在问题，且缺乏文档支持，认为这是对开源项目的不尊重。
• [swyx] 认为Cursor的1.0发布过于低调，缺乏市场推广和愿景描述，导致用户难以形成明确预期。
• [CafeRacer] 已经放弃使用Cursor，主要因为其不稳定的表现和IDE中的干扰性自动完成功能，同时提到VSCode市场不再适用于Cursor。
• [jadbox] 认为任何闭源的VSCode替代品都无法与VSCode加上多个开源扩展（如Copilot、CLINE、FOAM）竞争。
• [curiousElf] 希望Cursor能更好地支持多根目录仓库，并提到模型经常选错目录，需要手动引导。
• [mythz] 认为Cursor尝试创建自己的IDE是一个战略错误，并表示只会考虑集成到现有IDE（如VSCode和Rider）中的AI工具。
• [dkersten] 停止使用Cursor，转而使用Zed的代理模式，因为Cursor存在内存泄漏问题，且Zed更轻量。
• [sidgarimella] 提到同时运行多个IDE和终端会话，使用Claude Code，并通过Neuralink直接连接到MCP服务器，认为不同的工具在不同场景下各有用途。
• [serverlessmania] 认为Cursor作为VSCode的分支没有足够的理由让开发者放弃现有的工具（如Vim、JetBrains、VSCode），并预测随着终端代理（如Claude Code和Codex）的兴起，Cursor将变得过时。

补充讨论：
• 收费争议：[ai_assisted_dev] 和 [jimrandomh] 对Cursor的收费模式和闭源性质提出质疑，认为当前收费不合理且对开源社区不尊重。
• 功能需求：[ai_assisted_dev]、[jameslk] 和 [curiousElf] 提出了对Cursor功能改进的愿望，如异步请求、代码修改原因标识和多根目录支持。
• 竞争与替代：[mythz]、[CafeRacer]、[jadbox] 和 [serverlessmania] 讨论了Cursor与VSCode及其它AI工具（如Copilot、Claude Code）的竞争关系，认为Cursor面临巨大挑战。
• 技术问题：[BudaDude]、[blixt] 和 [dkersten] 提到了Cursor在扩展兼容性、内存管理和性能方面的技术问题。

1.0
BugBot, Background Agent access to everyone, and one-click MCP install
Cursor 1.0 is here!
This release brings BugBot for code review, a first look at memories, one-click MCP setup, Jupyter support, and general availability of Background Agent.
Automatic code review with BugBot
BugBot automatically reviews your PRs and catches potential bugs and issues.
When an issue is found, BugBot leaves a comment on your PRs in GitHub. You can click "
Fix in Cursor
" to move back to the editor with a pre-filled prompt to fix the issue.
To set it up, follow instructions in our
BugBot docs
.
Your browser does not support the video tag.
Background Agent for everyone
Since we released Background Agent, our remote coding agent, in early access a few weeks ago, early signals have been positive.
We're now excited to expand Background Agent to all users! You can start using it right away by clicking the cloud icon in chat or hitting
Cmd/Ctrl+E
if you have privacy mode disabled. For users with privacy mode enabled, we'll soon have a way to enable it for you too!
Agent in Jupyter Notebooks
Cursor can now implement changes in Jupyter Notebooks!
Agent will now create and edit multiple cells directly inside of Jupyter, a significant improvement for research and data science tasks. Only supported with Sonnet models to start.
Your browser does not support the video tag.
Memories
With Memories, Cursor can remember facts from conversations and reference them in the future. Memories are stored per project on an individual level, and can be managed from Settings.
We're rolling out Memories as a beta feature. To get started, enable from Settings → Rules.
Your browser does not support the video tag.
MCP one-click install and OAuth support
You can now set up MCP servers in Cursor with one click, and together with OAuth support, you can easily authenticate servers that support it.
We've curated a short list of official MCP servers you can add to Cursor at
docs.cursor.com/tools
.
If you're an MCP developer, you can easily make your server available to developers by adding a
Add to Cursor
button in your documentation and READMEs. Generate one at
docs.cursor.com/deeplinks
.

Richer Chat responses
Cursor can now render visualizations inside of a conversation. In particular, Mermaid diagrams and Markdown tables can now be generated and viewed in the same place!

New Settings and Dashboard
The setting and dashboard page have gotten some polish with this release.
With the new Dashboard, you can view your individual or team's usage analytics, update your display name, and view detailed statistics broken down by tool or model.

data.title: Amelia Earhart's Reckless Final Flights
data.author: Thevet
data.article_summary: 1937年，著名女飞行员阿梅莉亚·埃尔哈特（Amelia Earhart）试图驾驶洛克希德Electra 10-E飞机进行环球飞行，但在夏威夷的路克机场起飞时发生事故。飞机在跑道上失控旋转，幸好没有爆炸，埃尔哈特和两名导航员安全脱险。埃尔哈特此前因横跨大西洋的飞行而闻名，但她实际操作经验不足，且忙于宣传活动，缺乏充分准备。她的飞行依赖于导航员的帮助，且飞机技术先进但操控复杂。此次环球飞行计划长达29,000英里，途经豪兰岛等偏远地点，面临巨大风险。尽管如此，成功将带来巨大的声誉和商业机会。媒体对她的冒险高度关注，但她最终在尝试中失踪。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Amelia Earhart的飞行悲剧及其历史评价的多角度讨论

不同观点：
• **技术失误论**：cylinder714引用1993年美国海军学会的文章，认为Earhart的悲剧是由于无线电设备操作不当，特别是有人在她飞行前拆除了一个用于长距离通讯的可伸缩天线，这一技术失误是导致她失踪的重要原因。

• **历史背景论**：a-r-t提到Veritasium的一个视频深入探讨了她最后一次飞行的技术细节和问题，暗示飞行失败不仅仅是个人失误，还涉及当时的技术局限和风险。

• **个人评价论**：WalterBright分享其父亲作为B-17导航员和职业飞行员的看法，认为Earhart是个鲁莽的飞行员，并表示对她缺乏敬意，但同时对另一位女性飞行员Jacqueline Cochran表示钦佩，以证明其并非性别歧视。

• **历史地位论**：cameldrv指出Earhart因媒体宣传而广为人知，但实际上第一个完成环球飞行的女性并非她，而是被大众忽视，反映出公众记忆的选择性。

• **历史教训论**：beedeebeedee认为Earhart的飞行失败是当时航空发展阶段中常见的鲁莽飞行现象之一，并提到20世纪20年代阿拉斯加丛林飞行员的冒险故事，强调集体学习飞行技术的重要性。

• **英雄形象论**：0xbadcafebee表示喜欢这类历史故事，认为成为历史人物往往需要一些“疯狂”的举动，同时指出没有必要粉饰或掩盖英雄的缺陷，因为他们的传奇往往会继续流传。

• **文字编辑批评**：johnyzee对文章中使用"coördinated"这种带分音符号的拼写方式表示不满，认为这种用法显得过于正式和过时。

• **语义质疑**：bauble对文章中“人类导航员”的表述提出质疑，认为用“男性导航员”可能更为准确，因为Earhart本身也是人类一员，这种表述显得逻辑不通。

补充讨论：
• 评论中涉及到对历史事件的多角度审视，包括技术失误、个人性格、历史地位以及公众记忆的选择性等问题。
• 部分评论还涉及对媒体、语言使用以及历史人物形象的批判性思考。
• 争议焦点在于Earhart作为飞行员的专业能力和其历史地位是否被过度宣传，以及技术失误在其失踪事件中的实际影响。

Sparks flew, a wing bent, and the landing gear snapped off as the silver Lockheed Electra 10-E plane smashed into the runway at Luke Field, outside Honolulu. The pilot’s only stroke of luck was that the aircraft, which contained nearly a thousand gallons of fuel, didn’t explode.
The thirty-nine-year-old Amelia Earhart and her crew of two navigators, Fred Noonan and Harry Manning, crawled out of the wreckage, unsettled but otherwise unhurt. They had meant to depart on the second leg of a gruelling voyage: a round-the-world flight that had begun in Oakland, California, and would continue westward, with two dozen or so stops, before ending up back in Oakland. People close to Earhart knew that she wasn’t fully ready for a challenge of this magnitude, and so a work-around had been devised. An extra crew member with extensive flight experience, Paul Mantz, had joined the flight to Hawaii. On the runway in Oakland, he switched places with Earhart and assumed the throttles during takeoff. She then piloted most of the way to Oahu, but Mantz often took over.
As they approached Luke Field, Mantz sensed that Earhart had “pilot fatigue.” He asked her, “Do you want to land it?”
“No, you land it,” Earhart said.
He did so, then said farewell. Earhart had been able to observe Mantz’s handling of the plane over the Pacific, and from now on she would be the only pilot onboard. Flying the Electra solo wouldn’t be easy. Although the plane had state-of-the-art technology for its time, piloting it demanded constant coördination among the throttle, the rudder, and the control column—especially during takeoff and landing. While taking off on the second leg, Earhart ignored advice that Mantz had given her not to “jockey the throttles”—change the speed to maintain direction and balance—and the plane veered into a violent spin across the runway. The press had assembled to watch Earhart soar, and instead witnessed an embarrassment.
The stakes were huge. Men had been flying around the world since 1924, when a team of eight military officers completed a twenty-seven-thousand-mile journey in a hundred and seventy-five days (with seventy-four stops). Only one pilot had done a solo circumnavigation: a Texan named Wiley Post. In 1933, Post completed a fifteen-thousand-mile journey, traversing Germany, the Soviet Union, Alaska, and Canada. Four years later, a round-the-world flight remained daunting. Earhart planned to have human navigators on board with her, but she’d be the first female pilot to accomplish the feat.
Earhart had become instantly famous in 1928, as the first woman to cross the Atlantic in a plane. But, though she’d been photographed wearing a flight suit and a leather helmet, she was merely a passenger; the plane had actually been piloted by two men, Wilmer Stultz and Louis Gordon. She had since been working on establishing her command of the cockpit. There were plenty of accomplished female pilots who could’ve taken command of a transatlantic flight themselves, and some of these women considered Earhart’s notoriety unearned. In 1932, after logging more flight miles—but not as many as other top female pilots—she flew solo across the Atlantic in a cramped red Vega, a single-engine plane barely insulated against storms and cold temperatures. She fought exhaustion, iced wings, and a broken altimeter. Her intention was to land in Paris, but she ended up in a cow field in Ireland. Earhart approached the experience with an easy, almost reckless, confidence. She’d always been this way; as a girl growing up in the Kansas City area, she jury-rigged a “roller coaster” with steep ramps, then barrelled down it and fell off, only to exult, “This is just like flying!”
A globe-circling flight would be Earhart’s lengthiest journey by far, twenty-nine thousand miles hugging the equator. This wasn’t mere hopping among landmasses, as with Post’s route. Her path had been ambitiously charted to include a refuelling stop on Howland Island, a speck between Hawaii and Australia. A pilot making such a journey needed to be in excellent shape, with sufficient strength and stamina to manage the controls in turbulence, particularly during long hours in a cockpit with no autopilot. The dangers were extraordinary: enormous stretches over open ocean, unpredictable weather, extended isolation, intense psychological pressure. Yet the rewards promised to be substantial, from marketing opportunities to media attention. NBC and CBS were fighting over the rights to exclusive broadcasts.
Noonan and Manning had agreed to accompany Earhart nearly the whole way. They were excited to be associated with her glamour, but they also considered the job a risk. Rather than spending time practicing in the powerful Electra, Earhart had been crisscrossing the country, giving lectures, making sponsorship appearances, and attending promotional events. For a while, she had a gig as the aviation editor at
Cosmopolitan
44185078.article_summary: 1937年，著名女飞行员阿梅莉亚·埃尔哈特（Amelia Earhart）试图驾驶洛克希德Electra 10-E飞机进行环球飞行，但在夏威夷的路克机场起飞时发生事故。飞机在跑道上失控旋转，幸好没有爆炸，埃尔哈特和两名导航员安全脱险。埃尔哈特此前因横跨大西洋的飞行而闻名，但她实际操作经验不足，且忙于宣传活动，缺乏充分准备。她的飞行依赖于导航员的帮助，且飞机技术先进但操控复杂。此次环球飞行计划长达29,000英里，途经豪兰岛等偏远地点，面临巨大风险。尽管如此，成功将带来巨大的声誉和商业机会。媒体对她的冒险高度关注，但她最终在尝试中失踪。

data.author: zachdive
data.article_summary: AdamCAD是一个由AI驱动的CAD平台，可以在几秒钟内通过文字描述生成3D设计。用户可以通过文本提示创建和编辑3D模型，并进一步优化和导出设计。此外，AdamCAD还能将图像快速转换为3D模型，集成专业CAD软件，支持各种设计需求，如齿轮、支架、植物盆等模型。平台旨在通过自然语言帮助专业人士将创意变为现实，适用于工业设计和机械工程等领域。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI驱动3D模型工具的应用与功能改进

不同观点：
• arberavdullahu认为该工具在定制家具（如不同材质和设计选项）方面有很大潜力，并提到IKEA有类似应用。他提到工具在过度迭代时会改变物体形态，并建议结合高分辨率图片生成更逼真的渲染图。
• klaus silveira关注3D模型纹理的增强和重塑，分享了自己通过ComfyUI和Blender脚本实现的流程，并提出对网格简化和UV展开工具的需求，还询问了自动化绑定的可能性。
• lucasoshiro希望能够下载生成的.scad文件，并对工具在生成参数化模型（如瓶子）方面的失败表示失望，但总体上对工具表示肯定。
• chmod775对工具的表现超出预期，提到可以快速应用生成模型并进行修改，尽管模型不够完美，但比自己从头创建要快。
• adenta分享了自己在openSCAD和MCP方面的经验，并愿意提供帮助。
• Valk3_对Blender和openSCAD的功能进行比较，认为Blender在3D建模方面可能更强大，但实现类似工具可能更困难。
• WillAdams对工具的可用性表示失望，特别是对复杂模型的生成（如网格单元）失败，指出openSCAD在数学能力上的限制。
• ata_aman希望实现GPT支持的多物理仿真，设计CAD对象时希望通过语音转文本运行不同仿真。
• protocolture对工具的表现表示肯定，但指出工具在设计细节应用上的不足，并考虑在其他工具中完成设计。
• flippyhead对与孩子一起使用该工具进行3D打印表示兴奋，并好奇输出模型在prusa打印机上的效果。
• voidUpdate关注生成模型的拓扑结构问题，希望避免再次修复糟糕的拓扑。
• iancmceachern对工具与CAD软件的集成感兴趣，询问在Solidworks中使用的订阅级别。
• gavmor关注自支撑设计和参数化结构优化，询问工具如何与其他支持这些技术的流程结合。
• b0a04gl对工具在用户通过提示修改模型时的约束解决和几何验证机制感兴趣，询问是否维护共享参数模型或对比场景图，以及几何验证的处理方式。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是工具在生成复杂模型时的表现，部分用户（如WillAdams）对失败案例表示失望，而其他用户（如chmod775）则对工具的快速生成能力表示赞赏。
• 用户对工具与其他软件（如Blender、openSCAD、Solidworks）的集成和互补功能有较高兴趣，特别是自动化和优化方面的需求。
• 拓扑结构和模型质量是用户关注的重点，部分用户（如voidUpdate）希望避免修复糟糕的拓扑。
• 对工具的未来功能扩展（如多物理仿真、自支撑设计、自动化绑定）也有较多讨论，用户希望工具能在现有流程中更好地结合和应用。

data.title: Why I wrote the BEAM book
data.author: lawik
data.article_summary: 《BEAM书》的作者分享了撰写这本书的曲折经历和动机。在维护Klarna核心系统的十年中，他意识到即使是15毫秒的暂停也可能导致严重问题。他于2012年开始撰写此书，最初使用DocBook，后来转向AsciiDoc并编写自定义脚本，乐观预计六个月完成。然而，项目多次遭遇挫折，包括与O'Reilly和Pragmatic Bookshelf的出版合作相继取消。2017年，他在GitHub上重新启动项目，并获得社区贡献支持。书中涵盖了BEAM调度器、内存管理、垃圾回收、编译器和调试等方面，旨在为Erlang和Elixir系统开发和运维人员提供深入参考。作者强调，坚持比完美更重要，最终完成了这本深入解析BEAM的手册。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：BEAM 技术及其相关书籍、学习资源和应用情况

不同观点：
• elric 强调了对 BEAM 深入理解的驱动以及出版商与作者之间在选题上的分歧。他提到自己追求更深层次的技术内容，而非表面的解释，并且分享了与出版商在书籍主题上无法达成一致的经历。
• schonfinkel 高度评价了 BEAM 和 Erlang 技术，认为学习 BEAM 是他过去一年中最好的技术体验之一，并推荐了 Joe Armstrong 的书，同时对新出版的 BEAM 书籍表示赞赏。
• game_the0ry 认为 BEAM 是被低估的技术，并以 WhatsApp 为例，表示对 Elixir 和 Erlang 在高并发项目中未得到广泛应用的不解。
• bicx 表示 BEAM 和 Elixir 是他构建网络或管道密集系统的首选工具，虽然近期项目中不太适用，但仍乐于关注其发展，并对新出版的书籍表示欢迎。
• pyuser583 提到尽管 BEAM 的优点被广泛宣传，但其采用率仍然较低，对此表示疑惑。
• cgopalan 确认该书籍对有 Erlang/BEAM 经验的开发者更有用，并询问其对新手的适用性。

补充讨论：
• techpression 表示即使书籍可以在网上免费获取，仍然愿意购买以支持作者。
• asib 对 15ms 的后 mortem 事件表示不解，认为时间过短不足以引起如此重视。
• maerch 分享了 positive 网络评论对其产生的持久积极影响，强调了积极互动的重要性。
• graboid 提问是否存在其他类似 BEAM 的虚拟机，并探讨了开发新虚拟机的难度和工作量。
• spelunker 提到尽管 JVM 文档丰富，但 BEAM 对他而言仍然神秘，并对新资源表示欢迎。
• tra3 表示对未来能实际使用 Erlang 的期待。

争议焦点：
• BEAM 技术的采用率低，尽管其在高并发项目中表现出色，但未被广泛应用，这引起了多位评论者的讨论和不解。
• 出版选题上的分歧，尤其是技术作者与出版商在书籍主题选择上的矛盾。

其他值得注意的讨论点：
• BEAM 技术的深度和复杂性使其学习资源显得稀缺和珍贵。
• 对技术社区中积极互动和支持的重视，如 techpression 对作者的支持和 maerch 对积极评论的感受。

Hacker's Handbook
Why I Wrote the BEAM Book
Post-mortems, coffee, and a decade of stubborn curiosity
Posted:  2025-06-03
Categories:
development
,
Erlang
,
BEAM
,
theBeamBook
,
writing
Why I wrote the Beam Book
After ten years of keeping Klarnaâs core system upright I know this: a 15
millisecond pause in the BEAM can stall millions of peak-shopping payments, trigger a 3 a.m. Christmas-Eve post-mortem, and earn you a very awake call from the CEO. I wrote
The BEAM Book
so the next engineer fixes that pause before the coffee cools.
Origins
I opened the project on 12 October 2012 with a lone DocBook file with four lines of text and an oversized sense of optimism.
After two weeks, the commit log is mostly me adding structure, moving
headings, and updating metadata. Most of it is scaffolding. The actual
content is still just a few hopeful lines.
By November I had abandoned DocBook for AsciiDoc, written a custom build
script, and convinced myself the book could be wrapped up in six months.
Those early commits glow with energy: adds, rewrites, then more
rewrites to fix the rewrites.
Delusion is underrated.
In 2013 I managed to convince OâReilly to publish. Moving the repo to their
Atlas system sounded simple until Atlas began hiding my main file and
overwriting half-finished chapters.
The Git history reads like a diary of frustration:
âMoving files to top level to cope with Atlas,â âAtlas seems to be
overwriting book.asciidocâ. Word count shot past 120 000 while actual
progress crawled. On 10 March 2015 I was literally âSmashing chapters into sectionsâ just to keep the build green.
The quiet cancellation came two months later. No drama, just a polite call and a line through the contract. Relief mingled with embarrassment, I had spent two years rearranging files rather than finishing sentences.
Pragmatic Bookshelf took over that same year. I kept working in CVS for
their production system, but progress was slow. Eventually, they cancelled
too. On 20 January 2017, I imported everything into a new repo in one
massive commit: 6,622 files, over a million lines.
The rewrite stalled, and so did the project.
On 23 March 2017 I started fresh with Asciidoctor in a private GitHub repo, copy-pasting
only the parts that still made sense. Two weeks later, on April 7, minutes before
a lecture at Chalmers, I flipped the repository public. Within twenty-four
hours strangers fixed typos, added diagrams, and merged a Creative Commons
BY-4.0 license.
What Kept Me Going
I kept going because I wanted to understand the BEAM properly. Thereâs
value in following the real logic, not just the surface explanations.
Community feedback made a difference. As soon as the repo was public,
people began sending corrections, examples, and improvements.
Seeing the numbers of people starring the repo on GitHub kept me going.
One highlight:
Issue #113 - âPlease continue being awesome.â
That emoji-laced drive-by encouragement (August 2018) still pops into my
head whenever motivation dips.
The book started showing up as a reference in Erlang and BEAM conference
talks, sometimes several times in the same event. That was a clear signal
that others needed this as much as I did.
Even Twitter (in the good old days of Twitter) played a role. Whenever
someone mentioned the book or shared a
link, it was an extra nudge to keep at it.
Mostly, I just wanted a manual I could trust myself, a reference for the
parts of the VM that matter when things go wrong. Thatâs reason enough to
keep writing, even after the third rewrite.
Whatâs Inside the Book & Who It Helps
The book covers what I wish Iâd had when building and operating large
Erlang systems:
Schedulers and process management: How the BEAM schedules,
prioritizes, and balances processes under real load.
Processes and their memory: How process heaps,
stack, messages, and binaries are managed and
why these details matter in production.
Garbage collection and memory: What actually happens
with per-process and global garbage collectors, binary references,
and memory leaks.
Tagging schemes and terms: How the BEAM represents data-integers,
floats, tuples, binaries, references-down to the tagging bits.
The compiler and the VM: How code is turned into instructions,
what the compiler does (and doesnât do), and how the emulator executes it.
Tracing and debugging: Practical use of dbg, erlang:trace,
and other tools to follow messages, events, and identify bottlenecks.
Performance tuning: What matters when profiling real code,
understanding reductions, and tracking down real-world latency problems.
System architecture: How ERTS, the BEAM VM, and their subsystems
actually work together in a running node.
If you build or operate Erlang or Elixir systems, especially under any kind
of scale-this book is for you. It saves you from hunting through mailing
lists, scattered docs, and code comments just to answer, âWhy is the VM
behaving like this?â

44179257.article_summary: 《BEAM书》的作者分享了撰写这本书的曲折经历和动机。在维护Klarna核心系统的十年中，他意识到即使是15毫秒的暂停也可能导致严重问题。他于2012年开始撰写此书，最初使用DocBook，后来转向AsciiDoc并编写自定义脚本，乐观预计六个月完成。然而，项目多次遭遇挫折，包括与O'Reilly和Pragmatic Bookshelf的出版合作相继取消。2017年，他在GitHub上重新启动项目，并获得社区贡献支持。书中涵盖了BEAM调度器、内存管理、垃圾回收、编译器和调试等方面，旨在为Erlang和Elixir系统开发和运维人员提供深入参考。作者强调，坚持比完美更重要，最终完成了这本深入解析BEAM的手册。

data.title: UK Court Rules on Reverse Engineering of Mainframe Software
data.author: wslh
data.article_summary: 2025年5月13日，英国法院就大型机软件的反向工程问题作出裁决，IBM UK成功维护其软件许可协议的条款，对抗创建竞争产品的被告。法院强调严格遵守软件许可协议中的使用限制和潜在违约条款，尤其在涉及知识产权保护时，对版权例外采取限制性解释，以维护版权所有者的合法权益。此案中，Winsopia Ltd及其关联公司被发现利用IBM的许可软件协助开发竞争软件（SDM），违反了协议条款。法院最终判决禁止被告继续销售、推广或分发SDM软件，并要求销毁相关程序，同时IBM获赔诉讼费用。此判决提醒软件许可方应明确协议条款，而被许可方则需严格遵守约定，特别是在涉及反向工程和软件共享时。

May 13, 2025
UK Court Rules on Reverse Engineering of Mainframe Software
Sophie Burgess
,
Edouard Fortunet
,
Dr. Jakob Guhn
,
Rebecca Swindells
Jones Day

In Short
The Situation
: IBM UK ("IBM") successfully enforced the terms of a mainframe license against the defendants who had created a competing software product.
The Result
: Focusing on the discussion of intellectual property rights, the court favored a strict adherence to the terms of the software license agreement when assessing use restrictions and potential breaches. Copyright exceptions conferred by Directive 2009/24/EC ("Software Directive") are limited and will be applied restrictively, ensuring that copyright owners are able to exploit their work and protect their legitimate interests.
Looking Ahead
: Software licensors should ensure that their agreements are sufficiently clear to protect their intellectual property interests. Likewise, software licensees should ensure that the terms of software license agreements are adhered to, especially where the software is decompiled and shared with related entities. Such use must be in relation to the acts permitted by the agreement.
Background
In 2013, the second defendant, Winsopia Ltd ("Winsopia"), entered into a customer agreement with the claimant, IBM (the "ICA"). Unbeknownst at the time to IBM, Winsopia is a wholly owned subsidiary of the third defendant, LzLabs UK, which was ultimately owned by the first defendant, LzLabs GmbH ("LzLabs"). The sixth defendant, Mr. John Moores, is the main beneficial owner of LzLabs, Winsopia, and LzLabs UK.
Notably, back in 2009, Mr. Moore's separate company, Neon Enterprise Software LLC ("Neon"), had unsuccessfully sued IBM Corporation in the United States. In that dispute, which concluded in 2011 and involved a counterclaim by IBM, an employee from Neon admitted to acts of reverse assembly and the destruction of evidence related to IBM Corporation's proprietary software. IBM succeeded in preventing Neon from selling its infringing product and forcing it to hand over its source code to IBM; this led to the cessation of operations at Neon.
In December 2013, Winsopia and LzLabs entered into a consultancy services agreement, under which Winsopia agreed to perform discovery, quality assurance, and software development work for LzLabs. The court identified that Winsopia's use of IBM's licensed software was "
for the sole purpose of assisting LzLabs in its software development.
" The defendants explained that they had established clean room procedures to ensure compliance with the terms of the ICA during development of what became the central issue of the dispute, the software defined mainframe ("SDM"). Those included: (i) codes of conduct between Winsopia and LzLabs; and (ii) systems to record intercompany requests made concerning the mainframe software.
In 2016, LzLabs launched its SDM, which competes with IBM's mainframe software, offering a smaller, external, non-mainframe computer capable of executing batch processing tasks typically performed by a mainframe system. IBM became suspicious about the methods involved in SDM's development and in 2020 notified Winsopia that it intended to audit Winsopia's compliance with the terms of the ICA. When Winsopia declined the audit request, IBM commenced proceedings seeking a declaration that Winsopia's license had been lawfully terminated and an injunction preventing Winsopia from making any further use of IBM's licensed software.
The Court's Decision
There were several issues for the court's determination, which were delivered over a
253-page decision
(see paragraph 138). These issues included assessing the proper construction of the ICA, the alleged breaches (and procurement of such breaches), and whether the acts alleged to be in breach of the ICA fell within the rights conferred by the Software Directive, as implemented by the Copyright, Designs and Patents Act 1988 ("CDPA"), and whether these acts could be restricted or prohibited by contract.
This case summary focuses on the above-mentioned issues. However, further issues which were determined included assessing liability for the tort of unlawful means conspiracy, evaluating the validity of IBM's termination of the ICA and the determination of limitation periods in relation to IBM's claims. IBM was victorious in most issues.
At the consequentials hearing, the High Court ordered injunctive relief against the first, second, and sixth defendants, including prohibitions on the marketing, sale, and dissemination of the SDM software, and required delivery up or destruction of IBM’s ICA Programs, with compliance to be supervised by an independent forensic IT firm. The court awarded IBM its costs of the liability proceedings jointly against the first, second, and sixth defendants, with a payment on account of £20 million due by October

data.title: Tesla seeks to guard crash data from public disclosure
data.author: kklisura
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：特斯拉的自动驾驶系统（FSD）、数据披露、安全问题以及竞争利益之间的冲突

不同观点：
• **数据披露与竞争利益的冲突**：[qwertox] 提到马斯克曾公开表示愿意开放专利以推动电动车技术，但现在特斯拉却以可能造成竞争损害为由，不愿公开可能拯救生命的数据。这引发了对特斯拉是否真正为技术进步着想的质疑。
• **车辆安全性与监管不足**：[isodev] 对特斯拉在碰撞检测方面的表现表示担忧，特别是当涉及安全气囊部署和事故认定时，认为监管不足。
• **自动驾驶系统的实际效果**：[Fischgericht] 分享了个人经历，指出特斯拉的自动驾驶系统在识别行人和物体方面的不足，认为隐藏 crash 数据是不明智的。
• **数据公开的公众权利**：[duxup] 认为，如果国家公路交通安全管理局（NHTSA）拥有数据，那么纳税人也应该有权访问这些数据。
• **事故责任与自动驾驶**：[mosdl] 提到一个涉及特斯拉自动驾驶功能的事故，指出事故责任尚未明确，但初步报告对特斯拉不利。

补充讨论：
• **自动驾驶技术的进步与体验**：[cowlby] 分享了使用特斯拉 FSD 功能的积极体验，特别是硬件和软件升级后的显著改善，认为这是值得每月支付99美元的安全功能。
• **EDR 数据与 ADS/ADAS 的区别**：[dhx] 解释了联合国和美国对车辆事件数据记录（EDR）的法规差异，指出这些数据主要记录车辆的物理行为，而非自动驾驶系统（ADS/ADAS）的操作细节。
• **媒体报道与利益冲突**：[jfoster] 提到《华盛顿邮报》对特斯拉的报道，指出该报的拥有者也拥有自动驾驶公司 Zoox，可能存在利益冲突。
• **对特斯拉自动驾驶的怀疑与支持**：[1vuio0pswjnm7] 提供了多个 NTSB 事故调查链接，质疑特斯拉的安全性。[nemothekid] 则认为很多事故是由于用户鲁莽驾驶，而非 FSD 系统本身的缺陷。[redm] 则强烈支持 FSD 技术，认为其技术进步令人惊叹。
• **公众数据与公共安全**：[7e] 主张公共道路上的数据应为公共数据，认为应该知道周围特斯拉车辆带来的风险。

争议焦点：特斯拉是否应公开涉及自动驾驶系统的 crash 数据，以保障公众安全，还是以保护商业利益为由拒绝披露。各方对特斯拉自动驾驶技术的安全性和可靠性存在明显分歧。

data.title: How Much Energy Does It Take To Think?
data.author: nsoonhui
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了大脑在思考时的能量消耗。研究显示，尽管我们在进行专注的认知任务时感觉耗费大量精力，但实际上这些任务只比休息时多消耗约5%的能量。大脑的大部分能量用于维持生理系统的平衡，而非纯粹的认知功能。进化塑造了大脑的这种能量分配模式，以保存资源。大脑仅占身体重量的2%，却消耗约20%的能量，婴儿更是高达50%。ATP（三磷酸腺苷）是大脑能量的主要来源，通过葡萄糖和氧气生成，维持神经元间的通讯和膜电位。虽然直接测量人脑ATP消耗非常侵入性，但通过PET扫描和功能磁共振成像等方法可以间接估算能量使用。文章指出，大脑不仅是思考工具，更是复杂的生物系统，受进化限制和资源管理需求的制约。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大脑疲劳、能量消耗及其潜在解决方案

不同观点：
• [mellow_observer] 认为大脑在低能量环境下进化优化，但在高能量可得的时代，如何克服精神疲劳是一个重要问题。如果能克服疲劳，生活质量将大幅提高。同时提到疲劳可能有其他原因，但这一话题未得到足够关注。

• [user_7832] 强调了各种因素（如压力、睡眠不足、药物等）对神经化学的影响，并指出这些因素如何改变我们的认知和行为。该评论者认为，没有亲身经历的人难以理解这些影响，呼吁更多的理解和支持。

• [xyzzy123] 观察到孩子在集中思考时会呼吸加重，并对此现象表示好奇，但未提出具体解释。

• [jonplackett] 提出在高压力下大脑加速 firing 是否可以解释时间感知变慢的现象，暗示大脑在高压下可能以更高的频率运作。

• [gleenn] 分享了个人经历，指出高强度思考（如编写软件）会增加卡路里消耗，且糖分可以快速补充能量。

• [rkagerer] 认为大脑的大部分功能用于维持，类似于大型软件项目或设备维护，暗示大脑的能量使用效率问题。

• [debuggerson] 提出过度思考的人的能量消耗是否不同于专注工作的人，质疑不同思维模式下的能量使用是否不同。

• [fside] 认为大脑作为能量吝啬鬼，可能提示我们设计高效算法和AI的策略应注重能量分配和预测效率，而非单纯增加处理能力。

• [voidUpdate] 希望得到大脑能量消耗的实际瓦特数，但未获得具体数据。

• [Perz1val] 开玩笑地问是否存在药物可以把大脑从4Hz超频到100Hz或更高，并计算了可能的卡路里需求。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于是否可以通过某种方式克服精神疲劳以及其潜在的伦理和生理影响。
• 不同评论者对大脑能量消耗的原因和优化策略提供了多样化的见解，包括神经化学、物理现象（如呼吸加重）和计算效率等角度。
• 讨论中还涉及了实际生活中的观察（如孩子思考时的呼吸变化）和假设性问题（如超频大脑的药物）。

How Much Energy Does It Take To Think?
By
Conor Feehly
June 4, 2025
Studies of neural metabolism reveal our brain’s effort to keep us alive and the evolutionary constraints that sculpted our most complex organ.

You’ve just gotten home from an exhausting day. All you want to do is put your feet up and zone out to whatever is on television. Though the inactivity may feel like a well-earned rest, your brain is not just chilling. In fact, it is using nearly as much energy as it did during your stressful activity, according to recent research.
Sharna Jamadar
, a neuroscientist at Monash University in Australia, and her colleagues reviewed research from her lab and others around the world to estimate the
metabolic cost of cognition
— that is, how much energy it takes to power the human brain. Surprisingly, they concluded that effortful, goal-directed tasks use only 5% more energy than restful brain activity. In other words, we use our brain just a small fraction more when engaging in focused cognition than when the engine is idling.
It often feels as though we allocate our mental energy through strenuous attention and focus. But the new research builds on a growing understanding that the majority of the brain’s function goes to maintenance. While many neuroscientists have historically focused on active, outward cognition, such as attention, problem-solving, working memory and decision-making, it’s becoming clear that beneath the surface, our background processing is a hidden hive of activity. Our brains regulate our bodies’ key physiological systems, allocating resources where they’re needed as we consciously and subconsciously react to the demands of our ever-changing environments.
“There is this sentiment that the brain is for thinking,” said
Jordan Theriault
, a neuroscientist at Northeastern University who was not involved in the new analysis. “Where, metabolically, [the brain’s function is] mostly spent on managing your body, regulating and coordinating between organs, managing this expensive system which it’s attached to, and navigating a complicated external environment.”

The neuroscientist Sharna Jamadar compiled data from simultaneous MRI and PET imaging to estimate the brain’s energy use.
Emma Liang
The brain is not purely a cognition machine, but an object sculpted by evolution — and therefore constrained by the tight energy budget of a biological system. Thinking may make you feel tired, then, not because you are out of energy, but because you have evolved to preserve resources. This study of neural metabolism, when tied to research on the dynamics of the brain’s electrical firing, points to the competing evolutionary forces that explain the limitations, scope and efficiencies of our cognitive capabilities.
The Cost of a Predictive Engine
The human brain is incredibly expensive to run. At roughly 2% of body weight, the organ gorges on 20% of our body’s energetic resources. “It’s hugely metabolically demanding,” Jamadar said. For infants, that number is closer to 50%.
The brain is not purely a cognition machine, but an object sculpted by evolution.
The brain’s energy comes in the form of the molecule adenosine triphosphate (ATP), which cells make from glucose and oxygen. A tremendous expanse of thin capillaries — an estimated 400 miles of vascular wiring — weaves through brain tissue to carry glucose- and oxygen-rich blood to neurons and other brain cells. Once synthesized within cells, ATP powers communication between neurons, which enact the brain’s functions. Neurons carry electrical signals to their synapses, which allow the cells to exchange molecular messages; the strength of a signal determines whether they will release molecules (or “fire”). If they do, that molecular signal determines whether the next neuron will pass on the message, and so on. Maintaining what are known as membrane potentials — stable voltages across a neuron’s membrane that ensure that the cell is primed to fire when called upon — is known to account for at least half of the brain’s total energy budget.

data.title: A maths proof that is only true in Japan
data.author: monksdream
data.article_summary: 2012年，日本数学家望月新一（Shinichi Mochizuki）宣称通过其创立的“宇宙际Teichmüller理论”（IUT理论）解决了数论中重要的abc猜想。然而，他的500页论文因其复杂和独特的方法被称为“仅在日本成立的证明”，全球数学界难以理解。尽管abc猜想内容相对简单，即对于整数a、b、c，其不同质因数的乘积通常大于c，但证明该猜想意义重大，甚至能简化费马大定理的证明。然而，望月的证明因其晦涩和缺乏发表，引发了数学界的分歧。2018年，数学家Peter Scholze和Jakob Stix指出了证明中的致命错误，但望月及其支持者仍坚持其正确性，导致该问题悬而未决。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于Mochizuki及其IUT理论（特别是abc猜想证明）的争议，以及数学真理的普遍性与地域性问题

不同观点：
• [kitd] 提到Mochizuki及其同事因IUT研究获得10万美元的奖项，暗示此奖项可能存在问题，暗指其研究未得到广泛认可。
• [stavros] 认为标题具有误导性，指出如果只有少数日本人相信IUT理论，不能称之为“仅在日本成立”，因为数学真理应该是普遍的，而非地域性的。
• [practal] 提到曾提议将Mochizuki的证明形式化，但被礼貌拒绝，并认为当时的提议可能不可行。
• [Xss3] 质疑如果只有部分日本数学家支持IUT理论，能否说该理论在日本成立。
• [moomin] 怀疑Mochizuki及其支持者形成了“学术崇拜”，而非真正的数学证明，并通过历史上Galois的例子说明新数学思想被接受的困难。
• [Theofrastus] 提到人工智能在数学形式化中的应用，并质疑AI生成结果的验证问题，认为AI在当前状态下未必适用于此领域。
• [fside] 以讽刺口吻评论Mochizuki的证明为“地域性真理”，并调侃将来的数学定理可能根据时区决定其成立与否。
• [thaumasiotes] 指出如果某个证明的关键部分仍被称为“猜想”，那该证明就不成立，因为猜想应在证明后成为定理。

补充讨论：
• [petesergeant] 以“韩国独有的死亡方式”（Fan death）为例，暗示某些理论或观念可能仅在特定文化或地域内被接受。
• [madaxe_again] 认为这个争议像是“老教授/期刊编辑在其权力的晚期玩弄权术”，而非真正的学术突破。
• [IshKebab] 直白地批评Mochizuki的态度，认为其行为不当。
• [zkmon] 讨论数学概念的接受过程，指出许多数学和逻辑概念在历史上都经历了接受过程，并受到物理学等领域进展的影响。

争议的焦点：
1. Mochizuki的IUT理论及其证明是否有效。
2. 数学真理是否具有普遍性，或可能仅在特定区域或群体中成立。
3. AI在数学证明形式化中的适用性及其验证问题。

这些观点反映了学术界对新数学理论接受的复杂性，以及在科学验证和地域文化影响下的真理相对性问题。

44198583.article_content:
A baffling proof of the ABC conjecture set off a bitter divide among mathematicians
AndreasG/Shutterstock
As a science journalist, there are some stories that you return to again and again. There is climate change, of course – the biggest story of our time. Then there are the big questions, such as “what is consciousness?” or “are we alone in the universe?”, and so on. But one of the stories I simply cannot let go of is a mathematical argument that has been raging for over a decade. I call it “the proof that is only true in Japan”.
Let me start at the beginning. In 2012, mathematician
Shinichi Mochizuki
at Kyoto University, Japan, published an extraordinary set of papers, across 500 pages, detailing what he called inter-universal Teichmüller (IUT) theory. This was a framework for stretching and deforming our ordinary concepts of mathematical objects, like numbers and their relationships through multiplication and addition, transferring them to new mathematical “universes” where they can be poked and prodded to yield new insights. “He is literally taking apart conventional objects in terrible ways and reconstructing them in new universes,”
one mathematician told me at the time
.
That’s pretty cool-sounding, but what made this a particularly big deal was that Mochizuki was claiming to have used IUT to solve the abc conjecture, a deep problem in number theory that is now 40 years old. Unlike IUT, the statement of the conjecture is relatively easy to understand, as it simply starts with the equation a + b = c, where each letter stands for a whole number, or integer.
Read more
Mathematicians have discovered a mind-blowing new kind of infinity
You also need to know that every integer can be divided into its prime factors, the prime numbers that serve as the building blocks for all numbers. For example, the prime factors of 21 are 3 and 7, while for 12 they are 2, 2 and 3. For 12, 2 appears twice in the list of prime factors, so we can also talk about distinct prime factors, meaning we only list each number once.
What the abc conjecture proposes is that if you multiply the distinct prime factors of a, b and c together, the result is usually larger than c. For example, if we have 12 + 21 = 33. Our distinct prime factors are 2, 3, 7 and 11 (remember, we remove any that repeat), and their product is 462, which is larger than 33. Another way to think about this is that the interplay of addition and multiplication places restrictions on how numbers can be composed.
Receive a weekly dose of discovery in your inbox.
Sign up to newsletter
Besides telling us something deep about the nature of numbers, proving the abc conjecture would, in turn, unlock a whole host of other mathematical results that rely on it – not least a fairly simple proof of the infamously tricky
Fermat’s Last Theorem
– so Mochizuki’s claim seemed to be a big deal. There was just one problem: no one could understand it. At the time of publication in 2012, mathematicians compared Mochizuki’s work to a paper from “
outer space
”, so alien was his approach.
It isn’t unusual for mathematicians to take a while to process and fully understand a big proof, but what happened next is perhaps unlike anything else in the history of mathematics. A few years after Mochizuki’s initial post on his website, his epic proof had yet to be accepted for formal publication in a journal. At the end of 2014,
he posted an update
, criticising other mathematicians for not fully engaging with his work, pointing out that researchers who had taken the time to study under him at Kyoto University for many months were able to understand it.
This impasse continued for many years, with
conferences devoted to understanding IUT
and even
the publication of a 300-page “summary” of the work
. By 2017, it was said that maybe a dozen people actually understood Mochizuki’s work – all of them having submitted to his intense tutelage. But Mochizuki’s refusal to leave Japan to attend international conferences or engage with the wider world – he has never responded to a request for interview by
New Scientist
, for example – meant that most mathematicians simply didn’t want to devote the time to learning a theory that might not pay off.
Read more
5 mind-bending numbers that could reveal the secrets of the universe
But then, two German mathematicians seemed to bring a resolution to this saga. Enter
Peter Scholze
at the University of Bonn and
Jakob Stix
at Goethe University Frankfurt, two heavyweights in the field. They spent a week working with Mochizuki in Tokyo in March 2018, and in September announced they had found a
fatal flaw in his proof
.
The error concerned a part of the proof called Conjecture 3.12, seen as a vital part of Mochizuki’s efforts to solve the abc conjecture, which Scholze and Stix claimed suffered from an unjustified leap of logic. “We came to the conclusion that there is no proof,” wrote the pair, who didn’t respond to a request to comment for this article.

data.title: Second ispace craft has probably crash-landed on Moon
data.author: politelemon
data.article_summary: 日本私营公司ispace的HAKUTO-R Mission 2（M2） lunar lander在试图降落月球时失去联系，可能已坠毁。M2在距离月球表面192米时速度过快，且未能及时获取与月表的距离数据以减速至安全着陆速度。尽管进行了系统调整和软件更新，着陆仍未成功。若成功，M2本将为月球表面设备供电，包括水电解设备和食物生产实验模块等。ispace的Mission 1（M1）此前也在2023年4月坠毁。月球着陆极为复杂，ispace表示将分析问题以改进未来任务。
data.comments_summary:

You have full access to this article via your institution.
A Japanese spacecraft has probably crashed on the Moon, the second failed landing attempt for Tokyo-based private firm ispace.
The HAKUTO-R Mission 2 (M2) lander — also called Resilience — began its landing sequence from a 100-kilometre-altitude orbit at 3.13am local time on 5 June. The craft was due to land near the centre of Mare Frigoris (Sea of Cold) at 4.17am.
The ispace team said at a press conference that it lost contact with M2 when the craft was 192 metres above the Moon’s surface and descending faster than expected. An attempt to reboot M2 was also unsuccessful.
M2 didn't receive measurements of the distance between itself and the lunar surface in time to slow down and reach its correct landing speed, the team said.
“It eventually slowed down, but not softly enough,” says Clive Neal, who studies the Moon at the University of Notre Dame in Indianapolis, US. He speculates that the failure was probably caused by a systems issue that wasn’t identified and addressed during the M1 landing attempt. “It’s something that I believe will definitely be fixable, because getting that close means there’s a few tweaks that are going to be needed for the next one,” he adds.
If M2 had successfully landed on the lunar surface, the mission would have been the
second time
a commercial company had achieved the feat and a first for a non-US company. ispace's Mission 1 (M1) probably crashed during a landing attempt in April 2023.
Second chance
Lunar landings are challenging. When M1 crashed, Ryo Ujiie, ispace’s chief technology officer said the telemetry — which collects data on the craft’s altitude and speed — estimated that M1 was on the surface when it wasn’t, causing the lander to free fall.
Speaking to
Nature
last week, Ujiie said the company had addressed the telemetry issue with M2 and modified its software. “We also carefully selected how to approach the landing site,” he added.
Had M2 landed successfully, the craft would have supplied electricity for its cargo, including water electrolyzing equipment and a module for food production experiments — developed by Japan-based Takasago Thermal Engineering and biotechnology firm Euglena. A deep space radiation probe made by Taiwan’s National Central University, and the 54-centimetre Tenacious rover were also be on board. The rover, created by ispace’s European subsidiary in Luxemburg, was going to be released from the lander to collect imagery, location data and lunar sand known as regolith. Tenacious also carries a small red house made by Swedish artist Mikael Genberg.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于圣经文本的来源和组成的不同观点，特别是新算法结果的解读以及早期基督教文本的多样性。

不同观点：
• JPLeRouzic认为新算法的结果只是验证了学术界对圣经的共识，即圣经是由不同的文献和传统汇编、编辑而成，并没有什么特别复杂的新发现。
• n4r9进一步扩展，指出词频比较主要支持学术界对旧约作者身份的共识，并偶尔支持少数意见。接着详细介绍了新约形成过程中的复杂性，尤其是非正典福音和诺斯替文本的多样性及其被压制和发现的历史。n4r9还推测了诺斯替文本对伊斯兰教的影响。
• renlo则批评评论更像是在为一个起源神话的合法性背书，而不是真正讨论作者身份问题，暗示对讨论的客观性或目的性存疑。

补充讨论：
• n4r9详细描述了早期基督教文本的多样性，包括《约翰福音》与《对观福音》的差异，以及诺斯替文本的内容和历史背景。特别提到在1945年发现的大量诺斯替文本（纳格·哈玛迪文库）对理解早期基督教的重要性。
• 讨论中还涉及到早期教会如何通过伊里奈乌斯（Irenaeus）的《反异端》文本在公元180年左右将《约翰福音》正典化，并压制诺斯替基督教社群及其文本，可能是为了统一宗教教义和巩固教会权威。
• 争议的焦点之一在于新算法结果的实际意义，以及这种结果是否只是验证了已有的学术共识，还是提供了新的视角或发现。
• renlo的评论暗示了对该讨论的怀疑，认为其可能是在为某种特定的起源神话提供合法性，而不是客观地讨论作者身份问题。

总体而言，讨论围绕圣经文本的组成和早期基督教文本多样性的复杂性展开，涉及正典与非正典文本的历史和影响。

data.title: Google confirms more ads on your paid YouTube Premium Lite soon
data.article_summary: YouTube正在使其应用上的广告更难被屏蔽。今年3月，用户在Chrome、Opera和Firefox等浏览器上发现了相关问题。同月，Google推出了新的付费订阅级别“YouTube Premium Lite”，但该级别并非完全无广告，且不包括视频下载、后台播放和YouTube Music等功能。更糟糕的是，Google计划从2025年6月30日开始，在短视频（Shorts）中添加广告，这一变化将全球同步实施。目前，用户可以选择每年28美元的无广告订阅以支持平台。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：YouTube Premium Lite订阅服务的价值和目标用户，以及广告对用户体验的影响。

不同观点：
• [planb] 认为YouTube Premium Lite去除了许多实用功能（如视频下载和后台播放），仅提供了无广告体验，价格却不合理。他质疑该订阅计划的目标用户是谁。
• [saubeidl] 将广告视为心理战，使用Adblock是数字自卫，建议使用ublock origin和sponsor block等工具来屏蔽广告，特别是在桌面和Android设备上。
• [krige] 对“Premium Lite”这个名称进行讽刺，认为这是大企业复杂政策的一个体现，反映了当前科技公司的政策混乱。
• [recursivecaveat] 认为Premium Lite可能无法长久存在，因为其复杂性和不明确的价值主张可能导致用户失去兴趣。他还将此问题与微软Office等其他产品的复杂订阅模式进行类比。
• [_Algernon_] 直接提供ublock origin插件链接，暗示使用此类工具可以解决广告问题。
• [Argonaut998] 表示不会为YouTube Premium付费，因为YouTube不仅展示广告，还收集用户数据。他认为两者不能兼得。
• [Reubensson] 提到YouTube曾经有过更好的Lite版本，但被移除，现在的版本在类似价格下显得更差。
• [globular-toast] 认为YouTube和其他版权行业一样，追求更多利润是贪婪的表现，这是可预见的。要改变这种状况，可能需要AGPL软件和去中心化互联网等更根本的解决方案。
• [charcircuit] 解释了Shorts和音乐视频在版权使用上的不同，认为两者被同样对待是有道理的。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于YouTube Premium Lite提供的功能和价格是否匹配，特别是去除了下载和后台播放等实用功能后，用户认为其性价比低。
• 广告对用户体验的影响也是讨论重点，许多用户建议使用Adblock和第三方工具来避免广告。
• 对大企业政策和数据隐私的批评反映了用户对科技公司普遍的不信任。
• 对YouTube未来发展的悲观预期和呼吁根本性变革的声音也在评论中有所体现。

44198176.article_content:
It is no secret that YouTube has been trying to make it harder and harder for users to block ads on its app. Back in March, earlier this year, we reported on problems users, including us, noticed across various browsers
including the likes of Chrome, Opera, and Firefox
.
Later in the same month, Google released its new paid subscription tier called "
YouTube Premium Lite.
" However, this is not a completely ad-free service as users are still served adverts during their YouTube sessions, although the number of ads is far lower than what a user would see on the free app. The idea is quite similar to
Netflix's Basic with Ads plan, which
was released back in 2022.
Besides a non-ad-free experience, the $7.99 Premium Lite subscription also removed several other cool features like the ability to download videos for offline viewing and background play, which can be quite convenient for listening to music on the app. Speaking of music, YouTube Premium Lite also does not include access to YouTube Music.
Unfortunately, Google is tweaking this plan for the worse, as it will soon add adverts to short videos. The company has seemingly started sending emails to customers who are using the Premium Lite tier, informing them about the change that begins later this month, on 30 June.
Here is what the mail says:
Thank you for being a Premium Lite member. Premium Lite offers fewer interruptions so you can watch more of the YouTube you love.
We are writing to let you know that beginning 30 June 2025, ads may appear on Shorts, in addition to music content and when you search or browse. Most videos will continue to remain ad-free.
The above was shared by user
big_D
on the TWiT.community forum. German outlet
Deskmodder
also reported on this, which suggests that the rollout might be happening globally on the same June 30, 2025 date.
As an online publication, Neowin too relies on ads for operating costs and, if you use an ad blocker, we'd appreciate being whitelisted.
In addition, we have an
ad-free subscription for $28 a year
, which is another way to show support!

data.title: Cory Doctorow on how we lost the internet
data.author: signa11
data.article_summary: Cory Doctorow在PyCon US 2025上发表主题演讲，讨论了当前互联网的衰退现象，称之为"enshittification"（腐化）。他描述了这个过程分为三个阶段：首先，平台通过提升用户体验来吸引用户，同时通过各种手段建立主导地位；接着，在锁定用户后，平台开始牺牲用户体验来满足商业客户的需求，例如增加广告；最后，平台提供的价值逐渐减少，仅维持最低限度以留住用户和商业客户。Doctorow以Google为例，说明其通过操纵搜索结果和广告市场来实现这一过程，最终导致用户体验下降。他还提到类似现象出现在护理行业，通过"Uber for nursing"应用压低工资，显示出平台腐化对劳动市场的负面影响。Doctorow的演讲警示了当前互联网平台的衰退趋势及其广泛的社会影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对文章风格及内容价值的评价

不同观点：
• [支持观点] 读者riffraff认为文章延续了Cory Doctorow的风格，内容详实，具有深度。具体而言，文章篇幅较长，信息密度高，并提出了许多有价值的观点。例如，文章指出社会不必永远受制于过去无能立法者所制定的灾难性政策错误。这一观点受到riffraff的认可，认为具有启发性。

• [潜在批评] 尽管riffraff总体上对文章持积极态度，但其提到文章“长”且“密集”，暗示可能对部分读者来说，文章的信息量和长度可能会造成阅读负担。虽然riffraff本人未明确批评，但这暗示了文章可能存在不易消化的问题。

补充讨论：

By
Jake Edge
May 27, 2025
PyCon US
Cory Doctorow
wears many hats
:
digital activist, science-fiction author, journalist, and more.  He has
also written many books, both fiction and non-fiction, runs the
Pluralistic blog
, is a visiting
professor, and is an advisor to the
Electronic
Frontier Foundation
(EFF); his
Chokepoint Capitalism
co-author, Rebecca Giblin, gave a
2023 keynote
in Australia
that we covered.  Doctorow gave a rousing keynote on
the state of the "enshitternet"—today's internet—to kick
off the recently held
PyCon US
2025
in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania.
He began by noting that he is known for coining the term
"
enshittification
" about the decay of tech platforms, so attendees were
probably expecting to hear about that; instead, he wanted to start by
talking about nursing.  A
recent
study
described how nurses are increasingly getting work through one of
three main apps that "
bill themselves out as 'Uber for nursing'
".
The nurses never know what they will be paid per hour prior to accepting a
shift and the three companies act as a cartel in order to "
play all
kinds of games with the way that labor is priced
".
In particular, the
companies purchase financial information from a data broker before offering
a nurse a shift; if the nurse is carrying a lot of credit-card debt,
especially if some of that is delinquent, the amount offered is
reduced. "
Because, the more desperate you are, the less you'll accept to
come into work and do that grunt work of caring for the sick, the elderly,
and the dying.
"  That is horrific on many levels, he said, but "
it
is emblematic of 'enshittification'
", which is one of the reasons he
highlighted it.
Platform decay
Enshittification is a three-stage process; he used Google to
illustrate the idea.  At first, Google minimized ads and maximized spending
on engineering to produce a great search engine; while it was doing that,
however, it was buying its way to dominance. "
They bribed every service,
every product
that had a search box to make sure that that was a Google search box.
"
No matter which browser, phone carrier, or operating system you were using,
Google ensured that you were using its search by default; by the early
2020s, it was spending the equivalent of buying a Twitter every 18 months
to do so, he said.  That is the first stage of the process: when the
provider is being good to its users, but is finding ways to lock them in.
The second phase occurs once the company recognizes that it has users
locked in, so it will be difficult for them to switch away, and it shifts
to making things worse for its users in order to enrich its business
customers.  For Google, those are the publishers and advertisers.  A
growing portion of the search results page is shifted over to ads
"
marked off with ever-subtler, ever-smaller, ever-grayer labels
distinguishing them from the organic search results
".  While the
platform is getting better for business customers—at the expense of the
users—those customers are also getting locked in.
Phase three of enshittification is when the value of the platform is
clawed back until all that is left is kind of a "
homeopathic residue—the
least value needed to keep both business customers and end users locked to
the platform
".  We have gained a view into this process from the three
monopoly cases that Google has lost over the last 18 months. In 2019, the
company had 90% of the world's search traffic and its users were loyal;
"
everyone who searched on Google, searched everything on Google
".
But that meant that Google's search growth had plateaued, so how was the
company going to be able to grow?  It could "
raise a billion humans to
adulthood and make them Google customers, which is
Google Classroom
, but that's a
slow process
".  From the internal memos that came to light from the
court cases, we can see what the company chose to do, he said: "
they
made search worse
".
The accuracy of the search results was reduced, which meant that users
needed to do two or three queries to the get the results they would have
seen on the first page.  That increased the number of ads that could be
shown, which is obviously bad for searchers, but the company was also
attacking its business customers at the same time.  For example, "
Google entered into
an illegal, collusive arrangement with Meta, called
Jedi Blue
" that
"
gamed the advertising market
" so that publishers got paid less and
advertisers had to pay more, he s
44197806.article_summary: Cory Doctorow在PyCon US 2025上发表主题演讲，讨论了当前互联网的衰退现象，称之为"enshittification"（腐化）。他描述了这个过程分为三个阶段：首先，平台通过提升用户体验来吸引用户，同时通过各种手段建立主导地位；接着，在锁定用户后，平台开始牺牲用户体验来满足商业客户的需求，例如增加广告；最后，平台提供的价值逐渐减少，仅维持最低限度以留住用户和商业客户。Doctorow以Google为例，说明其通过操纵搜索结果和广告市场来实现这一过程，最终导致用户体验下降。他还提到类似现象出现在护理行业，通过"Uber for nursing"应用压低工资，显示出平台腐化对劳动市场的负面影响。Doctorow的演讲警示了当前互联网平台的衰退趋势及其广泛的社会影响。

data.article_summary: Merlin是一个鸟类识别应用，提供三种主要功能。Sound ID可实时识别周围鸟鸣，支持离线使用，适用于美国、加拿大、欧洲等地，并将扩展到更多地区。Photo ID可以通过照片识别鸟类，同样支持离线使用。Bird ID Wizard通过回答三个简单问题提供可能的鸟类匹配。应用还允许用户将识别的鸟类保存到生活清单，并根据位置创建自定义鸟类列表。Merlin由eBird社区贡献的数据和专家建议支持，是鸟类爱好者的强大工具。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对Merlin鸟类识别应用的评价与建议

不同观点：
• [积极评价] 用户rigrassm和japhyr对Merlin应用表示高度赞赏，认为它极大地改变了他们的早晨routine，并帮助他们识别鸟类，尤其是通过声音识别功能。japhyr进一步赞扬了应用的公益性质，没有使用不良的营销手段。
• [技术细节与研究背景] 用户gcr作为研究人员的朋友，对Sound ID部分的技术实现给予高度评价，指出其基于领域专家研究的机器学习模型非常可靠。eichin补充说明了应用通过 spectrogram 实现音频识别的技术原理。
• [功能建议与问题反馈] 用户togume指出应用在无网络环境下表现良好，但用户界面存在多个问题，如按钮失效和结果丢失。他们建议添加iNaturalist桥接功能和快速反馈按钮。barefootcoder提醒用户注意播放鸟叫声可能对实际鸟类行为的干扰。codingdave抱怨无法通过PC上传图片，UX设计对DSLR用户不友好。
• [地区与物种限制] 用户Maultasche提到在新西兰使用Merlin时，识别效果不如在美国，尤其是对本地独有鸟种的识别能力不足，甚至错误识别了火鸡。OptionOfT分享了一次有趣的误识别经历。

补充讨论：
• [物种识别准确性] 用户AnotherGoodName对应用的识别准确性总体信任，但对其在相似物种识别上的可靠性持怀疑态度。
• [应用使用体验] 用户JR1427鼓励未尝试过鸟类观察的人使用Merlin，认为它像现实版的Pokemon。

争议焦点：

data.title: VectorSmuggle: Covertly Exfiltrate Data in Embeddings
data.author: smugglereal
data.article_summary: VectorSmuggle是一个展示基于向量隐匿数据泄露技术的概念验证平台。它利用向量表示隐藏敏感文档，通过伪装成合法的RAG（检索增强生成）操作逃避安全监控。该项目支持15种以上的文档格式，采用隐写术和规避技术，具备行为伪装和检测逃避能力，并提供增强的查询引擎和分析工具。其核心模块包括多格式加载器、内容预处理器、隐写引擎、规避层、向量存储和分析恢复工具。该平台可容器化部署，并支持Kubernetes，适用于AI/ML环境中的安全分析和防御研究。用户可通过提供的脚本和演示快速上手，进行数据嵌入、查询重建和风险评估。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过隐蔽方法（如DNS查询和AI/ML系统中的RAG）进行数据窃取的可行性及其实际应用。

不同观点：
• [anonymousiam] 认为十多年前就有通过DNS查询绕过防火墙的隐蔽数据窃取方法。具体方法是将base64编码的 payload 作为主机名前缀附加到恶意域名上，并通过时间戳保证唯一性，绕过本地缓存DNS服务器。

• [acmiyaguchi] 对隐蔽数据窃取技术表示一定兴趣，但认为所描述的方法（文档和代码）不够清晰，威胁模型和案例研究显得人为设计，不太现实。他认为项目缺乏技术总结和实际演示，难以让人信服。

• [stephantul] 仅简短提到“具体的攻击向量”，未展开具体讨论，但暗示了对攻击技术的关注。

• [smugglereal] 支持该项目，认为这是一个全面的概念验证，展示了在AI/ML环境中基于向量的数据窃取技术。该项目旨在教育和防御分析，强调了RAG系统中的潜在风险，并提供了相关工具。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于该隐蔽数据窃取方法的实际可行性和应用场景。acmiyaguchi认为项目缺乏实际案例和技术细节，而smugglereal则强调该项目的教育和防御价值。

• anonymousiam提供了具体技术细节和历史背景，支持隐蔽数据窃取的可行性，但未涉及RAG系统。

• 不同观点之间反映了对于安全研究项目在实际应用和理论教育之间价值的不同看法。

VectorSmuggle
"The smuggle is real!"
A comprehensive proof-of-concept demonstrating vector-based data exfiltration techniques in AI/ML environments. This project illustrates potential risks in RAG systems and provides tools and concepts for defensive analysis.
📋 Overview
VectorSmuggle demonstrates techniques for covert data exfiltration through vector embeddings, showcasing how sensitive information can be hidden within seemingly legitimate RAG operations. This research tool helps security professionals understand and defend against attack vectors in AI/ML systems.
Key Features
🎭 Steganographic Techniques
: Embedding obfuscation and data hiding
📄 Multi-Format Support
: Process 15+ document formats (PDF, Office, email, databases)
🕵️ Evasion Capabilities
: Behavioral camouflage and detection avoidance
🔍 Enhanced Query Engine
: Data reconstruction and analysis
🐳 Production-Ready
: Full containerization and Kubernetes deployment
📊 Analysis Tools
: Comprehensive forensic and risk assessment capabilities

From Steam to Silicon: Patterns of Technological Revolutions
From agriculture to AI, each major economic revolution is driven by a new kind of value conversion: a way of transforming one type of value into another.
These revolutions are not defined by a single invention, but by a sequence of innovations: a core conversion, the infrastructure to scale and distribute various innovations, and the technologies that reduce the cost of distance and delays.
We shall analyse six major revolutions through this lens and show how each laid the groundwork for the next.
Technological revolutions
There are seven key components to each technological revolution:
Core conversion
: a new capability that transforms one form of value into another. Value can be either tangible (e.g. natural resources and goods) or
intangible (e.g. trust, information, and actions).
Scaling infrastructure
: physical systems that make the conversion repeatable and cost-efficient at scale.
Spatiotemporal compression
: tools that shrink the cost of distance or time in the economy by i) increasing connectivity, ii) reducing the latency of interactions, or iii) expanding the scale or speed of economic coordination.
Key resources
: physical or non-physical ingredients that are needed in the core conversion recipe.
Economic mode
: each technological revolution has its own dominant way of creating and capturing value.
Centralization/decentralization arc
: core conversions start centralised to exploit economies of scale, but as complementary technologies lower transaction costs, production disperses.
Administrative innovations
: standards and bureaucratic tools to support the technological revolution at scale and across geographical areas, which may or may not be from the era itself.
Each technological revolution is also a bridge to the next revolution, in that its innovations enable the next one to thrive.

data.title: DiffX – Next-Generation Extensible Diff Format
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了传统Unified Diff格式的局限性，并提出了一种新的可扩展 diff 格式，称为DiffX。Unified Diffs目前仅标准化了一部分内容，如文件标识、差异块偏移和增删行，但缺乏对编码、修订、元数据以及文件路径表示的标准。这使得工具在解析diff文件时面临困难，特别是需要支持多种源代码控制系统时。现代开发需求如表示提交列表、二进制补丁、文本编码以及元数据等，Unified Diffs无法满足。

文章建议在现有Unified Diffs基础上增加可扩展性，提出DiffX格式。DiffX文件向后兼容现有工具，同时具有未来适应性且保持人类可读性。它通过定义结构和标准来解决当前Unified Diffs的问题，如支持元数据和二进制文件等。DiffX旨在让工具能够以标准化方式解析diff文件，并能够修改它们而不必担心破坏内容。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Diff/Patch 格式的设计及其在不同版本控制系统（SCM）中的一致性与实用性

不同观点：
• laserbeam认为当前的层次化格式（带有重复的“meta”命名和多种格式如JSON和键值对）不易读且容易出错，建议使用更直观的命名和单一格式以提高可读性和减少解析错误。
• HelloNurse指出当前讨论中涉及的许多问题实际上是不必要的，例如单个diff表示多个提交、二进制补丁的表示等，认为这些问题属于特定系统的内部结构问题，而非通用diff格式需要解决的。
• blacklion觉得当前的设计混合了自定义的头部和JSON内容，显得笨重且混乱，需要两个解析器，但认为扩展diff格式并标准化元数据是有价值的。
• ed认为现有的补丁格式（如git-format-patch）已经解决了这些问题，没有必要重新设计。
• bawolff质疑这些问题的实际需求，认为当前的diff格式对于大多数用户来说已经足够，且多提交的表示、元数据等问题更像是特定系统内部的需求。
• redleader55直接质疑该格式要解决的实际问题是什么，怀疑是否有实际用户在抱怨当前的patch/diff格式不够好。
• itake提到当前diff工具在处理长行变化（如压缩的JSON）时的困难，认为这是一个未解决的实际使用问题。
• tlb认为最通用的diff表示方式是直接包含两个文件的完整内容，而不是复杂的diff格式，并指出颜色编码的并排比较视图更适合人类阅读。
• koiueo认为JSON作为元数据格式过于复杂，不适合作为通用格式。
• signal11推荐了difftastic工具，认为其使用tree-sitter进行更好的diff信息处理，优于当前讨论的设计。
• greatgib支持扩展diff格式，但认为多行JSON或YAML不适合这种设计，单行命令更易于处理和解析。
• charcircuit不理解为什么单个diff不能表示多个提交会是一个问题，认为每个提交可以有自己的diff。

补充讨论：
• chipx86（DiffX的作者之一）详细解释了设计DiffX的背景和目的，强调该格式旨在解决工具在处理各种SCM的diff文件时遇到的一致性和扩展性问题，而非针对终端用户。他还提到了诸如文本编码、二进制文件处理、元数据注入等实际问题，并指出DiffX的设计目标是提供一种更通用且易于解析的格式。
• karmakaze觉得格式中包含长度信息（如"length=270"）显得冗余且脆弱，并质疑是否真的需要如此复杂的格式，建议在多VCS环境下可以通过转换器解决格式不一致的问题。

争议焦点：
• 是否需要一个新的、复杂的diff格式来解决当前工具在处理多种SCM时的痛点，还是通过简单的转换器或现有工具即可解决这些问题。
• 使用JSON作为元数据格式的合理性，部分人认为JSON过于复杂且不适合此类用途。
• 单个diff是否应该能够表示多个提交，以及这种需求是否真的普遍存在。

44176737.article_content:
DiffX - Next-Generation Extensible Diff Format
¶
If you’re a software developer, you’ve probably worked with diff files. Git
diffs, Subversion diffs, CVS diffs.. Some kind of diff. You probably haven’t
given it a second thought, really. You make some changes, run a command, a
diff comes out. Maybe you hand it to someone, or apply it elsewhere, or put it
up for review.
Diff files show the differences between two text files, in the form of
inserted (
+
) and deleted (
-
) lines. Along with this, they contain some
basic information used to identify the file (usually just the name/relative
path within some part of the tree), maybe a timestamp or revision, and maybe
some other information.
Most people and tools work with
Unified Diffs
. They look like this:
--- readme    2016-01-26 16:29:12.000000000 -0800
+++ readme    2016-01-31 11:54:32.000000000 -0800
@@ -1 +1,3 @@
Hello there
+
+Oh hi!
Or this:
Index: readme
===================================================================
RCS file: /cvsroot/readme,v
retrieving version 1.1
retrieving version 1.2
diff -u -p -r1.1 -r1.2
--- readme    26 Jan 2016 16:29:12 -0000        1.1
+++ readme    31 Jan 2016 11:54:32 -0000        1.2
@@ -1 +1,3 @@
Hello there
+
+Oh hi!
Or this:
diff --git a/readme b/readme
index d6613f5..5b50866 100644
--- a/readme
+++ b/readme
@@ -1 +1,3 @@
Hello there
+
+Oh hi!
Or even this:
Index: readme
===================================================================
--- (revision 123)
+++ (working copy)
Property changes on: .
-------------------------------------------------------------------
Modified: myproperty
## -1 +1 ##
-old value
+new value
Or this!
==== //depot/proj/logo.png#1 ==A== /src/proj/logo.png ====
Binary files /tmp/logo.png and /src/proj/logo.png differ
Here’s the problem
¶
Unified Diffs themselves are not a viable standard for modern development.
They only standardize parts of what we consider to be a diff, namely the
---
/
+++
lines for file identification,
@@
...
@@
lines for
diff hunk offsets/sizes, and
-
/
+
for inserted/deleted lines.
They
don’t
standardize encodings, revisions, metadata, or even how
filenames or paths are represented!
This makes it
very
hard for patch tools, code review tools, code analysis
tools, etc. to reliably parse any given diff and gather useful information,
other than the changed lines, particularly if they want to support multiple
types of source control systems. And there’s a lot of good stuff in diff files
that some tools, like code review tools or patchers, want.
You should see what GNU Patch has to deal with.
Unified Diffs have not kept up with where the world is going. For instance:
A single diff can’t represent a list of commits
There’s no standard way to represent binary patches
Diffs don’t know about text encodings (which is more of a problem than you
might think)
Diffs don’t have any standard format for arbitrary metadata, so everyone
implements it their own way.
We’re long past the point where diffs should be able to do all this. Tools
should be able to parse diffs in a standard way, and should be able to modify
them without worrying about breaking anything. It should be possible to load a
diff, any diff, using a Python module or Java package and pull information out
of it.
Unified Diffs aren’t going away, and they don’t need to. We just need to add
some extensibility to them. And that’s completely doable, today.
Here’s the good news
¶
Unified Diffs, by nature, are
very
forgiving, and they’re everywhere, in
one form or another. As you’ve seen from the examples above, tools shove all
kinds of data into them. Patchers basically skip anything they don’t
recognize. All they really lack is structure and standards.
Git’s diffs are the closest things we have to a standard diff format (in that
both Git and Mercurial support it, and Subversion pretends to, but poorly),
and the closest things we have to a modern diff format (as they optionally
support binary diffs and have a general concept of metadata, though it’s
largely Git-specific).
They’re a good start, though still not formally defined. Still, we can build
upon this, taking some of the best parts from Git diffs and from other
standards, and using the forgiving nature of Unified Diffs to define a new,
structured Unified Diff format.
DiffX files
¶
We propose a new format called Extensible Diffs, or DiffX files for short.
These are
fully backwards-compatible with existing tools
, while also being
future-proof
and remaining
human-readable
.
#diffx:
encoding=utf-8, version=1.0
#.change:
#..preamble:
indent=4, length=319, mimetype=text/markdown
Convert legacy header building code to Python 3.
Header building for messages used old Python 2.6-era list comprehensions
with tuples rather than modern dictionary comprehensions in order to build
a message list. This change modernizes that, and swaps out six for a
3-friendly `.items()` call.

44176737.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了传统Unified Diff格式的局限性，并提出了一种新的可扩展 diff 格式，称为DiffX。Unified Diffs目前仅标准化了一部分内容，如文件标识、差异块偏移和增删行，但缺乏对编码、修订、元数据以及文件路径表示的标准。这使得工具在解析diff文件时面临困难，特别是需要支持多种源代码控制系统时。现代开发需求如表示提交列表、二进制补丁、文本编码以及元数据等，Unified Diffs无法满足。

文章建议在现有Unified Diffs基础上增加可扩展性，提出DiffX格式。DiffX文件向后兼容现有工具，同时具有未来适应性且保持人类可读性。它通过定义结构和标准来解决当前Unified Diffs的问题，如支持元数据和二进制文件等。DiffX旨在让工具能够以标准化方式解析diff文件，并能够修改它们而不必担心破坏内容。
